definition_zh: 平装本；纸皮书
definition_en: a book with a flexible paper cover rather than a stiff hard one, usually cheaper than a hardback
core_image: 薄软纸封的书被一只手按得封面微微弯起，塞进外套口袋
scene: 车站小书店的架子上，一本封面柔软的小说被人顺手塞进了外套口袋。She bought a paperback to read on the train.
sceneCN: 这里 paperback 是「平装本」（第 1 个义项：封面柔软、价格较低的书）；句意：她买了一本平装书，好在火车上读。

derivatives.zh: 平装的；纸皮装订的
平装本（非正式说法，少见）
平装本大小的

senses.title: A soft-covered book
senses.definition: a book bound in a flexible paper cover, sold more cheaply than a hardback
senses.definitionCN: 以柔软纸封面装订、售价低于精装本的书
senses.example: She bought a paperback to read on the train.
senses.exampleCN: 她买了一本平装书，好在火车上读。
senses.why: The word simply puts paper before back, naming the soft cover that replaces the stiff board of a hardback.
senses.whyCN: 这个词就是 paper 加 back，直说柔软的纸封面取代了精装本那块硬纸板。

senses.title: The soft-cover format
senses.definition: the publishing format itself, as opposed to a copy of the book
senses.definitionCN: 指出版形态本身，而非某一本书这个物件
senses.example: The novel first came out in paperback five years later.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说五年后才以平装形式出版。
senses.why: A format is not a thing but a way of making things, so the noun comes to name the cover style that publishers choose.
senses.whyCN: 装帧形态不是一件东西，而是一种制作方式，于是这个词转而指出版社所选用的封面样式。

senses.title: Cheap and light reading
senses.definition: a cheap book that is easy to carry, casual in tone in older use
senses.definitionCN: 便宜、便于携带的书，旧时也用来指格调通俗的读物
senses.example: He packed two paperbacks for the week at the beach.
senses.exampleCN: 他去海滩度假一周，带上了两本平装书。
senses.why: Because the format costs little and travels easily, the word also carries the flavour of light, holiday reading.
senses.whyCN: 这种装帧成本低、便于携带，因此这个词也带上「轻松的假日读物」的味道。

senses.title: The soft-cover adjective
senses.definition: describing a book or a product line that uses a flexible paper cover
senses.definitionCN: 描述使用柔软纸封面的书或出版系列
senses.example: The paperback edition sells far more than the hardback.
senses.exampleCN: 平装版卖得远比精装版好。
senses.why: Placed before a noun, the same pair of words becomes a label for any book of that kind.
senses.whyCN: 放在名词前面时，同一组词就成了这一类书的标签。

senses.title: The paperback era in publishing
senses.definition: the period and market created when cheap paper editions made books widely affordable
senses.definitionCN: 廉价纸皮版使书籍广为大众买得起的那个时期与市场
senses.example: The paperback revolution put good books into millions of hands.
senses.exampleCN: 平装书革命把好书送进了无数人手里。
senses.why: When one cheap format changes who can read, the word grows a historical sense, naming a whole shift in publishing.
senses.whyCN: 当一种便宜的装帧改变了谁能读书，这个词便长出历史义，指整个出版格局的转变。

intro.en: Paperback is a plain English compound, paper plus back, coined to answer the older hardback.
intro.cn: paperback 是朴素的英语复合词，paper 加 back，为对应更早出现的 hardback 而造。

items.en: The English word paper comes from Greek papyros, the papyrus plant used for writing sheets.
items.cn: 英语 paper 来自希腊语 papyros，即用来抄写纸页的纸莎草。

items.en: Latin papyrus carried the plant name, and its reduced form charta meant a sheet of writing material.
items.cn: 拉丁语 papyrus 承袭了这种植物的名称，其缩短形式 charta 表示书写材料的一张。

items.en: Paper, meaning the writing material, is recorded in English from the fourteenth century.
items.cn: paper 表示书写材料，自十四世纪起在英语中有记录。

items.en: In the nineteenth century cheap books were sold in stiff paper boards, sometimes called paper boards, while hardback described a cloth or board binding.
items.cn: 十九世纪的廉价书以硬纸板包封面出售，有时称为 paper boards，而 hardback 指布面或硬纸板装帧。

items.en: The compound paperback appears in the twentieth century alongside the mass-market edition; its first printed date is uncertain and dictionaries differ by a few years.
items.cn: 复合词 paperback 与大众廉价版一同在二十世纪出现；首次见于印刷物的年代不确定，各家词典相差数年。

note.en: Paperback belongs to the family of cover words and is defined against hardback; the look-alike group holds the early spelling, the counter-word and the old trade term.
note.cn: paperback 属于以封面材质为核心的一族词，并以 hardback 为对照；形近组收录早期拼写、反义词与旧的行业用语。

entries.definition: the early hyphenated spelling, the same word
entries.definitionCN: 早期带连字符的写法，与目标词同义

entries.definition: a book bound with a stiff cover
entries.definitionCN: 精装本；硬面书

entries.definition: stiff cardboard used for covers and boxes; nearer in spelling than in meaning
entries.definitionCN: 硬纸板，用于封面和盒子；只是拼写相像，意思并不相同

entries.definition: a book with a flexible cover, the American variant
entries.definitionCN: 平装本；美式说法

entries.definition: a book with a stiff cover
entries.definitionCN: 精装本

entries.definition: a small cheap book, or a purse
entries.definitionCN: 袖珍平装书；钱包

normalIntro.en: Paperback is a compound of two everyday English words, paper and back, made to stand against hardback.
normalIntro.cn: paperback 是两个常见英语词 paper 与 back 的复合，专为与 hardback 对照而造。

normal.en: Back is the back cover, so paperback is a book whose back is paper, not board.
normal.cn: back 指封底，所以 paperback 就是封底用纸、不用硬纸板的书。

normal.en: Hardback has the same shape with hard, so the two words are a neat pair.
normal.cn: hardback 用同一个构形、换个词头 hard，两词正好成对。

normal.en: The usual phrase is in paperback, as in the novel came out in paperback.
normal.cn: 常见搭配是 in paperback，如小说出了平装本。

normal.en: softback and softcover are the American parallels.
normal.cn: 美式对应说法是 softback 与 softcover。

normal.en: Paper itself goes back to Greek papyros, the papyrus reed.
normal.cn: paper 本身可追到希腊语 papyros，即纸莎草。

abstract.en: Press a thumb into the front cover of a thin book and watch the cover bend.
abstract.cn: 用大拇指按一本薄书的封面，看封面弯下去。

abstract.en: Slide a cheap novel into a coat pocket, corner bent, and it fits.
abstract.cn: 把一本廉价小说塞进外套口袋，一角折弯，正好装得下。

abstract.en: Picture a spinning rack in a station shop, rows of thin spines glowing in colours.
abstract.cn: 想象车站小店里一个旋转书架，一排薄书脊闪着彩色。

examples.en: The paperback edition came out a year after the hardback.
examples.cn: 平装版在精装版一年之后出版。

examples.en: I read the whole paperback on the flight home.
examples.cn: 我在回家的航班上读完了整本平装书。

examples.en: Publishers now release paperbacks first and hardbacks later.
examples.cn: 如今出版社先出平装本，后出精装本。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「陪跑本」——随身陪着你跑的书，轻便的平装本；纯属谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 英语 paper（纸，源自希腊语 papyros「纸莎草」经拉丁语 papyrus、charta）+ back（封底）→ paperback，与 hardback 相对，核心义「软纸封面」。

sensesIntro.en: Paperback names a soft-covered book, then the publishing format, then cheap portable reading, then the adjective use, and finally the historical market the format created.
sensesIntro.cn: paperback 先指封面柔软的书，再指这种出版形态，进而指廉价便携的读物、形容词用法，最后指这种装帧所开创的历史性市场。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thumb presses the soft paper cover of a thin book and the corner bends into a coat pocket.
core.cn: 核心意象：拇指按下薄书的软纸封面，封面一角弯进外套口袋。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: one soft-covered book you can hold and carry.
branches.cn: 物件线：一本可以拿在手里的软纸封面书。

branches.en: THE FORMAT: the way publishers make and sell the book.
branches.cn: 形态线：出版方制作与销售这本书的方式。

branches.en: THE TONE: cheap and portable reading, often light or holiday fare.
branches.cn: 格调线：廉价便携的读物，常指轻松的假日阅读。

branches.en: THE LABEL: used before a noun, the word describes any book of the kind.
branches.cn: 标签线：置于名词前，用来描述这一类书。

branches.en: Both the format and the era it created trace back to the same paper back cover.
branches.cn: 第 02 义与第 05 义中的形态与时代，都同出一个纸封面。

intro.en: Paperback is an English compound of two free words; its parts are paper, from Greek, and back, a native English word.
intro.cn: paperback 是两个自由词的英语复合；构词成分是来自希腊语的 paper 与本土词 back。

latinIntro.en: Paper reaches English through Latin papyrus and charta, both recorded, while back is native English; only the Latin forms are listed as cognates.
latinIntro.cn: paper 经拉丁语 papyrus 与 charta 进入英语，二者均有文献；back 则是英语本族词。此处只列拉丁语形式作为同源参照。

items.example: Paper is the material of the cover.
items.exampleCN: paper 正是封面的材料。

items.meaning: the hind part of a book or object
items.example: Back names the cover at the rear of the book.
items.exampleCN: back 指书后部的封面。

items.example: Paperback joins both words into one label.
items.exampleCN: paperback 把两个词合成一个标签。

items.example: Hard- builds the opposite hardback.
items.exampleCN: hard- 构成反义词 hardback。

items.example: Hardback sets the pattern for paperback.
items.exampleCN: hardback 为 paperback 提供了构词格式。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms paperbacked.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 paperbacked。

items.example: The suffix -er forms paperbacker in casual use.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 在口语中构成 paperbacker。

items.example: Paper- builds compounds such as paperboard.
items.exampleCN: paper- 构成 paperboard 等复合词。

items.example: Paperboard is the stiff opposite of a paper back.
items.exampleCN: paperboard 是纸封面相对的硬材质。

a sheet of writing material, paper

definition_zh: 视差；位置偏移；摄影测距差
definition_en: the apparent shift in the position of an object when it is seen from two different places
core_image: 两只看似错开的指针：其实一直是同一根针
scene: 天文学家在相隔半年的两个夜晚观测同一颗恒星，发现它的位置相对背景星空挪动了一点，这点偏移就是视差。Astronomers measure Parallax by viewing the same star from opposite points in the Earth orbit.
sceneCN: 这里 parallax 是「视差」（第 1 个义项：从两个不同位置看同一物体时出现的视觉位移）；句意：天文学家通过从地球公转轨道两端的相对位置观测同一颗恒星，来测量视差。

collocations.zh: 视差误差（读数偏移误差）
视差滚动（网页与游戏效果）

derivatives.zh: 由 parallax 加形容词词尾 -tic 构成，义为「视差的；视差造成的」
在 parallactic 后加 -ly 构成副词，义为「从视差上；以视差方式」

senses.title: Apparent shift seen from two places
senses.definition: the apparent change in the position of an object when it is viewed from two different points
senses.definitionCN: 从两个不同位置观察同一物体时，物体位置看起来发生的变化
senses.example: The finger seems to jump sideways, and that jump is parallax.
senses.exampleCN: 手指似乎横向跳了一下，这一跳就是视差。
senses.why: The Greek root means a change or alteration, and the word names the change of position that the eye alone creates.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语词根意为「变化、改变」，这个词所指的正是只由眼睛位置造成的「位置改变」。

senses.title: A measured distance read by the shift
senses.definition: a technique of finding how far away something is by measuring how much its apparent position shifts
senses.definitionCN: 通过测量物体视位偏移的大小来推算其距离的方法
senses.example: Surveyors may use parallax to judge how far a marker lies.
senses.exampleCN: 测量员可能用视差来判断标杆有多远。
senses.why: Once the shift can be measured, it becomes a number, and that number gives a distance.
senses.whyCN: 一旦位移可以被测量，它就变成一个数值，而这个数值可以换算成距离。

senses.title: Stellar parallax in astronomy
senses.definition: the slight shift in a star position across the sky as the Earth moves around the Sun
senses.definitionCN: 地球绕太阳公转时，恒星在天球上出现的细微位置移动
senses.example: Parallax gave astronomers their first reliable measurement of stellar distance.
senses.exampleCN: 视差让天文学家第一次可靠地测出恒星距离。
senses.why: The Earth orbit gives exactly two widely separated viewpoints, so the everyday head-turning shift becomes a cosmic ruler.
senses.whyCN: 地球公转为观测提供了两个相距极远的位置，于是日常中「换个位置看」的位移变成了宇宙尺子。

senses.title: Photographic framing shift
senses.definition: the difference between what a camera lens sees and what the viewfinder or rangefinder shows
senses.definitionCN: 相机镜头所看到的画面与取景器、测距窗所显示的画面之间的差异
senses.example: A film camera suffers from parallax at short range.
senses.exampleCN: 胶片相机在近距离拍摄时会受视差影响。
senses.why: The viewfinder and the lens sit a few centimetres apart, so the camera suffers the same two-point shift as the eye.
senses.whyCN: 取景窗与镜头相隔几厘米，相机于是承受了与双眼相同的「两点位移」。

senses.title: Reading error from a slanted eye line
senses.definition: an error in reading a scale or gauge that happens when the eye is not directly in line with it
senses.definitionCN: 视线未与刻度或仪表正面垂直时，造成的读数误差
senses.example: Never read a thermometer at an angle, or parallax will distort the value.
senses.exampleCN: 读温度计时千万不要斜着看，否则视差会让读数失真。
senses.why: When the eye is not level with the mark, the pointer seems to sit against a different division, so the same gauge shows two values.
senses.whyCN: 当视线不与刻度齐平时，指针看起来对着另一条刻度线，同一块表就显示出两个读数。

senses.title: Layered movement in images
senses.definition: an effect in which different layers of an image move at different speeds and reveal how far apart they are
senses.definitionCN: 图像中不同层次以不同速度移动，从而显示出彼此远近关系的一种效果
senses.example: Parallax scrolling makes a website feel three-dimensional.
senses.exampleCN: 视差滚动让网站有了立体感。
senses.why: The eye reads speed difference as depth, so designers borrow the old displacement cue to fake distance on a flat screen.
senses.whyCN: 眼睛会把速度差读成远近差别，设计师于是借用这个古老的位移线索，在平面上伪造出纵深。

senses.title: A viewpoint that seems to differ
senses.titleCN: 立场造成的看法偏差（引申）
senses.definition: a figurative use in which two people in different positions seem to see a different version of the same thing
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法：身处不同位置的两个人，似乎看到同一事物的不同版本
senses.example: Each witness described the same accident through a kind of parallax of memory.
senses.exampleCN: 每位目击者都透过一种记忆视差来描述同一场事故。
senses.why: If a physical position changes what you see, then a social or personal position can seem to do the same with ideas.
senses.whyCN: 如果物理位置能改变所看到的景象，那么社会或个人立场似乎也能同样改变对事物的看法。

intro.en: Parallax is built from two Greek elements and appears in English in the sixteenth century as an astronomical term.
intro.cn: parallax 由两个希腊语成分拼合而成，在十六世纪以天文学术语的身份进入英语。

items.en: Para means beside, and allassein means to change, giving parallaxis as a change.
items.cn: para 意为「在旁边」，allassein 意为「改变」，二者合起来形成 parallaxis，意为「变化」。

items.en: Greek writers on optics and astronomy use parallaxis for the change of apparent position.
items.cn: 希腊的光学与天文作者用 parallaxis 表示「视位的变化」。

items.en: Latin learning passes the term on in the forms parallaxis and parallaxos.
items.cn: 拉丁学者以 parallaxis、parallaxos 的形式把这一术语传下去。

items.en: The form parallaxis appears in early modern Latin scientific writing.
items.cn: parallaxis 这一形式出现在近代早期的拉丁科学著作中。

items.en: English takes the word as parallax and applies it first to the moon and the stars.
items.cn: 英语以 parallax 的形式引入，最初用于月亮与恒星。

items.en: The word spreads to photography, metrology, and later to screen design.
items.cn: 这个词随后扩展到摄影、计量，后来又进入屏幕设计。

note.en: Parallax sits in a large para- family and is easily confused with parallel and paradox.
note.cn: parallax 属于庞大的 para- 词族，容易与 parallel、paradox 混淆。

entries.definition: two lines or things that stay the same distance apart
entries.definitionCN: 平行线；并行的；相似的（与 parallax 只是拼写接近，词源不同）

entries.definition: a statement that seems to contradict itself
entries.definitionCN: 悖论；自相矛盾的说法（与 parallax 同有 para- 前缀，词源不同）

entries.definition: to make a person or limb unable to move
entries.definitionCN: 使瘫痪；使动弹不得（与 parallax 共享 para- 前缀，词源不同）

entries.definition: a movement from one position to another
entries.definitionCN: 位移；挪动

entries.definition: a departure from an expected line or standard
entries.definitionCN: 偏差；偏离

entries.definition: the way objects look smaller and spread out with distance
entries.definitionCN: 透视；远近关系

normalIntro.en: Parallax is para (beside) plus a change, so it is the change you see when you stand beside another point.
normalIntro.cn: parallax 是 para（在旁边）加「改变」，也就是站到另一个位置时看到的那种变化。

normal.en: parallax error is what your teacher warns about when reading a thermometer.
normal.cn: 老师提醒看温度计要正对刻度，说的就是 parallax error（读数视差误差）。

normal.en: stellar parallax is the standard way to think of distance in the night sky.
normal.cn: stellar parallax（恒星视差）是理解夜空距离的经典方式。

normal.en: The adjective is parallactic, used for shifts and angles caused by parallax.
normal.cn: 形容词是 parallactic，用于描述由视差造成的位移与角度。

normal.en: Remember para- means beside: parallax depends on looking from beside.
normal.cn: 记住 para- 表示「在旁边」：视差就是「从旁边看」才出现的。

normal.en: Do not confuse the plural with parallel, the word for lines that keep a constant gap.
normal.cn: 别把复数变体与 parallel 搞混，后者指始终保持间距的平行线。

abstract.en: Blink one eye, then the other, and watch a finger jump beside the far wall.
abstract.cn: 先闭上左眼再闭上右眼，看手指在远处墙面旁来回跳。

abstract.en: Picture a long baseline with two cameras at each end, each seeing a star in a different spot.
abstract.cn: 想象一条长长的基线，两端各有一台相机，各自看到恒星处在不同的位置。

abstract.en: Think of the night sky as a road trip: six months of travel redraws the stars.
abstract.cn: 把夜空想成一趟公里旅行：半年的行程会把星星重新画一遍。

examples.en: A parallax error made the reading on the gauge too high.
examples.cn: 读数时的视差误差使仪表的读数偏高。

examples.en: Parallax is one of the oldest tools for measuring the distance to nearby stars.
examples.cn: 视差是测量附近恒星距离的最古老工具之一。

examples.en: The parallax effect in the game makes the deep forest look almost endless.
examples.cn: 游戏里的视差效果让幽深的森林看起来几乎没有尽头。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕人拉叉」——两人从不同方向拉绳子，接口都错开了，就像两只眼看到的错位；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 para（在旁）+ allassein（改变）→ parallaxis（变化）→ 拉丁语 parallaxis → 英语 parallax，核心义「在旁观察时产生的位移」。

sensesIntro.en: Parallax starts from a plain visible shift, turns into a measuring tool, spreads to stars and cameras, and ends as a metaphor for differing viewpoints.
sensesIntro.cn: parallax 从最朴素的「看到的位移」出发，进而成为测距工具，扩展到恒星与相机，最后引申为「立场造成的看法偏差」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one finger, two eyes, two different places for the finger.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根手指，两只眼睛，手指看起来有两个位置。

branches.en: The plain visible shift is the basic sense.
branches.cn: 最朴素的可见位移是基础义项。

branches.en: Measuring the shift turns it into a distance, on Earth and in the sky.
branches.cn: 测量位移就把视差变成距离，地面上与星空中都是如此。

branches.en: Cameras and gauges suffer the same shift as small errors.
branches.cn: 相机与仪表承受同样的位移，表现为小误差。

branches.en: Layered screens borrow the shift to fake depth.
branches.cn: 分层屏幕借用这种位移来伪造纵深。

branches.en: The metaphor extends the physical shift to viewpoints on ideas.
branches.cn: 隐喻把物理位移延伸到对观念的不同看法上。

intro.en: Parallax joins the Greek prefix para- with the verb allassein, and English builds parallactic around it.
intro.cn: parallax 由希腊语前缀 para- 与动词 allassein 拼合，英语围绕它构成 parallactic。

definition_zh: 使瘫痪；使麻痹；使失去活动能力；使陷入停滞
definition_en: to make a person, limb, or system unable to move or work properly
core_image: 绷紧的身体突然松塌：四肢还在，却动不了
scene: 一场意外伤到脊柱后，他的双腿再也无法动弹。A spinal injury left him paralysed from the waist down.
sceneCN: 这里 paralyse 是「使瘫痪」（第 1 个义项：因神经受损而失去运动能力）；句意：脊柱受伤使他腰部以下瘫痪。

pos.zh: 使陷入停滞；使失去效力

collocations.zh: 使城市交通或运作瘫痪

derivatives.zh: 由过去分词形容词化而来，义为「瘫痪的；僵住的」
由现在分词形容词化而来，义为「令人发麻的；使人僵住的」

senses.title: To make a body or limb unable to move
senses.titleCN: 使瘫痪；使失去运动能力
senses.definition: to cause a person or part of the body to lose the power of movement, usually through injury or disease
senses.definitionCN: 因受伤或疾病而使某人或身体某部位丧失活动能力
senses.example: The stroke paralysed the left side of her face.
senses.exampleCN: 中风使她左侧面部瘫痪。
senses.why: The Greek element para sits beside the verb lyein, to loosen, so the body is loosened on one side and cannot hold its tension.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语要素 para（在旁）加上动词 lyein（松开），身体一侧被「松开」了，再也绷不起来。

senses.title: To freeze a person with fear or shock
senses.definition: to make someone unable to speak or act because of strong emotion such as fear
senses.definitionCN: 因强烈的恐惧等情绪而使某人说不出话或无法行动
senses.example: Fear paralysed her and she could not shout.
senses.exampleCN: 恐惧使她僵住，喊不出声。
senses.why: The physical loosening of the limbs is read as a loss of control, and fear takes command the same way.
senses.whyCN: 肢体的「松垮」被读成「失去控制」，而恐惧正是以同样的方式接管了身体。

senses.title: To bring activity to a standstill
senses.definition: to stop a place, service, or process from working or make it unable to continue
senses.definitionCN: 使某地、某项服务或某个过程停止运作或无法继续
senses.example: Heavy snow paralysed the northern rail network.
senses.exampleCN: 大雪使北部铁路网陷入瘫痪。
senses.why: The metaphor carries the image to any working system, so a network can lose the movement the body lost.
senses.whyCN: 隐喻把这个意象移到任何运作系统上：网络也可以像身体那样失去行动能力。

senses.title: To render a drug or agent powerless
senses.definition: to stop a substance, mechanism, or plan from having its effect
senses.definitionCN: 使某物质、机制或计划无法发挥效果
senses.example: One bad command can paralyse a piece of software before it even starts.
senses.exampleCN: 一条错误指令就可能让某款软件还没启动就失去作用。
senses.why: A system that cannot act is treated like a body that cannot move, so a blocking agent is said to leave its target frozen.
senses.whyCN: 无法起作用的系统被当作无法活动的身体，于是起阻断作用的东西被说成让对方僵住。

senses.title: To hold back an effort
senses.definition: to prevent a person or group from acting or making progress
senses.definitionCN: 使某人或某群体无法行动或推进
senses.example: Doubt paralysed him at the last minute, and the offer passed.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一刻的犹豫使他束手无策，机会就此错过。
senses.why: Effort needs movement, and movement is exactly what the loosened body has lost, so hesitation can be pictured the same way.
senses.whyCN: 努力需要推进，而被「松开」的身体恰恰失去了推进力，所以「犹疑不前」也能用同一幅画面来表现。

intro.en: Paralyse comes from Greek paralysis, formed from para beside and lyein to loosen, and enters French and English by the sixteenth century.
intro.cn: paralyse 来自希腊语 paralysis，由 para（在旁）与 lyein（松开）构成，在十六世纪进入法语和英语。

items.en: Greek paralysis means a loosening beside, especially the loosening of a limb on one side.
items.cn: 希腊语 paralysis 意为「在旁的松开」，尤指身体一侧肢体的「松垮」。

items.en: Medical writers use it for the loss of movement in a part of the body.
items.cn: 医学作者用它表示身体某部位失去活动能力。

items.en: Latin takes the noun as paralysis and adds the verb form paralyzare.
items.cn: 拉丁语接收名词 paralysis，并补充动词形式 paralyzare。

items.en: French paralyser carries the verb into the modern languages.
items.cn: 法语 paralyser 把这个动词带进近代诸语言。

items.en: English borrows it as the verb paralize, and at first the word is spelled the French way.
items.cn: 英语以 paralize 的形式借用，早期拼写沿用法语式样。

items.en: Spelling settles on the Greek y in British usage, while American English prefers paralyze.
items.cn: 英式拼写最终按希腊语写作 y，美式英语则写作 paralyze。

note.en: Paralyse belongs to a para- and lysis word family and is easily confused with palsy and with the spelling of paralyze.
note.cn: paralyse 属于 para- 与 lysis 词族，容易与 palsy 混淆，也要注意与美式 paralyze 的拼写差别。

entries.definition: the loss of the ability to move
entries.definitionCN: 瘫痪；麻痹（paralyse 的名词形态）

entries.definition: to examine something by breaking it into parts
entries.definitionCN: 分析（与 paralyse 共享 lyein 词根，含「松开」义）

entries.definition: the American spelling of the same verb
entries.definitionCN: 美式拼写；与英式 paralyse 同义（只是拼写不同，不是另一个词）

entries.definition: unable to feel anything
entries.definitionCN: 麻木的；失去知觉的

entries.definition: to stop something from moving
entries.definitionCN: 使无法移动；固定住

entries.definition: to damage badly so that something cannot work
entries.definitionCN: 使严重受损；使丧失能力（较含贬义，慎用）

normalIntro.en: Paralyse keeps the Greek loosen image, so the word always points at a body or system that can no longer move.
normalIntro.cn: paralyse 保留了希腊语「松开」的意象，因此这个词总是指向无法再活动的身体或系统。

normal.en: The noun paralysis and the verb paralyse differ only in their ending.
normal.cn: 名词 paralysis 与动词 paralyse 只差词尾。

normal.en: Be paralysed with fear is the standard idiom for being frozen by terror.
normal.cn: be paralysed with fear 是表示「吓得僵住」的标准习语。

normal.en: The past participle paralysed is used as an adjective most of the time.
normal.cn: 过去分词 paralysed 多数时候被当作形容词使用。

normal.en: British English writes -ise, while American English writes -ize.
normal.cn: 英式英语写作 -ise，美式英语写作 -ize。

normal.en: Compare analyse: both words end in the Greek root for loosening.
normal.cn: 对比 analyse：两个词都以表示「松开」的希腊词根收尾。

abstract.en: Picture a puppet whose strings are cut in one half, so the arm drops.
abstract.cn: 想象一个木偶，一侧的线被剪断，那只手臂顿时垂落。

abstract.en: Picture a city fully lit yet silent, with every bus and train halted.
abstract.cn: 想象一座灯火通明却鸦雀无声的城市，公交与列车全部停摆。

abstract.en: Picture traffic lights frozen at red at every crossing on a Monday morning.
abstract.cn: 想象周一清晨，每个路口的红灯都冻住不变。

examples.en: The infection can paralyse the muscles of the face.
examples.cn: 这种感染会使面部肌肉麻痹。

examples.en: The sudden blackout paralysed the whole town for hours.
examples.cn: 突如其来的断电使整个小镇瘫痪了数小时。

examples.en: A failure in the payment system paralysed trade for a full day.
examples.cn: 支付系统故障让交易瘫痪了整整一天。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕软来」——一害怕、一腿软，就动不了了，正是 paralyse 的「瘫痪、僵住」；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 para（在旁）+ lyein（松开）→ paralysis（一侧松开；瘫痪）→ 法语 paralyser → 英语 paralyse，核心义「身体一侧被松开而失去张力」。

sensesIntro.en: Paralyse begins with a body losing movement, then extends to a mind frozen by emotion and to systems and plans that stop working.
sensesIntro.cn: paralyse 始于身体失去活动能力，再扩展到被情绪冻住的头脑，以及停摆的系统与计划。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body whose limbs suddenly cannot obey.
core.cn: 核心意象：四肢突然不听使唤的身体。

branches.en: Loss of movement in the body is the literal sense.
branches.cn: 身体失去活动能力是字面义项。

branches.en: A mind frozen by fear copies the still body.
branches.cn: 被恐惧冻住的头脑复制了静止的身体。

branches.en: Places and networks stop working like a limb that cannot move.
branches.cn: 地点与网络像无法活动的肢体一样停摆。

branches.en: A blocked agent leaves its target powerless and still.
branches.cn: 被阻断的作用对象失去效力，如同静止。

branches.en: Stalled effort is the loosened body seen as a blocked action.
branches.cn: 停滞的努力就是被松开的身体在行动层面的投影。

intro.en: Paralyse joins the Greek prefix para- with lyein and its noun form -lysis, a family that also includes analyse.
intro.cn: paralyse 由希腊语前缀 para- 与 lyein 及其名词形式 -lysis 构成，同一词族还有 analyse。

latinIntro.en: Latin keeps the Greek noun paralysis and builds the verb paralyzare on it, which French then passes on.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语保留希腊语名词 paralysis，并据此造出动词 paralyzare，再由法语传给英语。

items.exampleCN: 前缀 para- 标明「一侧」。

items.example: Lyein provides the loosening in the word.
items.exampleCN: lyein 提供词中的「松开」义。

items.example: The ending -lysis appears in the noun form.
items.exampleCN: 名词形式带有 -lysis 词尾。

items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ise 构成英语动词。

items.example: The suffix -ing gives paralysing.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 paralysing。

items.example: The suffix -s gives the present form paralyses.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -s 构成现在时单数形式 paralyses。

items.example: A negative prefix such as un- would clash with the loosened state this word names.
items.exampleCN: 像 un- 这样的否定前缀，与这个词所指的「松开」状态相冲突。

definition_en: the loss of the ability to move or function, in a body or in any system
core_image: 定格的人：四肢完好却像被卸掉了发条
scene: 车祸之后，他胸部以下都失去了知觉和活动能力。Since the crash he has had paralysis below the chest.
sceneCN: 这里 paralysis 是「瘫痪」（第 1 个义项：因神经损伤而失去活动能力）；句意：自车祸以来，他胸部以下一直瘫痪。

pos.zh: 麻痹分析（决策分析中的术语）

collocations.zh: 分析瘫痪（过度分析导致无从决断）

senses.title: Physical loss of movement
senses.definition: the medical loss of the ability to move in part or all of the body
senses.definitionCN: 医学上指身体局部或全部失去活动能力
senses.example: Nerve damage can cause paralysis in one leg.
senses.exampleCN: 神经感染可能导致一条腿瘫痪。
senses.why: The Greek root pairs para (beside) with lysis (a loosening), so the limb is loosened and can no longer hold itself up.
senses.whyCN: 希腊词根把 para（在旁）与 lysis（松开）组合起来：肢体被「松开」了，再也撑不住自己。

senses.title: The numb state of a part
senses.definition: the state in which a limb or organ has lost feeling as well as movement
senses.definitionCN: 肢体或器官既失去感觉、也失去活动的状态
senses.example: The jaw loses all feeling after the injection, a brief numbness rather than true paralysis.
senses.exampleCN: 打针后下颌完全没有感觉，这是一种短暂的麻木而非真正的瘫痪。
senses.why: The loosening spreads beyond movement, so a part that feels nothing is described with the same word.
senses.whyCN: 「松开」的影响不限于活动能力，连感觉都失去了，于是也用同一个词来描述。

senses.title: A standstill in a system
senses.definition: a condition in which an organisation, service, or process has stopped working
senses.definitionCN: 某个组织、服务或流程完全停止运作的状态
senses.example: A strike in the ports caused paralysis across the supply chain.
senses.exampleCN: 港口罢工使供应链陷入停顿。
senses.why: A working system is pictured as a body, so when its activity stops the loosened, motionless image is reused.
senses.whyCN: 运作中的系统被想象成一具身体，一旦活动停止，就重新使用了那幅「松开、静止」的画面。

senses.title: Overwhelming inability to act
senses.definition: an inability to act that comes from strong emotion, doubt, or conflict
senses.definitionCN: 因强烈情绪、怀疑或冲突而无法行动
senses.example: Panic brought a kind of paralysis: nobody moved while the alarm rang.
senses.exampleCN: 恐慌带来了一种僵滞：警报响起时谁也没有动。
senses.why: The freezing of a fearful mind mirrors the freezing of a loosened body, so emotion borrows the medical word.
senses.whyCN: 恐惧中僵住的头脑映射了松弛身体的僵止，于是情绪借用了这个医学词。

senses.title: Paralysis analysis in decision making
senses.definition: a state in which too much study of a choice stops a person or group from deciding at all
senses.definitionCN: 对一项选择研究过多，反而使人或团体完全无法做出决定的状态
senses.example: Endless surveys left the committee in paralysis by analysis.
senses.exampleCN: 没完没了的调查让委员会陷入分析瘫痪。
senses.why: The loosened body cannot act, so a mind stuck inside endless weighing of options is said to suffer the same state.
senses.whyCN: 被松开的身体无法行动，被无穷权衡困住的头脑也被说成陷入了同样的状态。

senses.title: Deliberate removal of a key part
senses.titleCN: 摘除关键部分（工程术语）
senses.definition: the policy of removing a single crucial component so that a system can only fail safe
senses.definitionCN: 故意去掉某个关键部件，使系统只能以安全方式失效的做法
senses.example: Failsafe design sometimes plans a controlled paralysis of one part.
senses.exampleCN: 失效保护设计有时会计划让某一部件受控停摆。
senses.why: An agent that is out of action cannot be used wrongly, so an engineering tactic imagines its removal as an induced standstill.
senses.whyCN: 失去作用的东西就无法被误用，工程上的策略因此把「去掉关键件」想象成人为制造的一次停摆。

intro.en: Paralysis is a Greek medical noun formed from para, beside, and lysis, a loosening, and it reached English through Latin.
intro.cn: paralysis 是希腊医学名词，由 para（在旁）与 lysis（松开）构成，经拉丁语进入英语。

items.en: Greek paralysis names a loosening of the body on one side, later of limbs in general.
items.cn: 希腊语 paralysis 指身体某一侧的「松开」，后来泛指肢体麻痹。

items.en: Physicians of the Hippocratic school use it as a diagnosis for lost movement.
items.cn: 希波克拉底学派的医师用它作为失去活动能力的诊断名称。

items.en: Latin keeps the noun as paralysis and forms the adjective paralyticus.
items.cn: 拉丁语保留名词 paralysis，并构成形容词 paralyticus。

items.en: French can bring the word into English in the medieval period.
items.cn: 法语可能在中世纪把这个词带进英语。

items.en: The noun appears in medical and religious writing as early as the late Middle English period.
items.cn: 这个词在中古英语晚期已见于医学与宗教文本。

items.en: The sense widens to strikes, governments, and decision making.
items.cn: 义项扩展到罢工、政府与决策领域。

note.en: Paralysis is the noun behind the verb paralyse and the adjective paralytic, and it shares its ending with analysis and lysis.
note.cn: paralysis 是动词 paralyse 与形容词 paralytic 背后的名词，词尾与 analysis、lysis 同源。

entries.definition: the habit of studying a choice until no decision gets made
entries.definitionCN: 「分析瘫痪」：研究过度而迟迟无法决断

entries.definition: a condition that makes the body tremble or lose control
entries.definitionCN: 麻痹；震颤性瘫痪（与 paralysis 同源，但多指抽搐型）

entries.definition: a complete stop of movement or activity
entries.definitionCN: 停顿；停滞

entries.definition: the state of not being able to move
