normalIntro.en: Paralysis keeps the Greek image of loosening, so the word points to any state in which a body or system no longer moves.
normalIntro.cn: paralysis 保留了希腊语「松开」的意象，因此这个词指向身体或系统不再运转的任何状态。

normal.en: The verb is paralyse, and the adjective is paralytic.
normal.cn: 动词是 paralyse，形容词是 paralytic。

normal.en: The phrase paralysis by analysis is a common complaint in business writing.
normal.cn: paralysis by analysis（分析瘫痪）是商业写作中常见的抱怨。

normal.en: The plural paralyses is easy to confuse with the verb form paralyses.
normal.cn: 复数 paralyses 容易与动词第三人称单数 paralyses 混淆。

normal.en: The noun ending -sis usually marks a condition or process.
normal.cn: 名词词尾 -sis 通常标记一种状态或过程。

normal.en: Compare the suffix in analysis, which also ends with -lysis.
normal.cn: 对比 analysis：同样以 -lysis 收尾。

abstract.en: Picture a runner frozen mid-step, one foot off the ground and unable to come down.
abstract.cn: 想象一名跑者定格在跨步的瞬间，一只脚悬在空中落不下来。

abstract.en: Picture a factory line where every machine is lit but not one belt moves.
abstract.cn: 想象一条工厂生产线，机器都亮着灯，却没有一条传送带在转。

abstract.en: Picture a printer with a full tray of paper that cannot print a single page.
abstract.cn: 想象一台纸槽满满的打印机，却一页也打不出来。

examples.en: The illness left him with paralysis in both arms.
examples.cn: 这场病使他的双臂瘫痪。

examples.en: Paralysis of the port after the storm slowed deliveries for a week.
examples.cn: 风暴后港口陷入瘫痪，送货迟滞了一周。

examples.en: Writers often warn against paralysis by analysis in long meetings.
examples.cn: 作家们常提醒，冗长的会议里要小心分析瘫痪。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕了、懒死」——怕到懒到一动不动，就是瘫痪与停滞；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 para（在旁）+ lysis（松开）→ paralysis（一侧松开；瘫痪）→ 拉丁语 paralysis → 法语 paralysie → 英语 paralysis，核心义「被松开而无法活动」。

sensesIntro.en: Paralysis runs from the medical loss of movement, through numbness, to a stopped system, frozen emotion, and even a phrase about bad decision making.
sensesIntro.cn: paralysis 从医学上失去活动能力，经麻痹扩展到系统停摆、情绪僵住，甚至成为一个关于决策失误的固定说法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body that is whole but cannot move.
core.cn: 核心意象：躯体完好却无法活动。

branches.en: The medical loss of movement is the first sense.
branches.cn: 医学上的失去活动能力是第一个义项。

branches.en: Loss of feeling is the loosening taken one step further.
branches.cn: 失去感觉是「松开」再进一步的结果。

branches.en: Systems and machines can be stopped on purpose or by accident.
branches.cn: 系统与机器可能被故意或意外地停摆。

branches.en: A frozen mind and an over-analysed choice are the human forms of the same halt.
branches.cn: 僵住的头脑与过度分析的抉择，是同样停滞在人身上的表现。

branches.en: Nerve damage, numbness, and a stalled service all share the same still image.
branches.cn: 神经损伤、麻木与停滞的服务共享同一幅静止的画面。

intro.en: Paralysis is built from Greek para- and -lysis, with the English family of paralyse, paralytic, and paralysed around it.
intro.cn: paralysis 由希腊语 para- 与 -lysis 构成，英语中围绕它有 paralyse、paralytic、paralysed 等词。

latinIntro.en: Latin keeps the Greek noun paralysis and forms the adjective paralyticus, which English later takes up.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语保留希腊语名词 paralysis，并构成形容词 paralyticus，英语后来加以接收。

items.example: The prefix para- marks one side.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 para- 标明「一侧」。

items.example: The ending -lysis is the core of the noun.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -lysis 是名词的核心。

items.example: Paralysis is the head word itself.
items.exampleCN: paralysis 就是本词条的目标词。

items.meaning: builds a verb from the Greek stem
items.meaningCN: 由希腊词干构成动词的词尾
items.example: The ending -se gives the verb form.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -se 构成动词形式。

items.example: The suffix -tic gives paralytic.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -tic 构成 paralytic。

items.example: Paralytic describes an affected state.
items.exampleCN: paralytic 描述受影响的状态。

items.meaningCN: 过去式与形容词化词尾
items.example: The suffix -ed builds the participle.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成分词。

items.example: The suffix -ing builds the present participle.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成现在分词。

items.meaning: plural marker for nouns ending in s
items.meaningCN: 以 s 结尾名词的复数词尾
items.example: The plural ending gives paralyses.
items.exampleCN: 复数词尾构成 paralyses。

latinEntries.meaning: a loosening on one side, loss of movement

definition_zh: 瘫痪的；瘫痪病人；麻痹性的；极度紧张的；因酒而烂醉如泥的
definition_en: suffering from paralysis, or relating to paralysis; (informal) very drunk; (figurative) so frightened or tense that one cannot act
core_image: 全身的绳结突然松开：四肢仍连着，却再也拉不动了
scene: 洪水退后，救援队在倒塌的旅店墙边发现一个瘫痪的老人。After the flood, the rescue team found a paralytic old man beside the fallen wall of the inn.
sceneCN: 这里 paralytic 是「瘫痪的」（第 1 个义项：身体一侧或四肢失去活动能力）；句意：洪水退后，救援队在倒塌的旅店墙边发现一个瘫痪的老人。

pos.zh: 瘫痪的；麻痹的；（口语）烂醉的；（比喻）动弹不得的

derivatives.zh: 以 -sis 结尾的希腊语名词，义为「瘫痪；全面停顿」
英式拼写，动词，义为「使瘫痪；使失去作用」
美式拼写，动词，义为「使瘫痪；使麻痹」
由形容词加 -ly 构成，义为「瘫痪地；以麻痹的方式」
医学上同义场形容词，义为「偏瘫的」

senses.title: Unable to move the body
senses.definition: losing, or having lost, the power to move some or all of the body
senses.definitionCN: 失去或已经失去移动部分或全部身体的能力的
senses.example: The stroke left him partially paralytic on the left side.
senses.exampleCN: 那次中风让他左侧身体部分瘫痪。
senses.why: The Greek adjective paralytikos describes a person whose sinews have been loosened at the side, so the body can no longer be moved.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语形容词 paralytikos 指身体一侧的筋被「松开」的人，肌肉不再受控，身体因此无法移动。

senses.title: A person with paralysis
senses.definition: a person who is suffering from paralysis
senses.definitionCN: 正在遭受瘫痪之苦的人
senses.example: The clinic offers physiotherapy to paralytics and amputees alike.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所同时为瘫痪病人和截肢者提供理疗。
senses.why: An adjective of a condition turns into a noun for the person in that condition, as in other medical vocabulary.
senses.whyCN: 表示状况的形容词可以转用为名词，指处于该状况的人，这在医学词汇中很常见。

senses.title: Causing paralysis
senses.definition: of a substance, condition or disease, causing loss of movement in the body
senses.definitionCN: 指物质、疾病或状况导致身体失去活动能力的
senses.example: Doctors tested the paralytic substance in a controlled trial.
senses.exampleCN: 医生在受控试验中检测了这种引起瘫痪的物质。
senses.why: The same -ic ending that marks a quality lets the word shift from the sufferer to the cause that produces the loosening.
senses.whyCN: 同一个 -ic 词尾既能表示「具有某种性质」，也能从承受者转向造成「松开」的原因，于是长出「致瘫的」义。

senses.title: Frozen with fear
senses.definition: so frightened, tense or shocked that one cannot think or act
senses.definitionCN: 因恐惧、紧张或震惊而无法思考或行动的
senses.example: She felt paralytic with fear as the car skidded towards the barrier.
senses.exampleCN: 汽车朝护栏滑去时，她害怕得动弹不得。
senses.why: The core image of limbs that will not obey moves from the body to the mind, where fear freezes action just as injury freezes muscles.
senses.whyCN: 四肢不听使唤的画面从身体挪到心理，恐惧让行动冻结，就像受伤让肌肉冻结一样。

senses.title: Unable to function or stand
senses.definition: unable to stand, work or function because of extreme weakness or stiffness
senses.definitionCN: 因极度虚弱或僵硬而无法站立、工作或发挥作用的
senses.example: His legs were still weak and half paralytic after the fever.
senses.exampleCN: 高烧之后，他的双腿依然虚弱，几乎站不起来。
senses.why: Even before any disease, the root idea is a loosened side; anything that has gone slack cannot carry its own weight.
senses.whyCN: 早在指某种疾病之前，词根的意思就是「一侧松脱」；凡是松脱的东西都撑不住自身的重量。

senses.title: Senseless with drink
senses.definition: extremely drunk, to the point of being almost unable to move or speak
senses.definitionCN: 醉到几乎不能动弹或说话的程度的
senses.example: He came home paralytic and could not find the door.
senses.exampleCN: 他烂醉如泥地回家，连门都找不到。
senses.why: A drunk body also refuses to obey, so British informal speech borrows the clinical word for the most extreme kind of drunkenness.
senses.whyCN: 醉酒的身体同样不听使唤，英式口语便借这个临床词来形容最极端的醉态。

intro.en: Paralytic comes from Greek paralytikos, through Latin paralyticus, from the verb paralyein, which means to loosen at the side.
intro.cn: paralytic 来自希腊语 paralytikos，经拉丁语 paralyticus 进入英语，源头动词 paralyein 意为「从一侧松开」。

items.en: The verb paralysein is built from para, beside, and lyein, to loosen, and it means to disable or paralyse. The related adjective paralytikos describes someone so loosened at the side.
items.cn: 希腊语动词 paralysein 由「旁侧」的 para 与「松开」的 lyein 构成，意为「使瘫痪」；相关形容词 paralytikos 用来描述「一侧被松开」的人。

items.en: Medical Latin borrows the word as paralysis for the loss of movement and paralyticus for the person or condition affected by it.
items.cn: 医学拉丁语借入该词：paralysis 指失去活动能力，paralyticus 指受影响的人或状况。

items.en: The adjective paralitik appears in English medical writing, keeping both the bodily and the figurative loosening senses.
items.cn: 十四世纪，英语医学写作中出现 paralitik，同时保留身体与比喻两种「松脱」含义。

items.en: The spelling settles into paralytic. The word is used for palsy, for the disease that causes it, and also for a person who is struck by it.
items.cn: 十六至十七世纪拼写固定为 paralytic，既用于麻痹这一病症，也用于致病原因和患病的人。

items.en: Paralytic becomes a common adjective for paralysis and for anything that leaves one helpless, and British informal English adds the sense of being very drunk.
items.cn: 十九至二十世纪，paralytic 成为瘫痪及相关「令人无助」之事的常用形容词，英式口语又增添了「烂醉」一义。

note.en: Paralytic belongs to the Greek ly-, loosen, family, and stands beside clinical words for palsy and ordinary words for shock, numbness and drunkenness.
note.cn: paralytic 属希腊语 lyein（松开）词族，旁边既有表示麻痹的临床词，也有表示震惊、麻木和醉态的日常词。

entries.definition: the loss of the ability to move or feel
entries.definitionCN: 同根名词，义为瘫痪、麻痹。

entries.definition: to make someone or something unable to move or work
entries.definitionCN: 同根动词（英式拼写），义为使瘫痪、使失效。

entries.definition: the American spelling of the verb
entries.definitionCN: 同一动词的美式拼写，读音与英式相同。

entries.definition: an old medical word for paralysis, especially with trembling
entries.definitionCN: 古老的医学词，指瘫痪，尤指伴随颤动的麻痹。

entries.definition: unable to feel anything, usually in part of the body
entries.definitionCN: 麻木的，通常指身体某部分失去感觉，但未必失去力量。

entries.definition: unable to move because of terror or shock
entries.definitionCN: 因恐惧或震惊而定住不动，是比喻用法，不含生理病变。

entries.definition: having drunk too much alcohol
entries.definitionCN: 喝醉的；口语中与烂醉义相对照的普通说法。

normalIntro.en: Paralytic shares the Greek verb lyein with analysis, which means a loosening up, so the word pictures a body with its tight side undone.
normalIntro.cn: paralytic 与表示「拆开」的 analysis 同源于希腊语动词 lyein（松开），画面是身体紧绷的一侧被解开。

normal.en: The -ic ending turns a state into a describing word, as with heroic and poetic; paralytic describes a person or condition of paralysis.
normal.cn: -ic 词尾把状态变成描述词，如 heroic、poetic；paralytic 描述人或处于瘫痪的状况。

normal.en: The noun paralysis names the condition, the verb paralyse names making it happen, and the adjective paralytic describes those whom it affects.
normal.cn: 名词 paralysis 指病症本身，动词 paralyse 指使之发生，形容词 paralytic 描述受影响的人或物。

normal.en: Paralytic is common in medical writing, for example a paralytic stroke or a paralytic patient.
normal.cn: paralytic 常见于医学写作，如 paralytic stroke（致瘫中风）、paralytic patient（瘫痪病人）。

normal.en: In British informal speech, paralytic means extremely drunk, because a drunk body also refuses to obey.
normal.cn: 英式口语中 paralytic 表示烂醉，因为醉酒的身体同样不听使唤。

normal.en: Compare palsied, which is older and often implies trembling, with paralytic, which is the standard clinical adjective.
normal.cn: 对比 palsied：它更古老且常含颤动的意思；paralytic 是标准的临床形容词。

abstract.en: Picture strings that once pulled every limb being cut all at once, so the arms and legs hang loose.
abstract.cn: 想象原本牵动四肢的提线被同时剪断，手脚便松软地垂下来。

abstract.en: Imagine a car whose wheels still turn but whose engine has gone dead; the body is whole and yet it cannot move.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆车轮还能转、发动机却已熄火的汽车：车身完好，却寸步难行。

abstract.en: See a dry branch held flat as water rises around it, stiff and unable to lift itself.
abstract.cn: 想象一根干树枝被压在水线之下，僵硬地泡着，抬不起自己。

examples.en: The village was cut off by the snow and left half paralytic for a week.
examples.cn: 大雪切断了村庄与外界的联系，村里有整整一周半身瘫痪般的停滞。

examples.en: The patients were mostly elderly and some had been paralytic for years.
examples.cn: 病人多为老人，其中一些已经瘫痪多年。

examples.en: After three bottles of wine, he was absolutely paralytic.
examples.cn: 喝下三瓶葡萄酒之后，他完全烂醉如泥。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「par + a + lytic」——先想到 pair（一对），再到 paralyse（瘫痪）：瘫到连一对腿都抬不动；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 para（旁侧）+ lyein（松开）→ 希腊语 paralysein（使瘫痪）、paralytikos（一侧松脱的）→ 拉丁语 paralyticus → 英语 paralytic，核心义「一侧松脱、不能动弹」。

sensesIntro.en: Paralytic starts from the loosened body of a person struck by palsy, then takes in the person, the cause, and finally every situation where action is frozen.
sensesIntro.cn: paralytic 从中风病人被「松开」的身体出发，继而指病人本身、致病原因，最后扩展到一切行动被冻结的处境。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the strings that once moved every limb are cut at the same moment.
core.cn: 核心意象：牵动四肢的提线在同一刻全部被剪断。

branches.en: BODY LINE: the literal loss of movement is the sense medicine describes.
branches.cn: 身体线：字面上的失去活动能力，是医学描述中的本义。

branches.en: CAUSE AND SUFFERER: the adjective turns into a noun for the patient, while the same ending also names the substance or disease that causes it.
branches.cn: 因果线：形容词转为名词指病人，而同一词尾也能指引起瘫痪的物质或疾病。

branches.en: MIND LINE: terror freezes action the way injury freezes muscles.
branches.cn: 心理线：恐惧冻结行动，正如伤害冻结肌肉。

branches.en: WEAKNESS LINE: anything slack cannot carry its own weight or keep working.
branches.cn: 虚弱线：凡是松脱的东西都撑不住自身重量，也无法继续运转。

branches.en: EDGE LINE: the body that cannot obey reaches its extreme in a person too drunk to stand.
branches.cn: 极端线：身体不听使唤的极端，就是连站都站不稳的醉态。

intro.en: Paralytic is a Greek compound made of para, beside, and lyein, to loosen, with the ending -ic marking a describing word.
intro.cn: paralytic 是希腊语复合词，由表示「旁侧」的 para 与表示「松开」的 lyein 构成，词尾 -ic 表示描述性形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin medical writing took over Greek paralysis and paralyticus, and both meanings of loosening carried into English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语医学文献沿用了希腊语 paralysis 与 paralyticus，两种「松脱」含义都带进了英语。

items.example: The prefix para- tells us that only one side of the body is affected.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 para- 告诉我们只有身体的一侧受影响。

items.example: The suffix -lysis keeps the idea of loosening inside analysis.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -lysis 把「松开」的意思保留在 analysis 里。

items.example: Lyein supplies the picture of strings coming undone.
items.exampleCN: lyein 提供了提线松开脱落的画面。

items.meaning: to disable, to loosen at the side
items.example: Paralyein is the verb that gives the whole family.
items.exampleCN: paralyein 是整组词族的源头动词。

items.example: Paralysis names the condition itself.
items.exampleCN: paralysis 直接指病症本身。

items.example: Paralytikos describes the person suffering from it.
items.exampleCN: paralytikos 描述患此病的人。

items.meaning: relating to, having the quality of
items.example: The suffix -ic forms paralytic from paralysis, just as it forms heroic.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ic 由 paralysis 构成 paralytic，正如它构成 heroic。

items.example: The suffix -ly builds paralytically.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成副词 paralytically。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或过程的名词词尾
items.example: The ending -sis turns the action into the state of being paralysed.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -sis 把动作转为瘫痪的状态。

items.example: The British ending -e and the American ending -ze give paralyse and paralyze.
items.exampleCN: 英式 -e 与美式 -ze 分别构成 paralyse 和 paralyze。

definition_zh: 至上的；最重要的；至尊的；（北美）最高的山；最高统治者
definition_en: more important than anything else, or above all others in rank
core_image: 山峰高出群山，一览而下，一切都在它脚下
scene: 合同讨论到深夜，律师提醒大家条款可以再谈，但安全必须放在第一位。The lawyers talked long into the night and agreed that the safety of the workers must be paramount.
sceneCN: 这里 paramount 是「最重要的」（第 1 个义项：地位或重要性高于其他一切）；句意：律师们讨论到深夜，一致认为工人的安全必须放在第一位。

pos.zh: 至高无上的；最重要的；最优先的
最高的山；至尊者；最高统治者

derivatives.zh: 基础词加 -cy，义为「至上地位；最高权力」
基础词加 -ly，义为「至上地；最重要地」
基础词加 -ship，指至尊者的身份或地位
以 pre- 表达「居于前列」，义为「杰出的；卓绝的」

senses.title: Of the greatest importance
senses.definition: more important than all other things in a situation
senses.definitionCN: 在某一情形中比其余一切更重要的
senses.example: Patient safety is paramount in every operating theatre.
senses.exampleCN: 在每间手术室里，病人安全都是最重要的。
senses.why: Mount and amount share a Latin root for going up, so the word first names what rises above the rest, and importance is what rises highest.
senses.whyCN: mount 与 amount 同出表示「上升」的拉丁词根，因此这个词先指「高出其余的事物」，而重要性正是一同涨到最高处的那种东西。

senses.title: Supreme in rank
senses.definition: having the highest rank or authority, with no one above it
senses.definitionCN: 拥有最高等级或权力、其上再无他人的
senses.example: The company had become paramount in the shipping trade.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司在航运业中已居至尊地位。
senses.why: If something is at the top of the mountain, everything else lies below it, so the same word names the person or body with no superior.
senses.whyCN: 事物若位于山顶，其余一切都在它下方；于是同一个词也用来指其上再无上级的人或机构。

senses.title: A mountain higher than a neighbour
senses.definition: in North American geography, a mountain that stands higher than any mountain named after it
senses.definitionCN: 在北美地理中，指比以它命名的邻山山脉中的任何山峰都更高的山峰
senses.example: The massif is a paramount to the valley below it.
senses.exampleCN: 这座山体相对于下方的山谷，是一座最高的山峰。
senses.why: The physical meaning once covered anything supreme, and geography kept it for the summit that overtops its neighbours.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的实体义原本泛指一切「最高的东西」，地理学便把它保留给高过邻近山峰的那座主峰。

senses.title: A supreme ruler or chief
senses.definition: a ruler, chief or feudal lord who stands above all lesser ones
senses.definitionCN: 地位高于所有下级领主或首领的统治者、酋长或封建领主
senses.example: In the old system, a lord paramount held the land of the crown on behalf of the king.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧制度下，至尊领主代表国王持有王室的土地。
senses.why: The noun copies the adjective, naming the person at the very top of the ladder rather than the rank itself.
senses.whyCN: 名词义直接承接形容词，指等级阶梯顶端的那个人，而不是指等级本身。

senses.title: Taking priority over others
senses.definition: coming before all other claims, duties or interests when they conflict
senses.definitionCN: 在发生冲突时优先于其他一切诉求、职责或利益的
senses.example: In an emergency, the voice of the captain is paramount.
senses.exampleCN: 紧急情况下，船长的指令优先于一切。
senses.why: Rank is not only about status but about order, so the word turns into a rule: when two duties clash, the highest one wins.
senses.whyCN: 等级不仅关乎地位，也关乎次序，于是这个词变成一条规则：两种职责冲突时，排位最高的那一个胜出。

intro.en: Paramount was borrowed from Anglo-Norman French par amont, which means at or to the top, where amont comes from Latin ad montem, up the mountain.
intro.cn: paramount 借自英法（盎格鲁-诺曼）法语 par amont，意为「在最上方、到顶」，其中 amont 源于拉丁语 ad montem（向山上）。

items.en: Latin mons means mountain, and ad montem means up towards the mountain, a phrase of going upward.
items.cn: 拉丁语 mons 意为山，ad montem 意为「朝山而上」，是一句表示上升的短语。

items.en: Popular speech combines ad with montem into a single word for uphill, which Old French later keeps as amont.
items.cn: 民间拉丁语把 ad 与 montem 合成一个表示「上行」的词，古法语后来保存为 amont。

items.en: The phrase par amont, literally by the top, appears in the legal French of England from the mid thirteenth century.
items.cn: 自十三世纪中期起，英格兰的法律法语中出现短语 par amont，字面意为「在上方」。

items.en: The English spelling paramount is recorded in the fifteenth century, first as a legal position and then as a general adjective for whatever stands highest.
items.cn: 英语拼写 paramount 见于十五世纪，最初指一种法律地位，后来泛指任何处于最高处的事物。

items.en: By the late sixteenth century paramount is ordinary English for supreme, and a hundred years later Dr Johnson calls the adjective obsolete even though it has flourished ever since.
items.cn: 到十六世纪末，paramount 已是英语中表示「至高」的常规词；一百年后约翰逊博士却说这个形容词已废弃，可它此后的使用反而更加兴旺。

note.en: Paramount comes from a mountain phrase, and it sits between the mount family of words and the everyday vocabulary of importance.
note.cn: paramount 源自「山」的短语，位置介于 mount 一族词语与表示重要性的日常词汇之间。

entries.definition: a quantity, and the verb to add up to
entries.definitionCN: 同出 ad montem，指数量，或作动词意为「合计」。

entries.definition: a very high hill
entries.definitionCN: 同源于拉丁语 mons（山），义为高山。

entries.definition: an archaic word for a lover
entries.definitionCN: 只是拼写相近，词源不同：它来自法语的 par amour（因爱情），意为「情人」的旧词。

entries.definition: to climb up, or a mountain
entries.definitionCN: 同源词，动词意为「登上」，名词指山。

entries.definition: highest in rank or authority
entries.definitionCN: 近义词，指等级或权力最高，多用于权威与法律。

entries.definition: most important or leading in a group
entries.definitionCN: 近义词，指在一群中居首、最突出。

entries.definition: something required before something else can happen
entries.definitionCN: 义场相关词，指做某事之前必须具备的条件。

entries.definition: less important than something else
entries.definitionCN: 反义词，指重要性次一等、位居其后。

normalIntro.en: Break paramount into para and mount: walk beside the mountain until you reach the top of it.
normalIntro.cn: 把 paramount 拆成 para 与 mount：沿着山（mount）一步步走到它的顶端。

normal.en: Mount is the mountain inside the word, and the ending -amount is the same top-of-the-hill idea found in amount.
normal.cn: 词中藏着 mount（山），结尾的 -amount 与 amount 一样，都含「山顶、升至最高」的意思。

normal.en: The set phrase is of paramount importance, the most common way to use the adjective.
normal.cn: 固定搭配是 of paramount importance，这是该形容词最常见的用法。

normal.en: Because it is already superlative, paramount rarely takes more or most; writers prefer to say it is paramount.
normal.cn: paramount 本身已含最高级意味，较少再加 more 或 most，通常直接说某事是 paramount。

normal.en: The noun paramount mostly survives in titles such as Lord Paramount and Paramount Chief.
normal.cn: 名词用法主要保留在 Lord Paramount、Paramount Chief 一类头衔中。

normal.en: Compare paramount with supreme: both mean highest, but paramount is more often used with responsibilities and concerns.
normal.cn: 对比 supreme：两者都表示最高，但 paramount 更常与责任、关切等搭配。

abstract.en: See one peak lifted above a range of hills, with clouds far below it.
abstract.cn: 想象一座山峰耸立在群山之上，云层远远留在它的脚下。

abstract.en: Picture a single gold band laid across a pile of ordinary rings.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚金环压在普通铁环堆的最上面，一眼就能看出它的分量。

abstract.en: Think of a judge setting one document on the very top of a stack of files.
abstract.cn: 想象法官把一份文件放在整叠案卷的最上方，表示它优先处理。

examples.en: For the new government, rebuilding schools was of paramount importance.
examples.cn: 对新政府而言，重建学校是头等大事。

examples.en: The river remained paramount in the economy of the region for centuries.
examples.cn: 几个世纪里，这条河在该地区经济中始终居于至要地位。

examples.en: When values conflict, honesty must be paramount.
examples.cn: 当价值观发生冲突时，诚实必须摆在首位。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「牌 mount」——把最大的一张牌压在牌堆最高处，像山上加山；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 ad montem（向山上）→ 古法语 amont（在上方）→ 英法语 par amont（在顶端）→ 英语 paramount，核心义「位于最高处」。

sensesIntro.en: Paramount moves from the top of a mountain to the top of a ranking, and then to whatever must be dealt with first.
sensesIntro.cn: paramount 从山的顶端出发，走到等级的最上层，再走到凡事先办的那一层。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one peak stands above a whole range of hills.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座山峰高出整片群山。

branches.en: IMPORTANCE LINE: what stands highest in a situation is what matters most.
branches.cn: 重要性线：在一件事中站得最高的，就是最重要的。

branches.en: RANK LINE: the summit names the person or body with no superior.
branches.cn: 等级线：山顶用来指其上没有上级的人或机构。

branches.en: GEOGRAPHY LINE: the literal summit survives in the technical sense of a mountain higher than its neighbours.
branches.cn: 地理线：字面上的山峰义保留为「高过邻山的主峰」这一术语。

branches.en: TITLE LINE: the noun keeps the highest place in a ladder of feudal or tribal chiefs.
branches.cn: 头衔线：名词义保留在封建或部族首领阶梯的最顶端。

branches.en: ORDER LINE: highest rank becomes first claim whenever two duties clash.
branches.cn: 次序线：最高等级在两种职责冲突时变成最先兑现的那一项。

intro.en: Paramount is a phrase rather than a root word: par, by, plus amont, upward, so its parts are French words for above and mountain.
intro.cn: paramount 更像一个短语而非词根词：par（经由、在）加 amont（上行），各部分是法语中表示「上方」与「山」的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin ad montem, up the mountain, is the source of the whole phrase, and the same mons gives mount, mountain and amount.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ad montem（上山）是整条短语的源头，同一个 mons 也给出 mount、mountain 与 amount。

items.example: The French preposition par corresponds to Latin per.
items.exampleCN: 法语介词 par 对应拉丁语 per。

items.example: The prefix a- carries the sense of movement towards a place.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 a- 带「朝某处移动」的意思。

items.example: Mont means mountain and survives in names such as Vermont.
items.exampleCN: mont 意为山，还留在 Vermont 等地名里。

items.example: Amont names the upper stretch of a river.
items.exampleCN: amont 可指河流上游那一段。

items.example: Ad montem literally means towards the mountain.
items.exampleCN: ad montem 字面意思是「朝山而去」。

items.example: The noun mons is the ancestor of mount.
items.exampleCN: 名词 mons 是 mount 的祖先。

items.example: The ending -ant adds the feeling of being at the top.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ant 为词增添「正处于顶端」的感觉。

items.example: The suffix -cy forms paramountcy, meaning the highest authority.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -cy 构成 paramountcy。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms paramountly, the adverbial partner.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 paramountly。

items.example: The suffix -ship forms paramountship, a rare noun.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ship 构成 paramountship。

items.example: The element -mount points to rising above the rest.
items.exampleCN: -mount 这一成分指向「高出其余」。

latinEntries.meaning: the mountain, as the object of movement

definition_zh: 释义；改写；用不同的话表达相同意思
definition_en: to express the meaning of a text or statement in different words, or a reworded version of it
core_image: 同一棵树的枝干被重新捆成一束，果子还是那些果子
scene: 老师要求学生用自己的话复述这段话。The teacher asked the class to paraphrase the passage in their own words.
sceneCN: 这里 paraphrase 是「释义、改写」（第 1 个义项：用不同措辞传达原意）；句意：老师要求全班用自己的话复述这段话。

pos.zh: 释义；改写；用不同的话转述
释义；改写本；改述的文字

derivatives.zh: 基础词加 -stic，义为「改述的；释义性质的」
加 -able，义为「可以改述的」
借自希腊语的同义名词，指「改述、释义」
加 -er，指「转述者；释义者」

senses.title: To say the same thing in other words
senses.definition: to restate the meaning of a written or spoken passage in different words while keeping its sense
senses.definitionCN: 用不同的措辞重述书面或口头段落的意思，同时保留原有含义
senses.example: Students were asked to paraphrase the first paragraph of the report.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们被要求改写报告的第一段。
senses.why: Greek phrasein means to point out, and the prefix para- adds beside, so a paraphrase walks alongside the original saying the same thing from another side.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 phrasein 意为「指出」，前缀 para- 加「在旁边」，所以改写就是紧挨着原话，从另一侧说出同样的意思。

senses.title: A reworded version
senses.definition: a version of a text or statement that gives the same meaning in other words, or the act of producing it
senses.definitionCN: 用不同措辞表达同一含义的文本，或做出这种文字的行为本身
senses.example: This edition is a modern paraphrase rather than a literal translation.
senses.exampleCN: 这个版本是现代的改写本，而不是逐字直译。
senses.why: The verb turns into a noun, naming the result of walking beside the original text.
senses.whyCN: 动词转为名词，指伴随原文而行所得出的那份成文结果。

senses.title: To restate in order to explain
senses.definition: to put a difficult or dense statement into plainer words so that it can be understood
senses.definitionCN: 把难懂或晦涩的说法换成更浅白的话，以便他人听懂
senses.example: Let me paraphrase what the judge said so that everyone follows.
senses.exampleCN: 请让我把法官的话换种说法解释一下，好让大家都听得懂。
senses.why: If two versions stand side by side, the plainer one can cast light on the harder one, so the word drifts into explanation.
senses.whyCN: 两个版本并排而立时，浅白的那一版能照亮难懂的那一版，于是这个词渐渐带上解释的意味。

senses.title: To reword a song for new words
senses.definition: to adapt a song or musical piece by setting it to a fresh text in a related form
senses.definitionCN: 把歌曲或乐曲配上在形式上有联系的新歌词，从而加以改编
senses.example: The choir paraphrased the old hymn for the wedding.
senses.exampleCN: 合唱团为这场婚礼把那首老赞美诗改了词。
senses.why: In music the new words travel beside the old melody just as a paraphrase travels beside a text.
senses.whyCN: 在音乐里，新歌词与原旋律并肩而行，正如改写文字伴随原文本前行。

intro.en: Paraphrase comes from Latin paraphrasis, taken from Greek paraphrasis, which means a paraphrasing, from paraphrasein, to say the same thing in other words.
intro.cn: paraphrase 来自拉丁语 paraphrasis，后者借自希腊语 paraphrasis（释义、改述），源头是动词 paraphrasein（用别的话说同一件事）。

items.en: The verb phrazein means to point out, to show and to express. The phrase (phrasis) is the way something is worded.
items.cn: 希腊语动词 phrazein 意为「指出、表明、表达」；由此而来的 phrasis 指措辞方式，即一句话的说法。

items.en: The prefix para-, beside, is added so that paraphrasein means to say alongside, to express the same content in a different form.
items.cn: 加上前缀 para-（在旁边），paraphrasein 便意为「在旁边说、用不同形式表达同一内容」。

items.en: Hellenistic writers use paraphrasis for the literary exercise of recasting a passage, and the term passes into late Greek and Latin rhetoric.
items.cn: 希腊化时期作家用 paraphrasis 指改写文段的修辞练习，这一术语随后进入晚期希腊语与拉丁语修辞学。

items.en: Latin rhetoric adopts paraphrasis as the name of the exercise of rephrasing for clarity or ornament.
items.cn: 拉丁语修辞学采纳 paraphrasis，用来指为使表达更清晰或更华美而进行的改写练习。

items.en: English borrows both the noun paraphrase and the verb paraphrase from the restored Latin and Greek learning of the Renaissance, first in schools and in New Testament study.
items.cn: 十六世纪，英语随文艺复兴的古典学术复兴借入名词与动词 paraphrase，最初用于学校与《新约》研读。

items.en: By the eighteenth century paraphrase is ordinary classroom vocabulary, and today it also names a common task in language tests.
items.cn: 到十八世纪，paraphrase 已是课堂常用词；今天它还是语言考试里常见的题型名称。

note.en: Paraphrase is built on the Greek root for saying and showing, and it stands beside words for translation, summary and quotation.
note.cn: paraphrase 建立在希腊语「道出、表明」词根之上，旁边是翻译、概述与引用一族词。

entries.definition: a group of words that forms a unit of meaning
entries.definitionCN: 同源于希腊语 phrazein（说出），指由若干词组成、表达完整意思的词组或短语。

entries.definition: of the nature of a paraphrase
entries.definitionCN: 由基础词派生，义为「改述的；释义性质的」。

entries.definition: the Greek and Latin form of the noun
entries.definitionCN: 希腊语与拉丁语形式的同义名词，现代英语也偶用。

entries.definition: to write something again, often with substantial change
entries.definitionCN: 近义词，指重写，改动往往较大，可改变原意结构。

entries.definition: to express or translate something in another language or form
entries.definitionCN: 较正式，指用另一种语言或形式表达，常见于翻译语境。

entries.definition: to give only the main points in shorter form
entries.definitionCN: 义场相关词，指只留下要点、缩短篇幅，与改写保留全部意思不同。

entries.definition: to repeat the exact words of a speaker or text
entries.definitionCN: 反义对照词，指原样引用原文或原话。

normalIntro.en: Paraphrase is para, beside, plus phrase, so remember it as walking beside the original using a new phrase.
normalIntro.cn: paraphrase 是 para（旁边）加 phrase（措辞）：记作「用新的措辞走在原话旁边」。

normal.en: Greek phrazein means to speak or show, so phrase and paraphrase share the idea of wording.
normal.cn: 希腊语 phrazein 意为「说出、表明」，因此 phrase 与 paraphrase 都含「措辞」的意思。

normal.en: Paraphrase keeps the meaning but changes the wording, while a summary drops some meaning to shorten.
normal.cn: paraphrase 保留全部含义而更换措辞，summary 则为缩短篇幅而舍去部分含义。

normal.en: As a verb it takes a direct object: paraphrase the text, not paraphrase from the text.
normal.cn: 作动词时后接直接宾语：paraphrase the text，而不是 paraphrase from the text。

normal.en: In British exams, to paraphrase is the opposite of to copy, and credit is lost for lifting wording without quotation marks.
normal.cn: 在英式考试中，改写与照抄相对，直接搬用措辞而不加引号会被扣分。

normal.en: Compare paraphrase with translate: both move words aside, but translate moves across languages.
normal.cn: 对比 translate：两者都让措辞「挪位」，但 translate 是跨越语言，paraphrase 只是在同一语言里换说法。

abstract.en: Picture the same tree photographed from three different angles: the tree stays, the view changes.
abstract.cn: 想象同一棵树从三个不同角度拍照：树没变，画面变了。

abstract.en: See a sign on the road and its twin sign beside it, both pointing to the same town in different lettering.
abstract.cn: 想象路边的指示牌，旁边又立着一块牌子，用不同字体指向同一个城镇。

abstract.en: Hear one bell struck twice, once high and once low, the same chime in another voice.
abstract.cn: 想象同一口钟敲两下，一声高、一声低，是同一个声音换了嗓音。

examples.en: In your essay, paraphrase the sources rather than copying their sentences.
examples.cn: 在作文里请转述资料来源，而不要照抄原句。

examples.en: Her paraphrase of the lecture made the argument much clearer.
examples.cn: 她对讲座的改述让论证清楚了许多。

examples.en: He paraphrased the complaint so that the manager would not be offended.
examples.cn: 他把怨言换了个说法转述，以免经理受冒犯。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「papa 废 raze」——爸爸把旧稿「推倒重写」，其实就是换个说法；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 para-（在旁边）+ phrazein（说出、表明）→ 希腊语 paraphrasis（旁说、改述）→ 拉丁语 paraphrasis → 英语 paraphrase，核心义「紧挨原话、换种措辞说出」。

sensesIntro.en: Paraphrase begins as an exercise of recasting a text beside the original, then names the result, the plainer explanation, and even new song words.
sensesIntro.cn: paraphrase 起初指紧挨原文改述文段的练习，随后指改述的结果、更浅白的解释，乃至新填的歌词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the same tree, with its branches tied into a fresh bundle.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一棵树，枝干被重新捆成一束。

branches.en: ACT LINE: the verb names the act of rephrasing a passage.
branches.cn: 动作线：动词指改述一段文字的行为。

branches.en: RESULT LINE: the noun names the finished wording that walks beside the original.
branches.cn: 结果线：名词指伴随原文而生的那份改写成文。

branches.en: EXPLANATION LINE: a plainer version beside a dense one becomes the act of explaining.
branches.cn: 解释线：浅白版本与晦涩版本并立，就成了解释的行为。

branches.en: SONG LINE: new words beside an old melody are paraphrasing in music.
branches.cn: 歌曲线：旧旋律旁配上新歌词，就是音乐中的改述。

branches.en: BOTH FACES: the verb and the noun share one image, the meaning held constant while the words move.
branches.cn: 两面合观：动词与名词共享同一画面——意思不变，措辞挪动。

intro.en: Paraphrase is built from the Greek prefix para-, beside, and the root phrase, to speak, which English also has in phrase and phrasing.
intro.cn: paraphrase 由希腊语前缀 para-（在旁边）与词根 phrase（说出）构成，英语的 phrase、phrasing 也含这一词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin borrowed paraphrasis from Greek rhetoric and passed it to English in the sixteenth century together with the verb form.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语从希腊语修辞学借入 paraphrasis，并于十六世纪连同动词形式一起传给英语。

items.example: The prefix para- puts the new wording beside the old one.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 para- 把新措辞放在原话旁边。

items.example: The root phrase carries the idea of wording something.
items.exampleCN: 词根 phrase 带「把话讲出来」的意思。

items.example: Phrazein is the verb behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: phrazein 是整组词族背后的动词。

items.meaning: a way of speaking, a phrase
items.example: Phrasis gives English phrase.
items.exampleCN: phrasis 给出英语的 phrase。

items.example: Paraphrasis names the exercise of restating a passage.
items.exampleCN: paraphrasis 指重述文段的练习。

items.example: The suffix -stic forms paraphrastic, the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -stic 构成 paraphrastic。

items.example: The suffix -er forms paraphraser, the person.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 paraphraser。

items.example: The suffix -able forms paraphrasable, meaning able to be reworded.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -able 构成 paraphrasable。

items.example: The sibling prefix meta- gives metaphor, another Greek word for saying
items.exampleCN: 同族前缀 meta- 给出 metaphor，也是希腊语中与「说」相关的词。

latinEntries.meaning: the Greek accusative, carried over into Latin prose
latinEntries.meaningCN: 希腊语宾格形式，也被带入拉丁语散文。

definition_zh: 父母的；双亲的；与为人父母有关的；（生物学）亲代的；亲本的；（基因）来自父方或母方的
definition_en: relating to a parent or to parents as a whole, or in biology relating to the generation from which offspring come
core_image: 两个大人一左一右把孩子护在中间，三人的影子在地面上连成一个整体
scene: 傍晚的校门口，两个大人分站孩子两侧，一个接过书包，一个蹲下来系紧松开的鞋带。Parents crouched beside the child; parental support smoothed week one.
sceneCN: 这里 parental 是「父母的」（第 1 个义项：属于父亲或母亲这一角色的）；句意为父母的陪伴让孩子在学校的头一个星期轻松了许多。

pos.zh: 父母的；双亲的；为人父母的
（生物学）亲代的；亲本的（指产生子代的那一代）

collocations.zh: 家长指导（影视分级用语）

derivatives.zh: 由基础词加副词词尾 -ly 构成，义为「以父母的身份；在父母这一方面」
同根名词，由 parent 加状态词尾 -hood 构成，义为「为人父母的身份；做父母的阶段」
由否定前缀 un- 加基础词构成，义为「不合父母之道的；不像为人父母的做法」
同根名词，由动词 parent 加 -ing 构成，义为「养育；教养方式」

senses.title: Belonging to a parent
senses.titleCN: 父母的；属于父或母这一角色的
senses.definition: relating to the duties, rights, conduct or feelings of a parent towards a child
senses.definitionCN: 与父亲或母亲对子女的义务、权利、行为或感情有关的
senses.example: Both sets of grandparents met at the parental home before the wedding.
senses.exampleCN: 婚礼前双方祖父母在父母的家中见了面。
senses.why: The suffix -al turns the noun parent into an adjective, so parental names whatever belongs to a parent rather than to the child, the school or the state.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -al 把名词 parent 变成形容词，于是 parental 指的是属于父或母的那一部分，而不是孩子、学校或国家的那一部分：角色一旦被点名，义务、权利与情感就都挂在这个角色上。

senses.title: Involving both parents
senses.titleCN: 双亲共有的；父母双方的
senses.definition: shared by, or involving, the father and the mother together
senses.definitionCN: 由父亲和母亲共同拥有或共同参与的
senses.example: The court awarded parental rights to both sides of the dispute.
senses.exampleCN: 法院把亲权判给了纠纷的双方。
senses.why: The same adjective covers the pair as well as each person, which lets law and policy speak of parental consent or parental leave without naming the father or the mother.
senses.whyCN: 同一个形容词既能指一方，也能指双方，法律与政策于是可以不必点明父亲还是母亲，就直接说 parental consent 或 parental leave。

senses.title: Of the parental generation
senses.definition: in genetics and breeding, relating to the generation that produces the offspring being studied
senses.definitionCN: 在遗传学与育种中，指产生所研究子代的那一代
senses.example: The parental generation crossed in spring gave two distinct ratios by autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 春季杂交的亲代到秋季产生了两种明显不同的比例。
senses.why: Laboratory work needed a neutral label for the first generation in a cross, and the ordinary word for a parent was borrowed to supply one.
senses.whyCN: 实验需要一个中性词来标记杂交中的第一代，于是直接从日常的「父母」借来这个形容词充当术语。

senses.title: Inherited from one parent
senses.titleCN: 来自父方或母方的（亲源）
senses.definition: describing a gene or copy of a gene that came from the father or from the mother
senses.definitionCN: 指某个基因或基因拷贝来自父亲一方或母亲一方
senses.example: The parental copy of the gene carried the mutation.
senses.exampleCN: 来自父方或母方的那份基因副本携带着突变。
senses.why: Once parental means of a parent, it can also mark the side a gene came from, which is useful when the two sides differ.
senses.whyCN: 既然 parental 可以表示「属于某一方父母」，它就进一步用来标记基因来自哪一方；当父母双方的情况不同时，这个标记就派上了用场。

senses.title: Typical of parents
senses.titleCN: 父母式的；像父母一样操心或约束的
senses.definition: in a wider group, behaving in the protective or managing way that parents are expected to show
senses.definitionCN: 在更大的群体里，表现出人们期待父母才有的保护与管理姿态
senses.example: The coach had a parental tone when he told the team to be home by nine.
senses.exampleCN: 教练叮嘱球队九点回到住所时，用了父母般的口吻。
senses.why: The behaviour we call parental, namely protecting and laying down rules, can be copied by anyone who has charge of others.
senses.whyCN: 保护与立规矩本是父母的行为，任何照管他人的人都可以照做，形容词于是从家庭角色扩展到教练、老师或雇主身上。

intro.en: Parental is formed inside English from parent plus -al, and parent goes back through Old French to Latin parens, a parent, from the verb parere, to bring forth.
intro.cn: parental 是在英语内部由 parent 加词尾 -al 构成的；parent 经古法语上溯到拉丁语 parens（父母），源自动词 parere（生出）。

items.en: Parens, the present participle of parere, means one who brings forth, that is, a father or a mother.
items.cn: parens 是 parere 的现在分词，意为「生出的人」，即父亲或母亲。

items.en: Old French kept the word as parent, and English borrowed it in the late Middle Ages for a person who has produced a child.
items.cn: 古法语保留为 parent，英语在中世纪末期借入，指生下孩子的人。

items.en: For a time parent also named any source or cause, as in the parent of a crime; that sense later narrowed to the family.
items.cn: 有一段时间 parent 也指任何来源或起因，如罪行的 parents；后来这个意思收窄到家庭。

items.en: From around the sixteenth century the relational suffix -al made the adjective parental, which first served legal and theological texts about duties of parents.
items.cn: 大约十六世纪起，表关系的词尾「-al」构成形容词 parental，最初用于讨论父母义务的法律与神学文本。

items.en: Nineteenth-century biology took the adjective into English for the generation in a cross, which is why parental now pairs with generation and stock.
items.cn: 十九世纪的生物学把这个形容词用于杂交中的那一代，因此今天才有 parental generation 与 parental stock 这样的说法。

items.en: The twentieth century extended it to leave, consent, guidance and involvement, until the adjective carried policy as well as feeling.
items.cn: 二十世纪它被扩展到 leave、consent、guidance 与 involvement，这个形容词因此同时承载政策与情感。

note.en: Parental is the relational adjective of parent; it is easily confused with parental forms built on apparently similar stems, and with adjectives about marriage and family roles.
note.cn: parental 是 parent 的关系形容词，容易与词干看似相近的形容词混淆，也常与谈论婚姻、监护与家庭角色的词并置。

entries.definition: of a father, or related through the father
entries.definitionCN: 父亲的；父系的。多一个 t，只限父亲一方，与 parental 的「父母双方」不同。

entries.definition: of a mother, or related through the mother
entries.definitionCN: 母亲的；母系的。与 paternal 成对，二者合起来才是 parental 覆盖的双方。

entries.definition: the identity or origins of a person as a child of certain parents
entries.definitionCN: 出身；血统。同根名词，由 parent 加 -age 构成，问的是「谁的孩子」，不是「父母怎样」。

entries.definition: relating to marriage, especially to the relationship between husband and wife
entries.definitionCN: 婚姻的；夫妇之间的。看的是夫妻关系而非亲子关系，常与 parental 并列讨论家庭责任。

entries.definition: relating to a family, or found among members of a family
entries.definitionCN: 家庭的；家族内遗传的。范围比 parental 大，可指祖辈、兄弟姐妹与整户人。

entries.definition: a person legally responsible for a child who is not their own
entries.definitionCN: 监护人。法律上承担 parental 职责的人，但缺少「亲生父母」的身份。

normalIntro.en: Parental is simply parent plus the adjective ending -al: the ending means of or belonging to, so the whole word means of the parent.
normalIntro.cn: parental 就是 parent 加形容词词尾 -al；这个结尾表示「属于……的」，所以整个词的意思是「属于父母的」。

normal.en: Same suffix as national, cultural and natural: -al marks an adjective of relation.
normal.cn: 与 national、cultural、natural 用的是同一个词尾：-al 把名词变成关系形容词。

normal.en: Keep -al and -alize apart: parental is an adjective, but parent takes no -alize verb. The verb is parent, and its -ing form parenting names the activity.
normal.cn: 别把 -al 往动词上套：parental 是形容词，parent 没有对应的 -alize 动词；成年动词 parent 的 -ing 形式 parenting 才是名词「教养」。

normal.en: Pair it with -hood: parenthood is the state, parental is the quality, parent is the person.
normal.cn: 与 -hood 配对记：parent 是人，parenthood 是身份状态，parental 是这种身份的性质。

normal.en: Legal phrases fix the word in memory: parental consent, parental leave, parental responsibility.
normal.cn: 法律短语最能固定这个词：parental consent（家长同意）、parental leave（育儿假）、parental responsibility（父母责任）。

normal.en: In a biology text, parental generation is the first generation in a cross, the generation of the parents.
normal.cn: 在生物学里，parental generation 指杂交的第一代，也就是「父母那一代」。

abstract.en: Picture one umbrella held over a small figure by two hands, one from each side: the single pair of hands is the first sense, a role visible in what it does.
abstract.cn: 画面：一把伞罩在小小的人影上方，伞柄上搭着两只手，一左一右；这正是第一个义项所说的「父母这一角色」，角色只看它做了什么就看得出来。

abstract.en: Picture the same umbrella now held by four hands but only one signature on the form: the missing signature is the second sense, because both parents must agree.
abstract.cn: 画面：伞换成四只手一起握，纸上却只签了一个名字；缺的那个签名就是第二个义项所说的「父母双方」，共同的权利与同意缺一不可。

abstract.en: Picture a lab shelf of boxes where an older pair carries the same label: that labelled pair is the third sense, the parental generation.
abstract.cn: 画面：实验架上一排整齐的标本盒，标同一旧标签的那一对被称为亲代；这正是第三个义项所说的「亲代」，同一标签代表同一代。

examples.en: Parental involvement in reading at home predicts later school success.
examples.cn: 父母在家参与阅读，可以预示孩子日后在学校的表现。

examples.en: Employees may take parental leave of up to six months after a birth or adoption.
examples.cn: 雇员在生育或收养子女后最多可休六个月的育儿假。

examples.en: In the cross, the parental generation was pure-breeding for both traits.
examples.cn: 在这个杂交实验中，亲代在两个性状上都是纯系。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕热偷懒」——父母总是替孩子挡住热、偷偷把累活懒活都自己揽下；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 parere（生出）→ 现在分词 parens「生育者、父母」→ 古法语 parent → 英语 parent「父母」；英语再加关系词尾 -al 构成 parental，核心义「属于父或母这一角色的」。

sensesIntro.en: Parental starts as the adjective of a person, then widens to a pair of parents, narrows again in biology to a generation, and finally clings to habits that anyone in charge may copy.
sensesIntro.cn: parental 起初是「某位父母的形容词」，随后放宽到「父母双方」，在生物学里又收窄为「某一代」，最后被拿来形容任何掌事者身上那套像父母的作风。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two adults shielding one child from both sides.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个大人一左一右护住同一个孩子。

branches.en: The single parent is the starting point of the adjective.
branches.cn: 单个父母是这个词的起点：属于一方的那一份义务、权利与感情。

branches.en: Two parents meeting in one adjective is the family sense carried into law.
branches.cn: 父母双方共用一个形容词，这是家庭里的「共同」被搬进了法律语言。

branches.en: Biology moved the word from the household to the generation that produces offspring.
branches.cn: 生物学把词从饭桌移到了实验台：指的不是养育的义务，而是产生子代的那一代。

branches.en: Both the joint sense and the side-specific sense describe a pair of parents seen from different angles.
branches.cn: 「双方共同」与「来自某一方」是从两个角度描述同一对父母：一个看合力，一个看来源。

branches.en: Protecting and setting rules begin as a parent duty and can be borrowed by any adult in charge.
branches.cn: 保护与立规矩本是父母的义务，任何照管他人的成年人都可以把这套动作借去。

intro.en: Parental is a relational adjective built on parent; its word family runs through parent, parenthood, parenting and the adverb parentally.
intro.cn: parental 是以 parent 为基础的关系形容词，同族词包括 parent、parenthood、parenting 与副词 parentally。

latinIntro.en: Latin parere, to bring forth, supplied parens, one who brings forth; Old French passed it to English as parent, and English added -al.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 parere 意为「生出」，由此得来 parens「生育者」；古法语把 parent 传入英语，英语又加上词尾 -al。

items.meaning: to give birth to, to bring forth
items.example: Parere supplies the image of bringing a child into the world.
items.exampleCN: parere 提供「把孩子带到世上」这一层意象。

items.example: Parens is the Latin ancestor of the English noun parent.
items.exampleCN: parens 是英语名词 parent 的拉丁语祖先。

items.meaning: a person who has a child
items.example: Parent is the base from which the adjective grows.
items.exampleCN: parent 是形容词生长出来的词基。

items.example: The suffix -al turns parent into parental.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -al 把 parent 变成 parental。

items.example: Parental keeps the role, not the blood tie.
items.exampleCN: parental 看重的是角色，而不是血缘。

items.example: Add -ly and you have parentally.
items.exampleCN: 加上 -ly 就得到 parentally。

items.example: Parent fits -hood to form parenthood, the state of being a parent.
items.exampleCN: parent 加 -hood 构成 parenthood，表示「为人父母的状态」。

items.example: The verb parent takes -ing for parenting.
items.exampleCN: 动词 parent 加 -ing 得到 parenting。

items.example: Parent plus -age gives parentage, the line of descent.
items.exampleCN: parent 加 -age 得到 parentage，指血统出身。

items.meaning: a variant of the same stem, as in paternal and maternal
items.meaningCN: 同一词干的一种变体，如 paternal 与 maternal 中的 -t-
items.example: Latin pater stands beside parens, so the English pair paternal and maternal still splits the two parents.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 pater 与 parens 并存，所以英语里 paternal 与 maternal 这对词仍然把父母分成两方。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 父母的（晚期拉丁语关系形容词）

definition_zh: （某一行业、群体或时代特有的）说法；行话；用语；言语；谈论
definition_en: a particular way of speaking shared by a group, trade or period, or, in older writing, speech and talk in general
core_image: 一群穿同样工装的人围在机器旁，说出一串外人听不懂却彼此点头的短句
scene: 修车厂里，两个师傅隔着一辆抬高的车低声交谈，旁边的新学徒只能听懂一半。Doctors call recurring headaches chronic; medical parlance baffles the newcomer.
sceneCN: 这里 parlance 是「某一群体的特有说法、行话」（第 1 个义项：特定行业或群体的说法）；句意为照医学界自己的说法，反复发作的头疼叫作慢性的。

collocations.zh: 按通常的说法；通俗地说

forms.label: 极少见的复数（指多种说法）

derivatives.zh: 同根名词，与 parlance 共出法语 parler「说话」，原指供人交谈的接待室，后指店铺的某个「室」
远亲名词，共出法语 parler，原指「议事、谈话之处」，语义偏移为议会
近亲名词，源自法语 parler，义为「（与敌方）谈判」，词形同源而语义已与「说法」分开

senses.title: The talk of a group
senses.definition: the way of speaking that a particular profession, group or period habitually uses
senses.definitionCN: 某个行业、群体或时代习惯使用的说话方式
senses.example: In legal parlance, a room left in that state counts as abandoned.
senses.exampleCN: 照法律界的说法，那样空置的房间就算作被弃置了。
senses.why: Parlance comes from French parler, to speak, so it names speaking itself before it names anything about the group that does the speaking.
senses.whyCN: parlance 出自法语 parler「说话」，所以它首先指说话这件事本身，然后才用来限定是谁在说、说的是哪一群人内部的那套话。

senses.title: An ordinary way of saying it
senses.definition: the common or everyday use of a word, as opposed to a technical use in some field
senses.definitionCN: 与某个领域的技术用法相对，日常或通俗地使用某个词的方式
senses.example: In common parlance, the whole group is now simply the app.
senses.exampleCN: 按通常的说法，如今大家干脆把整个产品都叫那个应用。
senses.why: The phrase in common parlance sets up a contrast, so the noun marks one style of speech against another rather than naming a group on its own.
senses.whyCN: in common parlance 这个介词短语把两种说法摆在一起对照，于是名词成了「另一种风格」的标记，而不是单独指某一群人。

senses.title: A period way of saying it
senses.definition: the wording typical of a particular historical time rather than of a group
senses.definitionCN: 典型于某一历史时期的措辞，而非某一群体的说法
senses.example: The letters use a parlance that has long since vanished.
senses.exampleCN: 这些信件用的是一种早已消失的说法。
senses.why: Once parlance is a way of speaking, the group that shares it need not be a trade; it can be a whole age whose style of speech has since passed.
senses.whyCN: 既然 parlance 是一整套说话方式，共享它的人就不必是一个行业，也可以是整整一代人；当那代人散去，这种说法便只剩下文字里的痕迹。

senses.title: Speaking in general
senses.definition: in older or formal writing, speech or discussion as such, without reference to any special group
senses.definitionCN: 在较老或正式的文笔里，泛指言语或谈论，不指任何特定群体
senses.example: Much parlance on the matter had passed before anyone acted.
senses.exampleCN: 在有人真正行动之前，这件事已经被议论了许多。
senses.why: The oldest layer of the word is simply speech, which is why formal writing can still use it for talk that belongs to no profession.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最古老的一层意思就是「说话」，所以正式文笔至今仍可用它泛指谈论，而不必属于任何行业。

intro.en: Parlance goes back to Old French parler, to speak, from the Latin verb parabolare, from parabola, a comparison or a parable.
intro.cn: parlance 上溯到古法语 parler「说话」，再往前是拉丁语动词 parabolare，出自 parabola（比喻、寓言）。

items.en: Parabola meant a placing side by side, hence a comparison or a parable, and the verb parabolare came to mean to speak, especially in familiar speech.
items.cn: parabola 原指「并置」，由此有比喻、寓言之义；动词 parabolare 于是渐渐取得「说话」之义，尤其指日常交谈。

items.en: Parabolare became Old French parler, and with its endings the verb came to mean simply to speak or to talk.
items.cn: parabolare 演变为古法语 parler，连同它的各种词尾一起，这个动词的意思就是「说、谈」。

items.en: -ance, from Latin -antia, made nouns of condition or action, so parlance names the manner of speaking that a group keeps.
items.cn: 来自拉丁语 -antia 的 -ance 构成表示状态或动作的名词，因此 parlance 指的是一个群体所保持的那种说话方式。

items.en: The noun entered English about four hundred years ago, first naming talk and speech in general rather than any special style.
items.cn: 这个名词约在四百年前进入英语，最初泛指「谈话、言语」，而不是某种专门的风格。

items.en: By the nineteenth century phrases such as in common parlance had narrowed the noun to the style of speech belonging to a group.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，in common parlance 这类说法把这个名词收窄为某一群体所属的那种说话风格。

items.en: Today the noun almost always appears inside a prepositional phrase, with a qualifier naming the group, trade or era.
items.cn: 如今这个名词几乎总出现在介词短语里，后面或前面带一个限定成分，点明是哪个群体、行业或时代的说法。

note.en: Parlance is the noun of speaking, close in sound to dozens of adjectives beginning with pare, part and par, and close in meaning to words for the language of a trade.
note.cn: parlance 是表示「说话」的名词，读音上容易与许多以 pare、part、par 开头的形容词混淆，意思上则与各种表示「行业语言」的词相邻

entries.definition: the way that someone or something looks, or the arrival of someone
entries.definitionCN: 外表；出现。与 parlance 共 -ance 结尾，但词根是 appear「出现」，词源不同，只是拼写相近。

entries.definition: a vehicle that carries people who are ill or injured
entries.definitionCN: 救护车。同样以 -lance 收尾，词根却是拉丁语 ambulare「走动」，与 parlance 词源不同，只是拼写相近。

entries.definition: a room in a house for sitting and receiving visitors, or a shop room used for one service
entries.definitionCN: 起居室；接待室；店铺的某个服务「室」。与 parlance 同出法语 parler，同根，只是词尾不同。

entries.definition: words and phrases used by a particular group that outsiders find hard to understand
entries.definitionCN: 行话；专业黑话。最贴近 parlance，但明显带贬义，暗示外行听不懂、没必要。

entries.definition: the set of technical terms used in a subject or field
entries.definitionCN: 术语；术语体系。看重的是一批具体词条，而 parlance 看重的是整体的说话腔调。

entries.definition: the language or idiom used by ordinary people in daily life
entries.definitionCN: 本地话；俗语。强调的是「民间日常」而非某个行业的说法，常与正式学术语言对立。

normalIntro.en: Parlance is the speaking noun of parler: the -ance ending makes a style-of-speech noun out of the verb to speak.
normalIntro.cn: parlance 是 parler 的「说话」名词：-ance 这个结尾把动词「说」变成一个表示说话风格的名词。

normal.en: Same shape as parlour and parliament: all three descend from the French verb to speak or talk.
normal.cn: 与 parlour、parliament 同形：三者都源自法语中「说话、交谈」的动词。

normal.en: Learn it as a chunk: in common parlance and in legal parlance fix both the preposition and the word order.
normal.cn: 按整块记：in common parlance 与 in legal parlance 把介词和词序一起记牢。

normal.en: After in, add the group: in medical parlance, in police parlance, in modern parlance.
normal.cn: 在 in 之后补上群体：in medical parlance、in police parlance、in modern parlance。

normal.en: Contrast the antonyms of register: jargon sounds dismissive, parlance stays neutral.
normal.cn: 对比语体色彩：jargon 听起来带轻视，parlance 则是中性的。

normal.en: Look at the modern cousins: French parler, Spanish hablar and Italian parlare all descend from the same Latin speaking verb.
normal.cn: 看现代的小表亲：法语 parler、西班牙语 hablar、意大利语 parlare 都出自同一个拉丁语「说话」动词。

abstract.en: Picture a mechanic and an apprentice at the same bench: the mechanic strings several short words together and the apprentice nods, though she has not yet learned them.
abstract.cn: 画面：修车厂同一张工作台前，师傅连说几个短词，学徒点头称是，其实她还没学会这些词；这一画面正对应第一个义项所说的「某一群体的说法」。

abstract.en: Picture the same bench with two layers of labels on one toolbox: the technical label above and the street label below, side by side.
abstract.cn: 画面：同一个工具箱贴两层标签，上层是技术名称、下层是街坊的叫法，两张并排；对应第二个义项「通常的说法」，两种说法就摆在一起对照。

abstract.en: Picture an old letter in an archive box, with a note in a modern hand saying that these words are no longer used.
abstract.cn: 画面：档案盒里一封旧信，旁边有人用今天的笔迹备注「这些说法如今已不用」；对应第三个义项「某一时代的用语」，说法随那代人一起退场。

examples.en: In common parlance, a firm that grows that fast is simply a rocket.
examples.cn: 照通常的说法，增长那么快的公司干脆就叫火箭。

examples.en: In legal parlance, the child is now a ward of the court.
examples.cn: 用法律界的说法，这个孩子此刻是法院监护的对象。

examples.en: The engineers fell into their own parlance, and the visitors stopped taking notes.
examples.cn: 工程师们转而用起了自己的行话，来访者只好停下笔记。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕冷死」——行话太冷门，外行一听就怕冷场；这只是读音联想，与词源无关，真正的来源是法语「说话」。

root: 拉丁语 parabola（并置、比喻）→ 动词 parabolare（说话）→ 古法语 parler（说）→ 古法语名词形式 + -ance（状态、动作）→ 英语 parlance，核心义「某群人的说话方式」。

sensesIntro.en: Parlance begins as the speech of a group, is used to set the ordinary style of speech against the technical one, is extended to the style of an age, and still survives in formal writing for speech in general.
sensesIntro.cn: parlance 起于「一群人的说法」，常常被用来把通俗说法与技术说法摆在一起对照，又被推广到整整一个时代，最后在正式文笔里仍保留泛指「言语」的老义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a work crew speaking in code that insiders share.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一班组的人说着只有他们自己听得懂的那套话。

branches.en: A group speaking together is the earliest and most common sense.
branches.cn: 一群人共用一套说法，这是这个词最早也最常见的义项。

branches.en: The ordinary sense of a phrase is set up as the contrast of a technical one.
branches.cn: 「通常的说法」总是站在技术说法的对面：它的价值就在于给出一个大众都听得懂的版本。

branches.en: Replace the group with a period and the same word names the style of an age.
branches.cn: 把「群体」换成「时代」，同一个词就改指一代人留下的说话风格。

branches.en: The oldest sense of speech in general is the trunk from which the group sense branched.
branches.cn: 泛指「言语」的老义是主干，限于某个群体的新义是从这根主干分出来的枝。

branches.en: Both the ordinary style and the period style are defined by contrast with another way of speaking.
branches.cn: 「通俗说法」与「时代用语」都要靠与另一种说法对照才成立，因此都离不开语境。

intro.en: Parlance is built on the French verb stem parl-, to speak, with the English noun ending -ance; its relatives group around parlour, parley and parliament.
intro.cn: parlance 建在法语动词词干 parl-（说话）与英语名词词尾 -ance 之上；它的同族词围绕 parlour、parley 与 parliament 分布。

latinIntro.en: The line runs from Latin parabola to the verb parabolare, to speak, then to Old French parler; -ance from Latin -antia supplies the noun ending.
latinIntro.cn: 这条线从拉丁语 parabola 走到动词 parabolare（说话），再进入古法语 parler；名词结尾 -ance 则来自拉丁语 -antia。

items.example: Parabola began as a placing side by side, which is what a comparison does.
items.exampleCN: parabola 起初意为「并置」，而比喻正是把两样东西并排放。

items.example: Parabolare turned the image of comparison into plain speaking.
items.exampleCN: parabolare 把「比较」的意象变成了寻常的「说话」。

items.example: Parler is the French verb from which the English noun is formed.
items.exampleCN: parler 是构成这个英语名词的法语动词。

items.example: The suffix -ance makes a noun of the act of speaking.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ance 把「说话」这一动作变成名词。

items.example: Parlance names the style, not the speaker.
items.exampleCN: parlance 命名的是说法，不是说话的人。

items.example: Latin -antia became French and English -ance.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 -antia 变成了法语与英语里的 -ance。

items.example: Parlour keeps the talk in the room.
items.exampleCN: parlour 把「谈话」留在房间里，指的是供人交谈的屋子。

items.example: Parley keeps the sense of talking to someone across a line.
items.exampleCN: parley 保留了「隔着界线与人交谈」的意思。

items.meaning: a body that talks and decides
items.example: Parliament names the place where people talk to reach decisions.
items.exampleCN: parliament 本指人们聚谈并以谈定事的地方。

items.meaningCN: in 加限定语再加 parlance 的固定格式
items.example: Nearly every use of the noun sits inside a prepositional phrase.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词几乎总是嵌在一个介词短语里使用。

definition_zh: 参与者；参加者；参赛者；（语言学）参与角色；（金融）参与方；（体育）有资格参赛的人
definition_en: a person who takes part in an activity, event, study or arrangement, especially with others
core_image: 一张圆桌被推到房间中央，每人都伸出一只手按在桌面上，手与手之间没有空位
scene: 研讨室的圆桌刚摆好，主持人在白板上写下议题，十几个人依次落座并翻开同一份材料。Each participant signed a form.
sceneCN: 这里 participant 是「参加者」（第 1 个义项：参加某项共同活动的人）；句意为讨论开始前每位参加者都签了同意书。

pos.zh: 参与的；作为参加者之一的

derivatives.zh: 由同一拉丁词干派生的动词，义为「参加；参与」
由该拉丁动词加表动作的名词尾 -ion 构成，义为「参与；参加」
由名词 participation 加 -ory 构成，义为「参与式的；让众人参与的」
由动词 participate 的现在分词构成，义为「参与的；参加其中的」
由否定前缀 non- 加基础词构成，义为「未参加者；旁观者」

senses.title: One who takes part
senses.definition: a person who joins in an activity, event or discussion together with others
senses.definitionCN: 与他人一起加入某项活动、事件或讨论的人
senses.example: Every participant received the reading list a week in advance.
senses.exampleCN: 每位参加者都提前一周收到了书单。
senses.why: Latin particeps joins pars, a part, to capere, to take, so a participant is literally one who takes a part in something larger than themselves.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 particeps 由 pars（一部分）与 capere（拿取）合成，所以参与者字面上就是「在一个比自己更大的整体里拿下一份」的人。

senses.title: An active sharer
senses.titleCN: 积极投入的人；主动分担的人
senses.definition: a person who contributes effort, not merely one who is present
senses.definitionCN: 付出努力、而不只是人在现场的人
senses.example: He was an active participant in the debate, not a silent guest.
senses.exampleCN: 他是辩论中积极的参与者，而不是沉默的客人。
senses.why: Taking a part is something done with the hands rather than a seat occupied, so the noun implies that the person gives something to the activity.
senses.whyCN: 「拿一份」是伸手去做的动作，而不是占一个座位；因此这个名词自带「这个人给出了点什么」的含意，不是只出场而已。

senses.title: A person in a study
senses.titleCN: （研究或调查的）被试；样本对象
senses.definition: a person who gives data in a research study, trial or survey
senses.definitionCN: 在研究中提供数据、接受调查或参加实验的人
senses.example: Half of the participants reported better sleep after the trial.
senses.exampleCN: 半数参与者在试验后反映睡眠更好。
senses.why: Research needed a word that respected the people who supply data, so the neutral participant replaced older words that treated them as mere subjects.
senses.whyCN: 研究需要一个尊重数据提供者的称呼，于是中性的 participant 取代了把人只当「对象」看的旧称；这个词提醒写作者：数据背后是人。

senses.title: A contestant
senses.definition: a person in a competition, race or tournament
senses.definitionCN: 参加比赛、赛跑或锦标赛的人
senses.example: Each participant was timed from gate to gate.
senses.exampleCN: 每名参赛者都从起点门到终点门计时。
senses.why: A competition is one of the largest stages the verb is used with, and the noun follows the word there as well.
senses.whyCN: 比赛是「拿一份」这种说法最常出现的场面之一，名词也就顺势跟了过去，指赛场上领到自己赛号的那个人。

senses.title: A party in finance
senses.definition: a bank or other party that shares in a loan, a deal or an insurance arrangement
senses.definitionCN: 在贷款、交易或保险安排中分担一份的银行或其他参与方
senses.example: Four banks were participants in the syndicated loan.
senses.exampleCN: 有四家银行参与了这笔银团贷款。
senses.why: Commerce reused a word that already meant one who takes a part, because sharing a loan is literally each party taking a share of it.
senses.whyCN: 商业借用了这个本已表示「拿一份」的词：分摊一笔贷款，正是每一方各自拿下一份，语义几乎不需要改动。

senses.title: A role in grammar
senses.definition: a person or thing named in a sentence as taking part in the action or state described
senses.definitionCN: 句子中作为动作或状态的承担者而出现的参与者
senses.example: The agent is the participant that carries out the action.
senses.exampleCN: 施事就是执行动作的那个参与者。
senses.why: Linguistics borrowed the everyday word for someone who takes part, and reapplied it to the entities that take part in what a sentence describes.
senses.whyCN: 语言学把日常的「参加的人」借来，重新用在句子所描述的事情里「参与其中有份」的角色上：动作的施事、受事都算参与者。

senses.title: The adjectival use
senses.definition: used before a noun, as in participant observation, to mark a method or role in which others take part
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词前，如 participant observation，表示他人也参与其中的方法或角色
senses.example: The participant observer lived with the family for two years.
senses.exampleCN: 这位参与式观察者与这家人同住了两年。
senses.why: Nouns in English can stand before other nouns, so the same form also labels a method or a role rather than a person.
senses.whyCN: 英语名词可以放在另一个名词前面作定语，同一个词形于是又能标出方法或角色，而不只指人。

intro.en: Participant comes from the Latin present participle participans, of the verb participare, to share, from particeps, one who takes a part, from pars, a part, and capere, to take.
intro.cn: participant 来自拉丁语现在分词 participans，源自动词 participare（分享），再往前是 particeps（拿一份的人），由 pars（部分）与 capere（拿取）合成。

items.en: Pars meant a part or a share, and capere meant to take or to seize, so particeps described one who takes a part.
items.cn: pars 意为「部分、一份」，capere 意为「拿、抓取」，合起来 particeps 指「拿一份的人」。

items.en: The verb participare meant to share or to take part, and its present participle participans named the one then taking part.
items.cn: 动词 participare 意为「分享、参加」，它的现在分词 participans 指正在拿一份的那个人。

items.en: French kept the participle as participant, and the noun reached English with the ending still intact.
items.cn: 法语保留了这个分词形式 participant，名词带着完整的词尾进入了英语。

items.en: English uses the noun from about the sixteenth century, chiefly for a person who has a share in a matter.
items.cn: 英语大约在十六世纪开始使用这个名词，主要指对某件事有份的人。

items.en: Social science and market research made it the neutral word for people who supply data, replacing older labels that treated them as objects.
items.cn: 社会科学与市场调查把它变成指「提供数据的人」的中性词，取代了把人当对象的旧称。

items.en: Finance and linguistics borrowed it later, for parties sharing a loan and for roles inside a sentence.
items.cn: 商业与语言学后来分别借用它：一边指分摊贷款的参与方，一边指句子内部的角色。

note.en: Participant is the person noun behind participate, easily swapped with words for players in a contest, and often heard in research where it has displaced older terms.
note.cn: participant 是 participate 背后指人的名词，容易与各类「选手」词混用，在研究语境里则常取代旧称成为标准说法。

entries.definition: to take part in an activity
entries.definitionCN: 参加；参与。同根动词，说的是动作；participant 说的是人，两者不能互换。

entries.definition: the act of taking part
entries.definitionCN: 参与；参加。同根名词，指「参与这件事」，而 participant 指「参与的人」。

entries.definition: a verb form used as an adjective or to make tenses
entries.definitionCN: 分词。与 participant 同为分词形式出身，拼写相近，但词根是「分一份」而义指非限定动词。

entries.definition: a person who competes for a prize
entries.definitionCN: 参赛者；竞赛者。限于比赛语境，participant 则可用于任何共同活动。

entries.definition: a person who is present at a meeting or event
entries.definitionCN: 出席者；到场者。只说人到了，不保证出力；participant 通常暗示真的投入。

entries.definition: a person belonging to a group or organization
entries.definitionCN: 成员；会员。强调长期归属，participant 强调在一次具体活动中有份。

normalIntro.en: Participant is part plus cip, from capere, to take: the person who takes a part and carries it into the whole.
normalIntro.cn: participant 是 part 加上出自 capere（拿取）的 cip：拿下自己那一份、并把它带进整体的人。

normal.en: Same family, different jobs: participate is the act, participant the person, participation the state.
normal.cn: 同一家族分工不同：participate 是动作，participant 是人，participation 是状态。

normal.en: Keep the -ant family straight: attendant, contestant and assistant are also people, from verbs in -ate.
normal.cn: 把 -ant 这一家理清：attendant、contestant、assistant 也都是「人」，都从 -ate 结尾的动词来。

normal.en: In research writing, prefer participant to subject: the first respects the person, the second sounds clinical.
normal.cn: 写研究报告时，用 participant 而非 subject：前者把人当人，后者听起来像在说实验对象。

normal.en: The adjective use is fixed in phrases such as participant observation and participant consent.
normal.cn: 形容词用法固定出现在 participant observation 与 participant consent 这样的固定短语里。

normal.en: Do not confuse participant with participle: one is a person, the other is a verb form.
normal.cn: 别把 participant 和 participle 搞混：一个是人，一个是动词的一种形式。

abstract.en: Picture a round table pushed into the middle of a room, with a hand from every person resting on it and no gap between the hands.
abstract.cn: 画面：圆桌被推到屋子中央，每个人都有只手按在桌面上，手与手之间不留空隙；这张所有人都在场的桌，就是第一个义项所说的「一块儿参加的人」。

abstract.en: Picture the same table where only one pair of hands moves, passing a heavy box across; the extra effort marks the second sense.
abstract.cn: 画面：同一张桌上，只有一双手在动，把一只重箱子递过桌面；出力的那双手正是第二个义项所说的「主动投入」，坐在桌旁并不等于参与。

abstract.en: Picture a clipboard passed round the table with a name written beside each numbered line, and a printed sheet beside it for the researchers to count.
abstract.cn: 画面：一块夹板在桌上传递，每一行编号旁都写下名字，旁边还放着一张给研究者计数的表格；这就是第三个义项所说的「研究里的参与者」，人是数据的主人。

examples.en: Participants were told that they could leave the study at any time.
examples.cn: 参与者被告知，他们随时可以退出这项研究。

examples.en: Only a willing participant can be a useful witness.
examples.cn: 只有自愿的参与者才能成为有用的见证人。

examples.en: In the activity analysis, the subject of the verb is the participant that acts.
examples.cn: 在事件分析里，动词的主语就是执行动作的参与者。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕踢死扮他」——赛场上他怕被踢，索性当个十足投入的参赛者（participant）；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 pars（部分）+ capere（拿取）→ particeps（拿一份的人）→ participare（分享）→ 现在分词 participans → 古法语 participant → 英语 participant，核心义「在整体中拿下一份的人」。

sensesIntro.en: Participant starts as a person taking a part, deepens into a person who gives effort, then settles into research, competition, finance and grammar as each field finds its own part to take.
sensesIntro.cn: participant 起初指「拿下一份的人」，再指「肯出力的人」，随后分别进入研究、比赛、金融与语法：每个领域都从中挑出自己想要的那一份「参与」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one hand resting on a shared table.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手按在大家共用的桌面上。

chain: A PARTY IN A FINANCIAL DEAL

branches.en: A person taking a part is the first and widest sense.
branches.cn: 拿下自己那一份的人，是这个词最宽也最早的义项，圆桌边任何一个伸了手的人都在其中。

branches.en: Giving effort is the deepening of that first sense.
branches.cn: 肯出力是把第一个义项加深一层：桌上的手不只放着，还真的把东西递了过去。

branches.en: Research turned the neutral word into a label for people who supply data.
branches.cn: 研究把这个中性的词变成给数据提供者的称呼，于是夹板与计数表也进了画面。

branches.en: A contest is one stage where the taking of a part is watched and timed.
branches.cn: 比赛是「拿一份」被公开计时的那块舞台：参赛者领了赛号，就进了第一个义项所指的整体。

branches.en: Finance, grammar and compound labels all reuse the same taking of a part at different scales.
branches.cn: 金融、语法与复合定语把同一个「拿一份」用在不同的尺度上：一笔贷款的份额、句中的一个角色、一个方法的名称。

intro.en: Participant is Latin through and through: pars and capere form particeps, and the verb participare gives the noun, the verb participate and the abstract participation.
intro.cn: participant 整个词都出自拉丁语：pars 与 capere 合成 particeps，动词 participare 再衍生出这个名词、动词 participate 与抽象名词 participation。

latinIntro.en: Pars means a part and capere means to take; joined in particeps they mean taking part, and the related verb participare carries the same idea into French and English.
latinIntro.cn: pars 意为「部分」，capere 意为「拿取」；二者在 particeps 中合为「参与其中」，同源动词 participare 又把这一意思带进了法语与英语。

items.example: Latin pars is the first half of the word.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 pars 是这个词的前一半，意为「部分」。

items.example: Capere supplies the act of taking a part.
items.exampleCN: capere 提供「拿取一份」这个动作。

items.example: Particeps joins a part to a taking.
items.exampleCN: particeps 把「部分」与「拿取」合在一起。

items.example: Participare grew into the French verb and the English noun.
items.exampleCN: participare 演变成法语动词与英语名词这一路。

items.meaningCN: 正在做……的人的分词词尾
items.example: The participle ending -ns marks the person doing the sharing.

definition_zh: 微粒；颗粒物；（固体或液体）微粒的；颗粒状的
definition_en: a very small solid or liquid particle carried in air, smoke or water, or relating to such particles
core_image: 烟囱口飘出无数细尘，小到肉眼看不见，却悬在空气里久久不散
scene: 清晨的城市被一层灰白的雾罩住，远处的楼群只剩模糊的轮廓，空气里带着呛人的味道。Health officials warned that particulate pollution from traffic and factories could make breathing problems worse.
sceneCN: 这里 particulate 是「颗粒物、微粒污染」（第 1 个义项：悬浮在空气中、能进入呼吸道的细小固体或液体颗粒）；句意是卫生官员警告，来自交通与工厂的颗粒物污染会加重呼吸疾病。画面里可辨识的物件：灰白的雾、远处模糊的楼群、行人的口罩。

pos.zh: 微粒；颗粒物（尤其是空气中的污染物）
微粒的；颗粒状的（多用于技术语境）

collocations.zh: 颗粒物；颗粒物质（常缩写为 PM）
颗粒过滤器；微粒捕集器

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 pars「部分」的指小形 particula 演变而来，义为「小部分」，即微粒、粒子
由本词加后缀 -free（无……的）构成，义为「无颗粒的」
由本词加 -ed 构成的派生形，义为「成颗粒状的、含微粒的」，多见于早期技术文献

senses.title: Tiny solids or liquids floating in the air
senses.definition: very small solid or liquid pieces that stay suspended in the air and can be breathed in
senses.definitionCN: 悬浮在空气中、能够被吸入呼吸道的细小固体或液体颗粒
senses.example: Levels of particulate peaked during the winter heating season.
senses.exampleCN: 冬季取暖期间颗粒物浓度达到高峰。
senses.why: The Latin root particula means a tiny part, and the suffix -ate marks the thing as a physical, granular mass rather than a single speck.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 particula 意为「极小的部分」，后缀 -ate 让它指一整类颗粒状物质，而不是单单一粒尘埃；天气一冷、炉火烧得多，空气里的这些小东西就成倍数地增加。

senses.title: A technical term for granular matter
senses.definition: a collective, technical name for small solid grains in a carrier medium such as air, smoke, water or a gas stream
senses.definitionCN: 对空气、烟雾、水流或气流中所含细小固体颗粒的总称，属于技术术语
senses.example: Engineers measured the particulates released from the exhaust pipe.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师们测量了排气管排出的颗粒物。
senses.why: Because particula names a small part, the plural can mean the whole population of grains carried by a fluid, which is how scientists talk about it.
senses.whyCN: 因为 particula 本就指「小部分」，复数形式自然变成「一整套小颗粒」的集合称谓；科学家不数单颗尘埃，而是把气流里所有细粒一并称作微粒物质。

senses.title: Relating to grains rather than pieces
senses.definition: describing something made of or known by small separate grains, as opposed to whole objects or dissolved material
senses.definitionCN: 形容由细小独立颗粒构成的，或表现为颗粒状的，以区别于整体物件或溶解状态
senses.example: The sample was particulate, with loose grains of sand.
senses.exampleCN: 这份样品呈颗粒状，夹杂着散落的沙粒。
senses.why: The adjective sense keeps the word at the scale of single grains: the thing is not one solid object but a loose assembly of small parts.
senses.whyCN: 形容词义把视角停在单颗颗粒的尺度上：描述对象不是一整块东西，而是一堆松散的小部分；这也正是「部分」的词根含义换了一种词性后的延续。

senses.title: Pollution understood in particles
senses.definition: air pollution described in terms of small particles, often fine enough to penetrate deep into the lungs
senses.definitionCN: 以细小颗粒来计量的空气污染，其中细颗粒往往小到能深入肺部
senses.example: Many cities ban older cars to cut particulate in the air.
senses.exampleCN: 许多城市禁止老旧车辆上路，以减少空气中的颗粒物。
senses.why: Once the word names the matter, policy and public health borrow it as a shorthand for the pollution that matter causes.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词成为「颗粒物」的名字，政策与公共卫生话语就直接借它指代这些颗粒造成的污染；用词从物质本身转到了它带来的危害，于是多出一个义项。

senses.title: Screens and filters against particles
senses.definition: used of equipment, such as a filter, that is designed to catch or block small grains before they reach people or machines
senses.definitionCN: 用于形容过滤器一类设备，其用途是在颗粒到达人体或机械之前把它们拦截下来
senses.example: The plant fitted a particulate filter to each chimney.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂给每根烟囱装了颗粒过滤器。
senses.why: If particulates are the enemy, then any device defined by its fight against them takes the same name, so the word spreads to the tools as well.
senses.whyCN: 如果颗粒物是敌人，那么专门对付它们的装置也会借用同一个名字：先有「颗粒物」这个敌方概念，才有「颗粒过滤器」这个针对性设备；词义从对象延伸到了应对手段。

senses.title: A speck you can see
senses.definition: a single tiny grain or speck visible with a microscope or in bright light, the most concrete form of the word
senses.definitionCN: 在显微镜下或强光中能看见的单个细小颗粒，是该词最具体的用法
senses.example: A few dark particulates drifted in the glass of water.
senses.exampleCN: 水杯里有几粒深色微粒在漂动。
senses.why: This goes back to particula as one small part: the smallest, most visible end of the word, a grain you can almost pinch.
senses.whyCN: 这是回到 particula「一个小部分」的本义：词义最具体的一端，几乎是能用手捏起来的一粒细渣；从整片雾霾收拢到眼前一粒，画面随之变小。

senses.title: Particles carried by water
senses.definition: small solid grains suspended in water, such as silt, clay or sediment clouding a river or an aquarium
senses.definitionCN: 悬浮在水中的细小固体颗粒，如浑浊河水或鱼缸里的淤泥、黏土或沉积物
senses.example: The current carried fine particulate downstream after the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 暴雨过后，水流把细颗粒物带向下游。
senses.why: The same grain model transfers from air to water: a carrier medium moves tiny parts that then settle as sediment.
senses.whyCN: 同一套「颗粒模型」从空气挪到了水里：载着它们移动的介质换成了水流，等到流速变慢，这些细小部分就沉降成泥沙；义项随介质的改变而扩展。

senses.title: Small parts versus the whole
senses.definition: an abstract use in which a whole is described as broken into small parts, the most figurative extension of the word
senses.definitionCN: 较抽象的用法，把一个整体描述为由细小部分构成，是该词最抽象的引申
senses.example: In the report the problem of dust is treated as particulate rather than as one single event.
senses.exampleCN: 报告把粉尘问题当作细碎累积现象来处理，而不是一次单独的事件。
senses.why: At its widest the word stops naming matter and starts naming a way of seeing a whole as many small parts, which is the furthest the particle image can stretch.
senses.whyCN: 用到最宽处，这个词不再指某种实物，而是指一种视角：把一个整体看成许多细小部分的总和；颗粒意象被拉到抽象层面，这也是「小部分」这个词根能延伸到的极限。

intro.en: Particulate is a technical Latin-derived word built on particula, the diminutive of pars, part.
intro.cn: particulate 是拉丁语来源的技术词，建立在 particula（pars「部分」的指小形）之上。

items.en: Pars means a part or share of a whole.
items.cn: 拉丁语 pars 意为整体中的一个部分或份额。

items.en: Particula, the diminutive of pars, means a small part, a particle.
items.cn: pars 的指小形 particula 意为「小部分、微粒」。

items.en: English borrows the pattern of forming technical adjectives with the Latin suffix -ate.
items.cn: 英语借用拉丁语后缀 -ate 构成技术形容词的构词方式。

items.en: Chemistry and engineering adopt particulate for matter made of separate small grains.
items.cn: 化学与工程学采用 particulate 指由分散小颗粒构成的物质。

items.en: The word is fixed in air-quality discussion, and particulate matter is generally shortened to PM.
items.cn: 该词在空气质量讨论中固定下来，颗粒物通用说法常缩写为 PM。

items.en: Today it works as both a countable noun and a technical adjective.
items.cn: 今天它既可作可数名词，也可作技术形容词。

note.en: Particulate sits on the same small-part root as particle, while its near meanings are the related terms of air and grain.
note.cn: particulate 与 particle 共享「小部分」词根，而近义一侧则是空气与颗粒相关的词。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real root particula and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的词根 particula，以及这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Particle plus -ate: the small part becomes a technical word for grains.
normal.cn: particle 加 -ate：一个个小部分就成了指颗粒的技术词。

normal.en: Particulate matter is usually shortened to PM in reports.
normal.cn: 「颗粒物」在报告里通常缩写为 PM，记缩写就能连带记住全称。

normal.en: The same family shows a small part at work: particle, particular, partly.
normal.cn: 同一词族里都是「小部分」在起作用：particle、particular、partly。

normal.en: A particulate filter catches grains before they reach the air.
normal.cn: 「颗粒过滤器」把颗粒挡在进入空气之前。

normal.en: Compare dust: dust settles on surfaces, while particulate is the technical term for grains carried in air and water.
normal.cn: 对比 dust：dust 落在表面上，particulate 是气流与水流里颗粒的技术说法。

abstract.en: Picture a city morning under a grey, hazy blanket of tiny specks.
abstract.cn: 想象城市清晨笼着一层灰蒙蒙的细小尘幕。

abstract.en: Imagine counting the sparks in a plume of smoke.
abstract.cn: 想象数一数烟缕中闪烁的细尘。

abstract.en: Think of sand grains in a glass of water slowly sinking.
abstract.cn: 想象杯水中的沙粒一点点沉下去。

examples.en: Fine particulates from diesel engines can affect the lungs.
examples.cn: 柴油发动机排出的细颗粒物会影响肺部。

examples.en: The lab tested the water for particulate matter.
examples.cn: 实验室检测了水中的颗粒物。

examples.en: New rules require every factory to install a particulate filter.
examples.cn: 新规定要求每座工厂安装颗粒过滤器。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕提扣」——一怕吸入小颗粒，就提起衣扣掩住口鼻 → 微粒、颗粒物

root: 拉丁语 pars「部分」→ 指小形 particula「小部分、微粒」→ 英语 particle、particulate（-ate 构成技术形容词）。词根清楚可查；-ate 后缀从 19 世纪起被用于化学与工程术语，并非直接从某一种语言整体借入。

sensesIntro.en: Particulate starts from a visible speck of a small part, spreads to the collective grains carried by air and water, and then to the pollution, the filters and the abstract view of a whole as many small parts.
sensesIntro.cn: particulate 从一粒可见的小部分出发，扩展到空气与水流携带的成片颗粒，再延伸到颗粒物污染、过滤装置，以及把整体看作许多细小部分的抽象视角。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: fine grains drifting in the air, too small to hold and too many to count.
core.cn: 核心意象：空气里漂着的细尘，小到捏不住，多到数不清。

branches.en: THE AIR: the same grains are pollution when they harm us and technical matter when we measure them.
branches.cn: 空气线：同一些颗粒，伤人时叫污染，被测量时叫技术物质。

branches.en: THE SINGLE GRAIN: the adjective and the visible speck keep the word at the size of one small part.
branches.cn: 单粒线：形容词与可见微粒都让词义停在一个小部分的尺度上。

branches.en: THE CONTROL: once the grains are a danger, the word names both the pollution and the filters built to stop it.
branches.cn: 治理线：颗粒一旦成为威胁，这个词既指污染，也指为拦住它而造的过滤器。

branches.en: THE WATER: the carrier medium changes, but the tiny part moving and settling is the same.
branches.cn: 水流线：携带介质变了，移动并沉降下来的细小颗粒还是同一回事。

branches.en: THE ABSTRACT END: a whole seen as many small parts is the furthest the particle image reaches.
branches.cn: 抽象端：把整体看成许多细小部分，是颗粒意象延伸得最远的地方。

intro.en: Particulate is built from Latin small-part words plus English technical suffixes, so the family grows by ordinary derivation.
intro.cn: particulate 由拉丁语「小部分」词与英语技术后缀构成，词族靠普通派生扩展。

latinIntro.en: Latin pars, particula and particella record the small-part root; the suffix -ate is Latin but reused technically in English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pars、particula 与 particella 记录了「小部分」词根；后缀 -ate 源自拉丁语，在英语中被技术性地再用。

items.example: Pars is the root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: pars 是整组词的根本来源。

items.example: Particula gives English particle.
items.exampleCN: particula 派生出英语 particle。

items.meaningCN: 构成形容词或名词的后缀
items.example: The suffix -ate forms particulate from particula.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ate 把 particula 变成了 particulate。

items.example: Particle is the everyday small piece.
items.exampleCN: particle 是日常的「小颗粒」。

items.example: Particulate covers the whole study word.
items.exampleCN: particulate 覆盖了本条词条的全部用法。

items.example: The suffix -free forms particulate-free.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -free 构成 particulate-free。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms particulated in technical texts.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ed 在技术文献中构成 particulated。

items.example: Particular shares the small-part root.
items.exampleCN: particular 与目标词共享「小部分」词根。

items.example: Partly shows the same root as an adverb.
items.exampleCN: partly 体现同一词根的副词形式。

definition_zh: 游击队员；党派支持者；党派的；偏袒一方的；游击式的
definition_en: a strong supporter of a party, group or cause, especially an armed fighter in a small local force, or showing strong and often one-sided support
core_image: 山坡上的人抓起一支猎枪，站到自家村子这一边，哪怕对手是正规军
scene: 战争结束时，村民们在山谷里赶走了占领军，如今邻国的新政府想把这一带划给对手一方。A partisan from the hills joined the fight and refused to give up his rifle.
sceneCN: 这里 partisan 指「游击队员、地方武装战士」（第 1 个义项：在本乡本土作战的非正规武装成员）；句意是山里的游击队员参战，并且拒绝交出他的步枪。画面里可辨识的物件：山坡、猎枪与山谷里的村落。

pos.zh: 游击队员；党徒、党派支持者
党派的；偏袒一方的；游击式的

collocations.zh: 党派政治；党同伐异的政治

derivatives.zh: 由本词加后缀 -ship（状态、身份）构成，义为「党派性；党同伐异」
