senses.title: An armed local fighter
senses.definition: a member of a small armed group that fights an occupying force or a stronger army in its own region
senses.definitionCN: 在本地区与占领军或更强武装作战的小型非正规武装的成员
senses.example: Villagers sheltered a partisan hiding in the barn.
senses.exampleCN: 村民们庇护了一名藏在谷仓里的游击队员。
senses.why: From Latin pars, a part or side, comes the old sense of a supporter of one side; in occupied Europe the word shifted to the men who took up arms for their side.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 pars 意为「部分、一边」，引申出「支持某一方的人」；在被占领的欧洲，这个词又滑向「拿起武器支持自己一方的人」，于是从支持者变成了实际作战的游击队员。

senses.title: A loyal member of a party or camp
senses.definition: a person who strongly and uncritically supports a political party, group or cause
senses.definitionCN: 坚定并且往往不加批判地支持某个政党、团体或主张的人
senses.example: The senator is a partisan; she never votes against her party.
senses.exampleCN: 这位参议员是个坚定的党派人士，从不投与本党相悖的票。
senses.why: If many parts make a whole, being loyal to your own part means backing it automatically, which is where the political sense comes from.
senses.whyCN: 如果整体由许多部分构成，那么忠于「自己那一部分」就是无条件拥护它；这层政治含义正是从「部分」词根直接长出来的。

senses.title: One-sided and partial
senses.definition: showing strong preference for one side, so that judgement is not fair or open
senses.definitionCN: 强烈偏向某一方，导致判断不够公正或不够开放
senses.example: A partisan report blamed only one team in the dispute.
senses.exampleCN: 一份偏袒的报告只把争议中的一方当作责任方。
senses.why: A person loyal to one part will read every issue through that part, so the adjective describes an attitude taken from a fixed side.
senses.whyCN: 忠于某一部分的人会透过那一部分的立场去看待所有问题；形容词就把这种「先站稳一边」的态度定格下来。

senses.title: Guerrilla methods
senses.definition: describing irregular, harassing warfare carried out by local fighters against a stronger force
senses.definitionCN: 形容由地方武装对更强大军队进行的不正规、袭扰性的作战方式
senses.example: The border troops trained against partisan tactics.
senses.exampleCN: 边防部队针对游击战术进行训练。
senses.why: Because partisan first named the fighter, it could then describe his method: small, local, harassing force rather than open battle.
senses.whyCN: 既然 partisan 先指作战的人，再把他的方式拿来说明手段就顺理成章：以小股、本地、袭扰代替正面交战；词义从人转移到了打法。

senses.title: A party line in public life
senses.titleCN: 党派的；党派性的（政治用语）
senses.definition: belonging to or shaped by political party loyalty rather than by neutral judgement
senses.definitionCN: 属于某个政党或由党派忠诚所塑造的，而非出自中立的判断
senses.example: The new district map was called a partisan draw.
senses.exampleCN: 新选区图被称作一次党派性的划线。
senses.why: In modern democracies the name of a supporter became a label for any matter decided by party loyalty, from voting to drawing district lines.
senses.whyCN: 在现代民主政治中，「支持者」的名字变成了一个标签，凡是按党派忠诚决定的事都能贴上它，连选区划界也不例外；词义从人扩展到了制度性做法。

senses.title: Sharp support for a cause
senses.definition: an enthusiastic defender of a cause or idea outside formal politics
senses.definitionCN: 在正式政治之外，对某种主张或理念的积极拥护者
senses.example: She is a partisan of free speech on campus.
senses.exampleCN: 她是校园言论自由的坚定拥护者。
senses.why: The spelling of the root spread to any cause you take a side on, so a fan of an idea, not only of a party, can be called a partisan.
senses.whyCN: 词根的「站队」意味扩散到任何你所主张的事上，所以不只是党派，任何理念的拥护者都能叫 partisan；义项从政党扩展到了观点与主张。

senses.title: A label for viewpoint rather than fact
senses.definition: used to describe writing, history or media that takes sides instead of aiming at neutrality
senses.definitionCN: 用于形容文学、史学或媒体作品：站定一方而不是追求中立
senses.example: Some historians call the book a partisan account of the war.
senses.exampleCN: 一些历史学家称这本书是一部带立场的战争叙述。
senses.why: Once a person is a partisan of a side, any record they make tends to take that side, so the word comes to describe viewpoint as a quality of texts.
senses.whyCN: 一个人既然是某一方的 partisan，他留下的记录往往也站在那一方；于是这个词成了一种「文本性质」的描述，用来提示读者所读文字背后的立场。

intro.en: Partisan travelled from Latin pars, part, through Italian and French, changing from a division of a people to a fighter for one of those divisions.
intro.cn: partisan 由拉丁语 pars「部分」经意大利语、法语传入英语，从「人群的分派」演变为「为某一派而战的人」。

items.en: Pars means a part, a share, or a side in a dispute.
items.cn: 拉丁语 pars 意为部分、份额，或争执中的一方。

items.en: Partigiano could mean a member of a faction, and later an irregular soldier of a local force.
items.cn: 意大利语 partigiano 可指某一派系的成员，后来指地方非正规武装的士兵。

items.en: Partisan names a follower of a faction and the weapon it carried.
items.cn: 法语 partisan 既指派系追随者，也指他们所用的长矛。

items.en: English borrows partisan for a follower of a faction and for a halberd-like spear.
items.cn: 英语借入 partisan，表示派系追随者，也指一种类戟长矛。

items.en: World War II resistance fighters give the word its modern armed sense, first of all in occupied Europe.
items.cn: 二战抵抗运动战士赋予这个词现代的武装含义，首先是在被占领的欧洲。

items.en: Today the adjective mainly means one-sided, and the noun covers fighters, party loyalists and fans of a cause.
items.cn: 今天形容词主要指「偏袒一方的」，名词则覆盖游击队员、党派拥护者与理念支持者。

note.en: Partisan shares its root with partition, party and partial, while its near meanings split into fighters and people who take sides.
note.cn: partisan 与 partition、party、partial 共享词根，近义一侧则分成「武装者」与「站队者」两条线。

entries.definition: a division into parts, or the act of dividing
entries.definitionCN: 分开；隔断；分隔物

entries.definition: an organized political group, or a group gathered for fun
entries.definitionCN: 政党；社交聚会；一群人

entries.definition: not complete, or favouring one side
entries.definitionCN: 部分的；偏袒的

entries.definition: a fighter in a small irregular force operating in local terrain
entries.definitionCN: 游击队队员；游击作战者

entries.definition: someone who backs a person, team or idea
entries.definitionCN: 支持者；拥护者

entries.definition: showing an unfair preference for one side
entries.definitionCN: 有偏见的；偏袒的

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin root pars and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁词根 pars，以及这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Pars means part, so a partisan stands with one part of the whole.
normal.cn: pars 意为「部分」，partisan 就是站在整体的某一部分那边。

normal.en: Party and partisan share the same root: a party person is a partisan.
normal.cn: party 与 partisan 同根：党派里的人就是 partisan。

normal.en: Partisan politics is the phrase most reports use for party-line conflict.
normal.cn: partisan politics 是新闻报道里最常用的说法，指党派之争。

normal.en: Non-partisan means taking no side, the direct opposite of the word.
normal.cn: non-partisan 意为不站队，正是这个词的反面。

normal.en: Compare guerrilla: both fight local irregular wars, but partisan also means a party loyalist.
normal.cn: 对比 guerrilla：两者都打地方非正规战，但 partisan 还兼指党派拥护者。

abstract.en: Picture a farmer on a hillside raising a rifle, standing for his village.
abstract.cn: 想象山坡上的农夫举起一支步枪，为自己村子而战。

abstract.en: Imagine a courtroom where two sides sit with flags, each claiming the truth.
abstract.cn: 想象法庭里两边各坐一队人马，各自举着旗子说自己才是公理。

abstract.en: Think of a dividing hand splitting a chart in two colours.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把图表劈成两种颜色。

examples.en: Partisan fighting continued in the mountains for months.
examples.cn: 山区的游击战持续了数月。

examples.en: The charity tries to stay non-partisan in elections.
examples.cn: 这家慈善机构在选举中努力保持无党派立场。

examples.en: Readers should check whether a source is openly partisan.
examples.cn: 读者应核对消息来源是否公开带有党派立场。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「趴踢站」——党派聚会上谁都不肯趴下，非要站着选边 → 党派支持者、偏袒的

root: 拉丁语 pars「部分、一方」→ 意大利语 partigiano（派系成员）与法语 partisan（派系追随者）→ 英语 partisan。核心义「站定整体的某一部分」；近代「游击队员」义一般认为经由二战时期欧洲对 partigiano 的广泛使用稳定下来，确切最早用例的传播路径仍有争议。

sensesIntro.en: Partisan grows from a part to a side: first a fighter for the local side, then a party loyalist, then the one-sided attitude and method that loyalty produces.
sensesIntro.cn: partisan 从「部分」长成「一方」：先是为本地一方而战的人，再是忠于党派的拥护者，最后是这种忠诚带来的偏袒态度与作战方式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a village man with a rifle who stands on his own side of the hill.
core.cn: 核心意象：举枪站到山坡这边的人，只为自家一方而战。

branches.en: THE HILL: a local fighter and the harassing method he uses are the armed end of taking sides.
branches.cn: 山地线：地方战士与他的袭扰战法，是「站队」最武装的一端。

branches.en: THE PARTY: a party loyalist and a fan of a cause both side with their own part.
branches.cn: 党派线：党派拥护者与理念支持者，都是站在自己那一部分。

branches.en: THE VIEW: unfair judgement, party-line decisions and slanted writing all show the one-sided view in action.
branches.cn: 立场线：偏袒判断、党派划线、带立场的书写，都是这种单边视角的具体表现。

branches.en: THE CORE: literally anyone who holds firmly to one part is the root sense the whole word family circles back to.
branches.cn: 核心线：只要牢牢守住某一部分，就回到了整组词根都绕回来的本义。

branches.en: THE SPREAD: the same side-taking word names a person, an army member and an attitude.
branches.cn: 扩散线：同一个表示「站队」的词，分别指人、指军人和指态度。

intro.en: Partisan keeps the Latin part root pars and adds the Italian and French suffixes that turned it into a person word.
intro.cn: partisan 保留拉丁表示「部分」的词根 pars，并加上把它变成「人」的意大利语与法语后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin pars, partis and partire record the part root; partigiano and partisan are Romance forms built on it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pars、partis 与 partire 记录了这一「部分」词根；partigiano 与 partisan 都是在其上构成的后世语言形式。

items.example: Pars is the root of partisan.
items.exampleCN: pars 是 partisan 的词根。

items.meaning: belonging to, of the kind of
items.example: The Latin suffix -anus forms partisanus in later Latin.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语后缀 -anus 在后世拉丁语中构成 partisanus。

items.example: Partigiano carries the faction sense.
items.exampleCN: partigiano 承载了「派系」的含义。

items.example: French partisan gives English the noun.
items.exampleCN: 法语 partisan 提供了英语的名词。

items.example: The suffix -ship forms partisanship.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ship 构成 partisanship。

items.example: The suffix -ry forms partisanry.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ry 构成 partisanry。

items.example: The prefix non- forms non-partisan.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 non- 构成 non-partisan。

items.example: Party keeps the part root as a group noun.
items.exampleCN: party 以群体名词形式保留了「部分」词根。

items.example: Partition shows the dividing verb sense.
items.exampleCN: partition 体现了「分开」的动词义。

items.example: Partial carries the same one-sided meaning.
items.exampleCN: partial 承载了同样的「偏向一方」含义。

definition_zh: 充满热情的；热爱的；激情的；（爱与欲望）强烈的
definition_en: having or showing very strong feelings, especially enthusiasm for something or love for someone
core_image: 胸口像有一团火在烧，说话时声音发烫，眼睛发亮
scene: 深夜的排练室里，乐手一遍遍重来同一段乐句，直到手臂发酸也不肯停下。She is passionate about music and practices with the band almost every night.
sceneCN: 这里 passionate 是「对某事充满热情的」（第 1 个义项：对某项活动或事业抱有强烈而持久的热爱）；句意是她热爱音乐，几乎每天晚上都和乐队一起排练。画面里可辨识的物件：深夜的排练室、发酸的双手与反复演奏的乐句。

pos.zh: 充满热情的；热爱的；激情强烈的

derivatives.zh: 本词的词根名词，来自拉丁语 passio「受难、强烈情感」，义为「热情；激情；酷爱」
由本词加后缀 -ly 构成，义为「热烈地；强烈地」
由本词加后缀 -ness 构成，义为「热情强烈、充满激情」
由前缀 im-（使）+ passion 加 -ed 构成，义为「激昂的；充满感情的」，与本词义近但有区别

senses.title: Deep enthusiasm for an activity
senses.definition: having or showing very strong enthusiasm for a person, activity or cause
senses.definitionCN: 对某人、某项活动或某个事业抱有或表现出极强烈的热情
senses.example: He is passionate about marine biology.
senses.exampleCN: 他对海洋生物学充满热情。
senses.why: The noun passion came through Latin passio from a verb meaning to suffer, so the adjective describes a feeling strong enough to be endured rather than simply liked.
senses.whyCN: 名词 passion 经拉丁语 passio 来自一个意为「受苦」的动词，因此形容词描述的是一种强烈到需要承受的感情，而不只是「喜欢」；热情太满，会把人卷进去。

senses.title: Intense emotion in speech or manner
senses.definition: expressed or done with great emotion and energy
senses.definitionCN: 表达或进行时带有强烈情感与充足力量
senses.example: She gave a passionate defence of the small library.
senses.exampleCN: 她为那家小图书馆作了一场激昂的辩护。
senses.why: If the feeling is intense inside, it shows outside as heated words, raised voice and energy in the acting, which is what this derivative chiefly describes.
senses.whyCN: 内心的感受既然强烈，就会外化为发烫的言辞、抬高的声音和十足的气力；这条义项专指这种「外显的强烈」，是内心热情在言语与举止上的投影。

senses.title: Strong romantic love
senses.definition: having or showing strong romantic love or physical desire
senses.definitionCN: 带有或表现出强烈的浪漫爱情或身体上的欲望
senses.example: Their early letters were passionate and full of promises.
senses.exampleCN: 他们早年的来信热烈，满是诺言。
senses.why: Among the first uses of passion was the suffering of Christ, then violent feeling of any kind, so the loving sense keeps the same heat and intensity.
senses.whyCN: passion 最早可指基督受难，随后泛指一切剧烈的情感，于是「爱」这条义项保留了同样的热度与强度；火焰意象没变，燃烧的对象换成了恋人。

senses.title: Firm belief that drives action
senses.definition: strongly believing in something and acting on that belief
senses.definitionCN: 坚信某事并据此行动
senses.example: She became a passionate campaigner for clean water.
senses.exampleCN: 她成了为清洁水源奔走的热忱活动人士。
senses.why: Someone whose feeling is strong and enduring will work for the cause, so the word comes to describe commitment that shows in steady effort.
senses.whyCN: 感情强烈而持久的人总会为该事业出力，于是这个词也用来形容落在持续行动上的执着；从「心里烧着火」到「手上不停做事」，义项自然向前走了一步。

senses.title: Quick to feeling
senses.titleCN: 易动感情的；性情热烈的
senses.definition: having a personality that feels things strongly and shows feelings easily
senses.definitionCN: 性格上感受强烈，也容易把情绪表现出来
senses.example: My aunt is passionate and often moved to tears.
senses.exampleCN: 我姑妈性情热烈，常被感动得落泪。
senses.why: The word can describe not only a single feeling but a temperament that keeps producing intense feelings, which is the personality use.
senses.whyCN: 这个词不只能描述某一次强烈的感情，也能描述一个总在源源不断生出强烈感情的人；于是它从「这一阵燃烧」变成「常年烧着的性格」。

senses.title: An old image of a saint
senses.titleCN: 受难圣徒的画像（古旧用法）
senses.definition: in old usage, the picture or statue of a saint shown enduring suffering
senses.definitionCN: 在旧用法中，指描绘圣徒忍受苦难的画像或雕像
senses.example: A small passionate of Saint Sebastian hung above the door.
senses.exampleCN: 门上方挂着一幅圣塞巴斯蒂安受难的小画像。
senses.why: The Latin root passio literally means suffering, so the oldest noun use named an image of the Passion, which survives only in church usage.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语词根 passio 的字面义就是「受难」，所以最古老的名词用法指的是受难圣像；这条残留的义项证明了「热情」与「受苦」本来就是同一个词根的两个方向。

intro.en: Passionate is built on Latin passio, suffering, from pati, to suffer; the hot feeling sense entered through Old French.
intro.cn: passionate 建在拉丁语 passio（受难）之上，其动词 pati 意为「忍受」；炽热的情感义经古法语传入。

items.en: Pati means to suffer, endure or undergo something.
items.cn: 拉丁语 pati 意为受苦、忍受或经历某事。

items.en: Passio means suffering or strong emotion, and in Christian Latin the suffering of Christ.
items.cn: passio 意为受难或强烈情感，在基督教拉丁语中指基督受难。

items.en: Passion names strong emotion as well as suffering, and the adjective develops from it.
items.cn: 古法语 passion 兼指强烈情感与受难，形容词形式也由此发展出来。

items.en: Passionate appears in writing, first linked to suffering and then to intense feeling.
items.cn: passionate 进入书面英语，先与受难相连，后与强烈情感相连。

items.en: The modern sense of eager enthusiasm becomes common in ordinary prose.
items.cn: 表示热切热情的现代义在一般散文里逐渐通行。

items.en: Today the word is mainly positive and pairs naturally with about.
items.cn: 今天这个词多带褒义，常与 about 搭配使用。

note.en: Passionate belongs to the passion family built on the Latin suffering verb, while its near meanings range from keen enthusiasm to burning love.
note.cn: passionate 属于以拉丁语「受苦」动词为根的 passion 词族，近义一侧从热切到炽烈各有分工。

entries.definition: very strong feeling, or a deep enthusiasm
entries.definitionCN: 强烈的感情；酷爱；热情

entries.definition: in a very enthusiastic or emotional way
entries.definitionCN: 热烈地；强烈地

entries.definition: filled with strong emotion, used of speech and appeals
entries.definitionCN: 激昂的；充满感情的（多形容言辞与呼吁）

entries.definition: accepting what happens without acting or resisting
entries.definitionCN: 被动的；消极的（与目标词同源于 pati，但义为被动，与热情相对，只是拼写相近）

entries.definition: showing lively interest and eagerness
entries.definitionCN: 热情的；热心的

entries.definition: very enthusiastic and devoted
entries.definitionCN: 热切的；热诚的（较正式、偏书面）

entries.definition: giving all care and loyalty to someone or something
entries.definitionCN: 忠诚的；献身的

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin root and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁词根，以及这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Passion plus -ate: put passion into a person and you get passionate.
normal.cn: passion 加 -ate：把 passion 装进一个人，就成了 passionate。

normal.en: Passionate about is the usual pattern: passionate about music, about justice.
normal.cn: be passionate about 是常见句型：passionate about music，passionate about justice。

normal.en: The root pati means to suffer, so passion is a feeling you carry like a burden.
normal.cn: 词根 pati 意为「受苦」，所以 passion 是一种像担子一样背着走的情感。

normal.en: Compare passive: same root, opposite habit, one takes action and the other just waits.
normal.cn: 对比 passive：同根而习性相反，一个主动出击，一个只是等待。

normal.en: Passionately is the adverb, and impassioned fits speeches rather than people.
normal.cn: passionately 是副词形式，impassioned 多形容演讲而不形容人。

abstract.en: Picture a small fire burning behind the ribs that warms every word.
abstract.cn: 想象肋骨后面燃着一小团火，每一句话都被它烤得发烫。

abstract.en: Imagine a speaker gripping the lectern, cheeks red, voice rising.
abstract.cn: 想象演讲者紧握讲台，脸颊涨红，声音越来越高。

abstract.en: Think of two letters whose handwriting turns heavy and fast.
abstract.cn: 想象情书的字迹越写越重、越写越快。

examples.en: She is passionate about protecting coastal wetlands.
examples.cn: 她热心保护沿海湿地。

examples.en: His passionate speech persuaded the whole council.
examples.cn: 他激昂的演说说服了整个议会。

examples.en: They shared a passionate love for the old city.
examples.cn: 他们共同深爱着这座古城。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕身热」——一说起热爱的事就浑身发热，还怕别人看不出 → 充满热情的

root: 拉丁语 pati（忍受、受苦）→ passio（受难；强烈情感）→ 古法语 passion → 英语 passion；passionate 由 passion 加形容词后缀 -ate 构成。核心义「强烈到近乎折磨的情感」，可见于原始拉丁语「受苦」义与现代「热情」义之间的轨迹。

sensesIntro.en: Passionate keeps one heated feeling and shows it in three settings: enthusiasm for work, intense expression, and burning love, before spreading to commitment and character.
sensesIntro.cn: passionate 守住同一种发烫的情感，把它显现在三种场合：对事的热情、外显的强烈表达、炽烈的爱；随后再扩展到行动与性格。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fire burning behind the ribs, heating every word.
core.cn: 核心意象：胸口燃着一团火，把每句话都烤热。

branches.en: THE WORK: enthusiasm for a subject and belief that drives action are the steady, outward form of the heat.
branches.cn: 做事线：对学科的热爱与驱动行动的信念，是这股热度稳定向外的形态。

branches.en: THE FIRE SHOWN: heated speech and burning love let others see the heat directly.
branches.cn: 显火线：激昂的言辞与炽烈的爱，让别人直接看见这股热度。

branches.en: THE CHARACTER: a temperament that keeps producing strong feeling is the heat turned into a lasting trait.
branches.cn: 性格线：总在生出强烈感情的性情，就是热度变成了持久特质。

branches.en: THE ROOT: the old saint image holds the original sense of suffering inside the same word.
branches.cn: 词根线：古老的圣像义把「受苦」的本义留在同一个词里。

branches.en: THE COMMON SPARK: enthusiasm, public speech and love all run on the same intense feeling.
branches.cn: 共同火花：热情、演讲与爱情都由同一种强烈情感驱动。

intro.en: Passionate is a Latin root plus a Latin adjective suffix, with a small English family of adverbs and nouns.
intro.cn: passionate 由拉丁词根加拉丁形容词后缀构成，英语又添了少量副词与名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin pati, passio and passivus all come from the same suffering verb, which is why passion and passive look alike.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pati、passio 与 passivus 都来自同一个「受苦」动词，这正是 passion 与 passive 形似的缘故。

items.example: Pati is the root verb of the family.
items.exampleCN: pati 是这一词族的根动词。

items.example: Passio gives English passion.
items.exampleCN: passio 派生出英语 passion。

items.meaning: forming an adjective from a noun
items.meaningCN: 把名词构成形容词的后缀
items.example: The suffix -ate turns passion into passionate.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ate 把 passion 变成 passionate。

items.example: Passion is the base noun.
items.exampleCN: passion 是基础名词。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms passionately.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 passionately。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms passionateness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 passionateness。

items.example: The prefix im- helps form impassioned.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 im- 参与构成 impassioned。

items.example: The suffix -ed completes impassioned.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ed 补足 impassioned。

items.example: The suffix -ive forms passive from the same root.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ive 由同一词根构成 passive。

items.meaning: able to wait calmly, one who suffers
items.meaningCN: 耐心的；病人（原义为受苦者）
items.example: Patient also comes from pati, the one who endures.
items.exampleCN: patient 同样来自 pati，本指「忍受的人」。

definition_zh: 被动；消极；消极状态；不抵抗的顺从
definition_en: the state or quality of being passive, accepting what happens without acting or resisting
core_image: 一个人双手垂在身侧站着，任周围的事情一件件发生，始终没有伸出手
scene: 教室里同学在争论选哪个场地办汇演，坐在后排的人一直没有开口。The teacher was worried by the passivity of the class.
sceneCN: 这里 passivity 是「消极、不主动参与」（第 1 个义项：不行动、不主动）；句意：老师为全班这种消极沉默的状态感到担心。

pos.zh: 被动；消极；消极状态；不抵抗的顺从；不可数

derivatives.zh: 由 passivity 去掉 -ity 得到形容词「被动的；消极的」
passive 加 -ly，义为「被动地；消极地」
否定前缀 im- 加 passive，义为「无表情的；不动声色的」
impassive 加 -ity，义为「冷漠；无表情」
passive 加 -ness，与 passivity 同义，较少用

senses.title: Failure to act or take part
senses.definition: the state or quality of not acting, not taking part and not taking the initiative
senses.definitionCN: 不行动、不参与、不主动的状态或性质
senses.example: The report blames public passivity for the low turnout.
senses.exampleCN: 报告把投票率低归咎于公众的消极态度。
senses.why: Passivity is the abstract noun of passive, built with -ity from Latin passivus, so it names the quality of receiving an action instead of starting one.
senses.whyCN: passivity 是 passive 的抽象名词，由拉丁 passivus 加 -ity 构成，所以它命名的是承受动作而非发起动作的性质。

senses.title: Giving in without resistance
senses.definition: acceptance of events or treatment by others without protest, opposition or resistance
senses.definitionCN: 对发生的事或别人的对待不加抗议、不反对、不抵抗地接受
senses.example: Critics attacked the passivity of the government in the face of the crisis.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者抨击政府在危机面前一味顺从。
senses.why: Latin pati, the verb behind passivus, means to undergo or to suffer, so the noun keeps the image of someone who undergoes rather than pushes back.
senses.whyCN: passivus 背后的拉丁动词 pati 意为「承受、忍受」，所以这个名词保留了「承受而不还手」的意象。

senses.title: Inactivity seen as sluggish and spiritless
senses.definition: a habit of inertia or idleness, often shown with disapproval as a lack of energy and curiosity
senses.definitionCN: 常常带贬义指一种惰性或懒散状态，表现为缺乏活力与好奇心
senses.example: His mental passivity in class worried his tutors.
senses.exampleCN: 他在课堂上的思想惰性让导师们担忧。
senses.why: When a person receives rather than acts for long enough, the quality turns from a neutral description into a criticism of dullness and inertia.
senses.whyCN: 一个人长期只承受、不行动，这种性质就会从中性的描述变成对迟钝与惰性的批评。

senses.title: Being acted upon rather than acting
senses.titleCN: 被动性（被作用而非作用）
senses.definition: a technical sense in grammar, philosophy or chemistry: receiving an action rather than performing it
senses.definitionCN: 语法、哲学或化学中的技术义：承受作用而不是施加作用
senses.example: The pair of electrical terminals shows passivity when they merely absorb the current.
senses.exampleCN: 这对电极端子只吸收电流，便表现出被动性。
senses.why: Grammar and the sciences borrowed passivus for whatever receives an action, so the noun is the technical opposite of activity.
senses.whyCN: 语法与科学借 passivus 指承受作用的任何事物，于是这个名词成了 activity 的反面技术用语。

senses.title: A state of inactive repose
senses.definition: a condition of stillness or of doing nothing at all, close to repose in older and literary use
senses.definitionCN: 静止或什么也不做的状态，在较早的用法和文学用法中近似「安歇」
senses.example: The moralists warned that a life of pure passivity is not repose but stagnation.
senses.exampleCN: 道德家们警告说，纯粹无所作为的生活不是安歇，而是停滞。
senses.why: The same noun slides from the restrained person to the resting one, because both simply let things be.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词从「按捺不动的人」滑向「安歇休息的人」，因为两者都是任事情自行发生。

intro.en: Passivity is the Latin-derived noun passivus plus the noun ending -ity, entering English as the noun of the adjective passive after the adjective itself came through Old French. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: passivity 是拉丁来源的 passivus 加名词词尾 -ity，在形容词 passive 经古法语进入英语之后，作为其名词形式出现。年代均为约数。

items.en: Pati meant to suffer, endure or undergo, and it also feeds passion, patience and compassion.
items.cn: pati 意为受苦、忍受、承受，也衍生出 passion、patience 与 compassion。

items.en: Passivus described what could receive an action rather than perform it, in grammar as well as in ordinary speech.
items.cn: passivus 描述能承受动作而不发出动作的东西，语法中与日常言语中都如此用。

items.en: Old French passif carried the adjective to England, keeping both the general and the grammatical sense.
items.cn: 古法语 passif 把形容词带到英格兰，同时保留一般义与语法义。

items.en: English formed passyf, later passive, and the abstract noun of the -ity type was available for the same idea.
items.cn: 英语先有 passyf、后作 passive，而 -ity 型抽象名词也早可用来表达同一概念。

items.en: Latin passivitas supplied the scholarly noun, which English speakers reshaped as passivity for the quality of being passive.
items.cn: 拉丁 passivitas 提供了学术用名词，英语使用者把它改造为 passivity，表示「被动」这一性质。

items.en: Modern usage gives passivity to psychology, politics and technology, and dictionary dates for its first English record vary, so the century noted above is approximate.
items.cn: 现代用法把 passivity 用于心理学、政治与技术；各家词典对它在英语中首次出现的年代记载不一，上文的世纪只是约指。

note.en: The first group gathers words built on the Latin root for suffering; the second names the habits and moods that sit close to passivity in meaning.
note.cn: 第一组收建立在拉丁语「受苦、承受」词根上的词；第二组是与 passivity 意义相近的习惯与心境。

entries.definition: The adjective from which passivity is formed; it accepts an action rather than starting one.
entries.definitionCN: passivity 所由构成的形容词，表示承受动作而非发起动作。

entries.definition: The adverb of the same family, describing how a passive person behaves.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词族的副词，描述被动者行事的方式。

entries.definition: Intense feeling; both words go back to Latin pati and the idea of what one undergoes.
entries.definitionCN: 强烈的情感；两词都上溯到拉丁 pati 及「所承受之物」的观念。

entries.definition: The ability to bear delay or trouble calmly; it shares the root of undergoing.
entries.definitionCN: 平静地忍受延误或困难的能力；与「承受」共享词根。

entries.definition: Showing no feeling; the prefix im- adds not to the same adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 不露情感的；前缀 im- 在同形形容词上加出否定。

entries.definition: To attach or secure something; this verb is merely spelled alike and has a different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 系住、固定某物；这个词只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A tendency to stay as one is, in physics or in habit; passivity is inertia seen as a state.
entries.definitionCN: 保持原状的倾向，物理学与习惯中都可用；passivity 是把惰性看作状态。

entries.definition: Lack of interest or concern, especially towards public life; it is the emotional cousin of passivity.
entries.definitionCN: 缺乏兴趣或关心，尤指对公共事务；是 passivity 在情绪上的近亲。

entries.definition: Quiet acceptance of something unwelcome; it shares the giving-in without protest.
entries.definitionCN: 对不如意之事的平静接受；与「不抗议地让步」同义。

entries.definition: Obedient agreement with a request or rule; passivity can look like compliance but the two are distinct.
entries.definitionCN: 顺从地遵命或守规；passivity 看起来像遵命，但两者不同。

entries.definition: The habit of not working or not doing anything; it covers only the lazy edge of the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 不工作、不干事的习惯；只覆盖这个名词中「懒」的那一面。

normalIntro.en: Passivity is the -ity noun of passive, and the whole family goes back to Latin pati, to suffer or undergo.
normalIntro.cn: passivity 是 passive 的 -ity 名词，整个词族上溯到拉丁 pati（受苦、承受）。

normal.en: passive + -ity: the -ity ending turns the adjective into a quality or state, so passivity is the state of being passive.
normal.cn: 说明：passive 加 -ity 构成名词，-ity 表示性质或状态，所以 passivity 是「被动」这一状态。

normal.en: The suffix -ity goes back to Latin -itas and also forms activity, sensitivity and creativity.
normal.cn: 说明：词尾 -ity 出自拉丁 -itas，同样构成 activity、sensitivity 与 creativity。

normal.en: The family runs pati, passion, patience, passive, passivity and impassive.
normal.cn: 说明：这一词族的链条是 pati、passion、patience、passive、passivity、impassive。

normal.en: Passivity is used as a mass noun, so it appears without an article or plural in most writing.
normal.cn: 说明：passivity 是不可数名词，多数行文中不接冠词、不用复数。

normal.en: In grammar passivity contrasts with activity: one side receives the action, the other performs it.
normal.cn: 说明：在语法讨论中，passivity 与 activity 相对：一方承受动作，另一方施加动作。

abstract.en: Picture a pair of hands hanging loose while everyone else reaches for the same door.
abstract.cn: 想象所有人都伸向同一扇门，只有一双手松松垂着。

abstract.en: Picture a boat left to drift on a still lake with nobody at the oars.
abstract.cn: 想象一条船停在静湖上，没人划桨。

abstract.en: Picture a television that keeps talking while the room stays completely silent.
abstract.cn: 想象电视自己说个不停，屋里却毫无声音。

examples.en: The teacher was worried by the passivity of the class.
examples.cn: 老师为全班这种消极沉默的状态感到担忧。

examples.en: A survey measured the passivity of voters in small towns.
examples.cn: 一项调查测量了小城镇居民投票的消极程度。

examples.en: Learning needs activity on the part of the student, not passivity.
examples.cn: 学习需要学生主动，而不是被动。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕死又唯心」——遇事怕死、只想观望，于是什么都不做，这便是消极被动；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁 pati（受苦、承受）→ passivus（能承受的）→ 古法语 passif → 英语 passive 加 -ity → passivity；词根义「承受而非施为」贯穿全部义项。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses run from the neutral meaning of not acting and not taking part, through the giving-in without resistance, to a censuring sense of dullness, a technical sense of receiving an action, and a literary sense of stillness.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项从「不行动、不参与」的中性义，经「不抵抗的顺从」，扩展到带贬义的「怠惰迟钝」，再到「承受作用」的技术义，最后是文学化的「静止安歇」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: hands hanging loose while the world acts around them.
core.cn: 核心意象：双手垂着，任周围的世界动作。

branches.en: NOT TAKING PART: the neutral state of not acting or joining in.
branches.cn: 不参与：不行动、不加入的中性状态。

branches.en: GIVING IN: acceptance without protest or resistance.
branches.cn: 顺从：不加抗议与抵抗地接受。

branches.en: DULLNESS: the same habit judged as lazy and spiritless.
branches.cn: 迟钝：同一习惯被判为懒散而无生气。

branches.en: STATES AND TRANSITIONS: the everyday state of not acting becomes the technical name for being acted upon.
branches.cn: 状态与转换：日常的「不行动」延伸为「承受作用」的技术名称。

branches.en: QUIET AND REST: giving in without resistance and resting in stillness share the same hush.
branches.cn: 静与歇：不抵抗的让步与静止的安歇共享同一份安静。

intro.en: Passivity is built from the Latin participle stem passiv- plus the noun ending -ity, and it sits at the head of a family of English passive words.
intro.cn: passivity 由拉丁分词词干 passiv- 加名词词尾 -ity 构成，居于一族英语 passive 派生词之首。

latinIntro.en: Latin pati, to suffer or undergo, also gives passion, patience and compassion, all shaped by the -ivus and -itas endings.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 pati（受苦、承受）还给出 passion、patience、compassion，它们都由 -ivus 与 -itas 词尾塑造。

items.example: The stem carries the sense of being on the receiving end.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干承载「处于承受一方」的意思。

items.example: The ending turns pati into passivus, able to be acted on.
items.exampleCN: 这个结尾把 pati 变成 passivus，即能被作用的。

items.example: Passive shoulders the action without beginning it.
items.exampleCN: passive 承受动作而不发起动作。

items.example: The ending makes a quality noun from an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个结尾把形容词变成表示性质的名词。

items.example: Passivity names what passive describes.
items.exampleCN: passivity 命名 passive 所描述的性质。

items.example: The adverb tells how someone receives events.
items.exampleCN: 这个副词说明人如何承受事情。

items.example: The native ending gives the twin noun passiveness.
items.exampleCN: 本族词尾构成同义名词 passiveness。

items.example: The prefix negates passive to make impassive, showing no feeling.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀对 passive 加否定，构成 impassive，即不露感情。

items.example: The old verb still echoes in patience and passion.
items.exampleCN: 这个古老动词仍在 patience 与 passion 中回响。

definition_zh: 消遣；娱乐；业余爱好
definition_en: something that people do for pleasure in their free time, especially because it passes the time pleasantly
core_image: 午后长椅上的老人，一边晒太阳一边把时间慢慢地打发过去
scene: 一个孩子放学后坐在桌前折纸船，一折就是两个小时。Collecting old coins is his favourite pastime.
sceneCN: 这里 pastime 是「消遣、业余爱好」（第 1 个义项：为消磨时间而与愉悦之事投入的活动）；句意：收集旧硬币是他最喜欢的消遣。

derivatives.zh: pastime 的复数形式，义为「消遣；娱乐活动」
英语使用者有时误加的拼写变体，词典通常未收，正确形式仍为 pastime
法语同源词，字面即 pass 加 time，义为「消遣；打发时间之物」

senses.title: An activity done for pleasure
senses.definition: something a person does for enjoyment in free time, often a small regular activity
senses.definitionCN: 人在空闲时间里为了愉悦而做的事情，常是经常性的小活动
senses.example: Reading detective novels was her only pastime.
senses.exampleCN: 读侦探小说是她唯一的消遣。
senses.why: The word fuses pass and time, so whatever fills an empty hour pleasantly is named as an activity that lets time go by.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把 pass（度过）和 time（时间）合成，所以凡是能愉快地填满空闲时段的活动，都按「让时间过去的活动」来命名。

senses.title: An established leisure interest you keep up
senses.titleCN: 业余爱好；长期的休闲兴趣
senses.definition: a hobby or interest that a person keeps up and practises fairly regularly
senses.definitionCN: 一个人长期坚持、较有规律地从事的爱好或兴趣
senses.example: Fishing is a popular pastime in the villages along the river.
senses.exampleCN: 钓鱼是沿河村庄里很受欢迎的一项业余爱好。
senses.why: Because the word already implies something done again and again, it settled into the role that hobby plays in later English.
senses.whyCN: 由于这个词本身含有「反复去做」的意味，它逐渐填补了后来 hobby 所承担的角色。

senses.title: A characteristic leisure pursuit of a group
senses.definition: an activity that a particular nation, region or group regularly treats as its own favourite leisure
senses.definitionCN: 某个国家、地区或群体常视为自家最爱的一类休闲活动
senses.example: Baseball is often called the national pastime.
senses.exampleCN: 棒球常被称为国民消遣。
senses.why: When one activity is repeated so widely that a whole community shares it, the word shifts from one person to the community as a whole.
senses.whyCN: 当一项活动被广泛重复到整个群体共享时，这个词就从个人转向整个群体。

senses.title: Something that merely fills time
senses.titleCN: 打发时间的事；无足轻重的消遣
senses.definition: an activity treated as a mere way of killing time, sometimes regarded as trivial or not serious
senses.definitionCN: 仅仅用来打发时间的活动，有时被视为琐碎、不重要
senses.example: Gossip is a pastime, not a profession.
senses.exampleCN: 闲话只是一种打发时间的事，不是职业。
senses.why: The literal idea of making time pass can be read as frittering it away, so the same word also carries a faint note of triviality.
senses.whyCN: 字面上的「让时间过去」也可读作把时间消磨掉，于是同一个词还带着一点微不足道的意味。

senses.title: Literary use for an innocent diverting occupation
senses.titleCN: 文学用法：无害的消遣；排遣
senses.definition: a pleasing occupation that diverts the mind from care, common in older literary prose
senses.definitionCN: 指使人从忧烦中分心的愉悦之事，常见于较早的文学散文
senses.example: The writer called prayer his best pastime in a long illness.
senses.exampleCN: 这位作家把祈祷称作自己久病中最好的消遣。
senses.why: Older writers used the word for whatever pleasantly carries the mind elsewhere, and passing time and passing a care are the same motion.
senses.whyCN: 旧时的作者用它指任何能愉快地把心思带到别处的事，而「让时间过去」与「让愁绪过去」本是同一种运动。

intro.en: Pastime is an English compound of pass and time, recorded in the late fifteenth century and probably shaped on the model of French passe-temps, which has the same structure. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: pastime 是英语本土合成词，由 pass 与 time 构成，十五世纪末已有记录，很可能比照结构相同的法语 passe-temps 而形成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Pass in Middle English meant to experience or go through, and passing time was already an everyday idea.
items.cn: 中古英语的 pass 意为经历、经过，「度过时间」那时已是日常说法。

items.en: Old French passer gave the verb and, in combination, the idea of letting time or an occupation gladden the hour.
items.cn: 古法语 passer 提供了这个动词，并在组合中带来「让时间或某事使时间愉快度过」的观念。

items.en: French passe-temps, the present form and the plural unaltered, had the same parts and served as a pattern.
items.cn: 法语 passe-temps 由同样两个成分组成，现在式与复数同形，为英语提供了仿照的样式。

items.en: The English compound pastime is recorded in the late fifteenth century, written as two words in its first appearances and spelling time as tyme.
items.cn: 英语合成词 pastime 见于十五世纪末，早期写成两个词，其中的 time 还写作 tyme。

items.en: Early uses describe games and sports offered as pastime, and the word grows into the general noun for leisure amusement.
items.cn: 早期的用法把游戏与运动说成 pastime，这个词逐渐成为表示空闲娱乐的通用名词。

items.en: Modern English keeps pastime mainly for activity that amuses while the clock runs, with hobby taking over the sense of a steady personal interest.
items.cn: 现代英语让 pastime 主要用于「在时钟走动时给人乐趣」的活动，而把稳定持久的个人兴趣交给 hobby。

note.en: The first group unpacks the two elements of the compound; the second sets pastime beside the leisure words it is most often confused with.
note.cn: 第一组拆解这个合成词的两个成分；第二组把 pastime 与它最常被混用的几个休闲词并列。

entries.definition: The verb inside the compound, meaning to go by or to spend time.
entries.definitionCN: 合成词中的动词，意为经过、度过时光。

entries.definition: The second element of the compound and the thing a pastime pleasantly spends.
entries.definitionCN: 合成词的第二个成分，也就是消遣所愉快花掉的东西。

entries.definition: The same first letters as the past tense marker; the spelling is alike but the sense is different.
entries.definitionCN: 与过去式标记开头字母相同；拼写相近，意义不同。

entries.definition: A common misspelling with doubled s; only pastime matches the printed dictionaries.
entries.definitionCN: 常见错误拼写，多写了一个 s；只有 pastime 与词典一致。

entries.definition: A baked food of flour and butter; this word is merely spelled alike and has a different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 面粉与黄油制成的烘焙食品；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A steady personal interest pursued regularly in spare time; the most direct modern rival.
entries.definitionCN: 在业余时间长期稳定从事的个人兴趣；现代最直接的对应词。

entries.definition: Enjoyment or an activity that entertains; it stresses the pleasure rather than the passing of time.
entries.definitionCN: 乐趣或带来娱乐的活动；强调愉快而非打发时间。

entries.definition: Enjoyable activity that refreshes a tired body or mind; it is the formal word for leisure.
entries.definitionCN: 使疲惫的身心恢复的愉快活动；是休闲的正式用语。

entries.definition: Something that turns the attention aside for amusement; also a detour.
entries.definitionCN: 把注意力引开以供消遣的事物；也可指绕行道。

entries.definition: Free time itself rather than an activity; a pastime is what fills that time.
entries.definitionCN: 指空闲时间本身而非具体活动；pastime 是填充这段时间的东西。

normalIntro.en: Pastime is a transparent compound: pass plus time, an activity that lets the hours pass pleasantly.
normalIntro.cn: pastime 是一个意思透明的合成词：pass 加 time，即让人愉快地度过时光的活动。

normal.en: pass plus time spells pastime, and the compound means an activity that passes the time agreeably.
normal.cn: 说明：pass 加 time 拼成 pastime，意思是让人愉快地度过时间的活动。

normal.en: French passe-temps has the same shape and the same plural-free ending, which is why pastime ends with a silent e.
normal.cn: 说明：法语 passe-temps 结构相同、复数也不变形，pastime 词尾的 e 正源于此。

normal.en: The regular plural is pastimes, and the word takes a before the singular: a pastime.
normal.cn: 说明：常规定复数形式是 pastimes；单数前用不定冠词 a，即 a pastime。

normal.en: National pastime and popular pastime show the word used for a habit shared by a whole community.
normal.cn: 说明：national pastime 与 popular pastime 都显示这个词可指整个群体共享的习惯。

normal.en: Hobby and pastime overlap, but hobby names a settled interest while pastime leans on time being filled.
normal.cn: 说明：hobby 与 pastime 有重叠，但 hobby 指稳定的兴趣，pastime 更侧重填满时间。

abstract.en: Picture a clock face with a small figure happily walking round its edge.
abstract.cn: 想象钟面上有个小人绕着边缘愉快地走。

abstract.en: Picture a long Sunday afternoon turned into folded paper cranes.
abstract.cn: 想象一个漫长的周日下午被折成一只只纸鹤。

abstract.en: Picture a spare hour handed over to a chessboard that nobody is forcing you to play.
abstract.cn: 想象把一段空闲时光交给棋盘，而没人逼你下棋。

examples.en: Collecting old coins is his favourite pastime.
examples.cn: 收集旧硬币是他最喜欢的消遣。

examples.en: In many countries football is the national pastime.
examples.cn: 在许多国家，足球是国民消遣。

examples.en: Model boats are the pastimes of a patient kind of person.
examples.cn: 制作模型船是很有耐心的一类人的消遣。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕死他嗯」——怕死的人躲在屋里研究邮票打发时间，于是有了消遣；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 英语 pass（度过、经过）+ time（时间）合成 pastime，仿照法语 passe-temps；词根义「让时间过去」由游戏消遣扩展到业余爱好与打发时间之事。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses move from a pleasant free-time activity, through a settled hobby and a community-wide favourite, to mere time-filling and finally older literary use for a soothing diversion.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项从「愉快的空闲活动」，经「稳定的业余爱好」与「群体共享的最爱」，转到「单纯打发时间」，最后是较早文学用法中的「排遣」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an empty afternoon that a small activity turns into pleasant time.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个空荡的下午，被一件小事变成愉快的时光。

branches.en: PLEASURE: an activity chosen for enjoyment in free time.
branches.cn: 愉悦：空闲时为乐趣而选的活动。

branches.en: HABIT: the same pleasure kept up regularly turns into a hobby.
branches.cn: 习惯：同一快乐被规律地坚持，就成了业余爱好。

branches.en: COMMUNITY: one activity shared by a whole people becomes a national pastime.
branches.cn: 群体：一项活动被全体共享，就成了国民消遣。

branches.en: BELLIES AND SERIOUSNESS: what fills time pleasantly can also be dismissed as empty time-filling.
branches.cn: 轻重之间：愉快地填满时间的事，也可以被贬为纯属消磨时间。

branches.en: COMFORT: the hobby that steadies a person and the older diversion that eases a care are both gentle consolations.
branches.cn: 慰藉：稳定的爱好与旧时排遣愁绪的消遣，都是温柔的安慰。

intro.en: Pastime is a native English compound rather than a prefixed Latin word, so it is read through its two parts, pass and time, plus its relation to French passe-temps.
intro.cn: pastime 是英语本族合成词而非拉丁前缀词，因此要从 pass 与 time 两个部分，以及它与法语 passe-temps 的关系来理解。

latinIntro.en: Neither part comes from Latin directly: pass goes back through Old French to Latin passus, a step, while time is native Germanic. Latin supplies no separate root for the whole word.
latinIntro.cn: 两个成分都不直接来自拉丁语：pass 经古法语上溯到拉丁 passus（一步），time 则是日耳曼语本族词。整体词并无拉丁词根可拆。

items.structure: English verb, from Old French passer, from Latin passus (step)
items.meaning: to go past; to spend time
items.example: The first part says that the hour goes by rather than that it is worked through.
items.exampleCN: 第一部分强调的是时间流逝，而不是把时间干活用掉。

items.structure: English noun, from Old English tima
items.example: The second part names the thing that goes by.
items.exampleCN: 第二部分命名流逝的那个东西。

items.meaning: an activity that passes time pleasantly
items.example: The compound names leisure by what it does to the clock.
items.exampleCN: 这个合成词用它对钟表所做的事来命名休闲。

items.example: Pastimes covers several such activities at once.
items.exampleCN: pastimes 一次指多类这样的活动。

items.meaning: a way to pass the time
items.example: The French twin keeps the same parts and the same unchanged plural.
items.exampleCN: 法语对应词保留同样成分，复数也不变形。

items.example: Pass on its own simply means to move past.
items.exampleCN: pass 单独使用时只表示从旁经过。

items.meaning: a road or channel that goes around
items.example: By-pass shares the going-past image with the first half of pastime.
items.exampleCN: bypass 与 pastime 前半部分共享「经过」的意象。

items.meaning: something done only to make time pass
items.example: Time-killer is the bare version of the fourth sense.
items.exampleCN: time-killer 是第四义项的直白版本。

items.example: The same French verb heads another compound meaning goes everywhere.
items.exampleCN: 同一个法语动词还领起另一个意为「处处通行」的合成词。

derivatives.zh: 消遣（复数）

definition_zh: 牧场；草地；牧草；放牧；吃草
definition_en: an area of land covered with grass where farm animals graze, the grass itself, or the act of putting animals out to graze
core_image: 一片围栏里的绿草坡，牛群低头啃草，草叶在脚下被一茬茬吃掉
scene: 清晨的农场上，木栅栏围出一块坡地，几头奶牛低头慢慢啃草。The farmer turned the cows out to pasture in April.
sceneCN: 这里 pasture 是「牧场、放牧的草地」（第 1 个义项：牲畜吃草的草地）；句意：农夫在四月把奶牛放到牧场上吃草。

pos.zh: 放牧；把（牲畜）放到牧场吃草

derivatives.zh: 由 pasture 的同一拉丁词干加 -al 构成，义为「牧人的；田园的；牧灵的」
pasture 加 -age，义为「放牧；草场；牧草」
pasture 与 land 复合，义为「牧场用地」
与 pasture 同源，由「喂养者」引申为「牧人；牧师」
由拉丁 re- 加 pascere 而来，义为「一餐」

senses.title: Grassland where animals graze
senses.definition: a field or area of grassland used for the grazing of cattle, sheep or other farm animals
senses.definitionCN: 用于牛、羊或其他家畜吃草的田地或草地
senses.example: The herd was moved to a fresh pasture.
senses.exampleCN: 畜群被赶到一片新的牧场上。
senses.why: Pasture comes from Latin pascere, to feed or graze, by way of a form meaning the act of grazing, so the place is named after the feeding that happens there.
senses.whyCN: pasture 出自拉丁 pascere（喂养、放牧），经由一个表示「放牧」动作的形式而来，所以这块地方是按发生在那里的「吃草」来命名的。

senses.title: The grass or fodder itself
senses.definition: the grass or other plants grown on such land and eaten by animals
senses.definitionCN: 在这样的土地上生长、供动物吃的草或其他植物
senses.example: The sheep had already eaten the spring pasture down to the roots.
senses.exampleCN: 羊群已经把春季牧草啃到了草根。
senses.why: If the feeding is what the word means, then the material being eaten inside that feeding can carry the same name.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个词的意思就是「吃草」，那么吃草时被吃掉的东西自然也可以沿用同一名称。

senses.title: To put animals out to graze
senses.titleCN: 放牧；把牲畜放到草地上吃草
senses.definition: to put cattle, sheep or other animals out on grassland to feed
senses.definitionCN: 把牛、羊等牲畜放到草地上吃草
senses.example: They pasture the goats on the hillside every summer.
senses.exampleCN: 他们每年夏天把山羊放到山坡上吃草。
senses.why: The land was so basic to farming that its name turned into the verb for using it, a common pattern in English.
senses.whyCN: 这块地对农业如此基本，以至它的名称直接变成了使用它的动词，这是英语里常见的模式。

senses.title: A rural place presented as pleasant
senses.definition: a rural scene or district regarded as green, open and pleasant, often in poetic or praiseful writing
senses.definitionCN: 被视为青绿开阔宜人的乡村景象或地区，常见于诗歌或赞美性的文字
senses.example: Tourists come north to see the green pastures of the lowlands.
senses.exampleCN: 游客北上来看低地的青绿牧场。
senses.why: Green grass is the picture people keep of the countryside, so the word for grazing land doubles as the word for a lovely rural view.
senses.whyCN: 绿草是人们对乡野的固定印象，于是表示放牧用地的词也兼指美丽的乡村景色。

senses.title: A field of work or opportunity
senses.definition: a figurative sense, now somewhat literary, for a field of opportunity or a new area to work in
senses.definitionCN: 较文雅、略带文学色彩的比喻义，指施展机会的领域或新的活动天地
senses.example: The young engineers found greener pastures in the car industry.
senses.exampleCN: 这些年轻工程师在汽车工业里找到了更好的发展天地。
senses.why: Sheep and their food stand for livelihood in old pastoral metaphor, so a new pasture became a new chance to earn.
senses.whyCN: 在古老的牧养比喻里，羊与草就代表生计，所以 new pastures 就成了新的谋生机会。

intro.en: Pasture goes back to Latin pastura, a grazing, itself from the verb pascere, to feed or pasture, and reached English through Old French. Its deeper origin is not firmly settled. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: pasture 上溯到拉丁 pastura（放牧），再上为动词 pascere（喂养、放牧），经古法语进入英语。它更深的来源没有定论。年代均为约数。

items.en: Pascere meant to feed or to put out to graze; its further origin is reconstructed, not certain.
items.cn: pascere 意为喂养、放出去吃草；它更远的来源属重构，尚无定论。

items.en: Pastura was the noun for grazing, used of both the activity and the ground involved.
items.cn: pastura 是表示放牧的名词，既指这一活动，也指相关的地方。

items.en: Old French pasture carried the word north with its grass and grazing meanings intact.
items.cn: 古法语 pasture 把这个词连同草场与放牧两层意思一起带到北方。

items.en: English pasture is recorded from the fourteenth century, first as the grassland and then as the verb for grazing.
items.cn: 英语 pasture 自十四世纪起有记录，先指草地，继而用作表示放牧的动词。

items.en: Rural writers begin to use pastures of any green countryside, and the metaphorical field of opportunity follows.
items.cn: 乡村写作者开始用 pastures 泛指任何青绿的乡野，比喻意义上的「可图之利」随之而来。

items.en: Modern English adds the idiom put out to pasture for a person made to retire, drawn from retiring a horse from work.
items.cn: 现代英语补充了 put out to pasture 这一习语，指让人退休，源自把干活的马放归草地。

note.en: The first group gathers words built on the Latin grazing verb; the second puts pasture beside the land words and the action words that share its ground.
note.cn: 第一组收建于拉丁「放牧」动词之上的词；第二组把 pasture 与其同类土地词、同类动作词并列。

entries.definition: Of shepherds or of country life, and also of church care; the adjective of the same grazing word.
entries.definitionCN: 有关牧人或乡野生活的，也指教会牧养；同一放牧词的形容词。

entries.definition: A minister, literally a feeder of the flock; the person noun of the family.
entries.definitionCN: 牧师，字面即喂养羊群者；这一词族中指人的名词。

entries.definition: The business of grazing, or the grass used for it.
entries.definitionCN: 放牧这件事，或供放牧的草。

entries.definition: An activity that passes the time; this word is only spelled alike and comes from pass plus time.
entries.definitionCN: 打发时间的活动；只是拼写相近，来自 pass 加 time。

entries.definition: Baked goods made with flour; it shares the opening letters but has a different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 面粉制成的烘焙食品；只共享开头的字母，词源不同。

entries.definition: Grassland that is mown for hay rather than grazed; pasture is eaten where it grows.
entries.definitionCN: 割来晒草的草地；而 pasture 是就地被吃掉的草。

entries.definition: Any wide area of grass; pasture is the part of that land kept for animals to graze.
entries.definitionCN: 任何广阔的草地；pasture 是其中留给牲畜吃草的那部分。

entries.definition: The vast treeless grassland of central North America; pasture is usually fenced and farmed.
entries.definitionCN: 北美中部无边无树的草原；pasture 通常是有围栏、有人经营的。

entries.definition: A large farm of cattle or sheep including its land; pasture is one piece of ground inside such a place.
entries.definitionCN: 包含土地的大牧场；pasture 是这类地方内的一块地。

entries.definition: To search for and eat grass and plants; pasture names the ground, forage the searching.
entries.definitionCN: 寻找并吃草；pasture 指地方，forage 指寻找。

normalIntro.en: Pasture descends from the Latin feeding verb pascere, and the grazing family it leads includes pastor, pastoral and pasturage.
normalIntro.cn: pasture 出自拉丁「喂养」动词 pascere，它引出的放牧词族包括 pastor、pastoral 与 pasturage。

normal.en: pascere to graze gave pastura, the grazing, and English pasture kept the place-and-activity pair.
normal.cn: 说明：pascere（放牧）给出 pastura（放牧），英语 pasture 同时保留了「地方」与「动作」两面。

normal.en: The grazing family runs pascere, pastor, pastoral, pasturage and pasture.
normal.cn: 说明：放牧词族是 pascere、pastor、pastoral、pasturage、pasture。

normal.en: The word is both noun and verb, so the regular forms are pastures, pastured and pasturing.
normal.cn: 说明：这个词兼名词与动词，规则变化形式是 pastures、pastured、pasturing。

normal.en: The idiom put out to pasture sends a tired worker to rest, as a horse is sent to grass.
normal.cn: 说明：习语 put out to pasture 让疲倦的人歇手，正如把老马放到草地上。

normal.en: Pasture is usually fenced and managed, while the open wild grassland belongs to grassland and prairie.
normal.cn: 说明：pasture 通常有围栏、有人经营，而开阔的野草地属于 grassland 与 prairie。

abstract.en: Picture a fence that keeps the eaten grass from being eaten too fast.
abstract.cn: 想象一道围栏，让草不被啃得太快。

abstract.en: Picture a herd crossing a hill while the grass springs back behind it.
abstract.cn: 想象畜群翻过山坡，身后的草又长回来。

abstract.en: Picture an old horse at the edge of a field, no longer asked to work.
abstract.cn: 想象一匹老马立在田边，已不再被派活。

examples.en: The farmer turned the cows out to pasture in April.
examples.cn: 农夫在四月把奶牛放到牧场上吃草。

examples.en: After the drought the pastures were dry and bare.
examples.cn: 干旱过后，牧场又干又秃。

examples.en: The old manager was gently put out to pasture at sixty.
examples.cn: 那位老经理六十岁时被客气地请退了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕死丘」——草坡上一个土丘，牛群躲在后面吃草，不怕摔下去，这就是牧场；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁 pascere（喂养、放牧）→ pastura（放牧）→ 古法语 pasture → 英语 pasture；词根义「喂养」同时长出「吃草的草地」「牧草」与「放牧」三种用法。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses start from the grazing ground itself, pass to the grass on it and the act of grazing, then widen to any green countryside and finally to the figurative field of opportunity.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项从吃草的草地本身出发，转到草地上的牧草与放牧这个动作，再扩到任何青绿乡野，最后到比喻意义上的「施展天地」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fenced green slope where animals eat the grass down.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片围起来的绿坡，畜群把草啃低。

branches.en: THE GROUND: the fenced grassland kept for animals.
branches.cn: 地面：留给牲畜吃草的围栏草地。

branches.en: THE CROP: the grass itself, named after the feeding done on it.
branches.cn: 作物：草本身，因在其上的吃草而得名。

branches.en: THE WORK: the verb for turning animals out onto that ground.
branches.cn: 活计：把牲畜放上那块地的动词。

branches.en: GREEN VIEW: the working field becomes the pleasant rural scene in poetry and tourism.
branches.cn: 青绿景观：干活的田地变成诗歌与旅游中的宜人乡野。

branches.en: LIVELIHOOD: grazing animals and finding new grazing both stand for earning a living.
branches.cn: 生计：放牧牲畜与寻找新牧地都象征谋生。

intro.en: Pasture comes from the Latin feeding verb and noun, and it shares its stem with pastor, pastoral, pasturage and the less known repast.
intro.cn: pasture 出自拉丁「喂养」的动词与名词，与 pastor、pastoral、pasturage 以及较少见的 repast 共享词干。

latinIntro.en: Latin pascere belongs to a family that also gives pastor, the form pastus and pastio, all of which name feeding in some way.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 pascere 属于一个同时给出 pastor、pastus 形式与 pastio 的词族，它们都以某种方式表示喂养。

items.example: The stem supplies the feeding image behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干提供整个词族背后的「喂养」意象。

items.meaning: the act or place of grazing
items.example: The ending turns the feeding verb into the ground where it happens.
items.exampleCN: 这个结尾把「喂养」动词变成事情发生的地方。

items.example: Pasture names both the place and the act.
items.exampleCN: pasture 既指地方，也指动作。

items.meaning: an activity, a collective or a place
items.example: The ending gives pasturage, grazing as a practice.
items.exampleCN: 这个结尾给出 pasturage，即放牧这件事。

items.example: The ending makes pastoralis, of the shepherd.
items.exampleCN: 这个结尾构成 pastoralis，即牧人的。

items.example: The word moved from sheep to souls.
items.exampleCN: 这个词从羊群移到了灵魂。

items.example: The prefix returns again to feeding in repast.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀在 repast 中又回到「喂」的动作。

items.example: The compound keeps the ground sense clear.
items.exampleCN: 这个合成词使「地面」这一层意思保持清晰。

items.meaning: to retire a person or animal
items.example: The phrase keeps the old image of a horse sent to grass.
items.exampleCN: 这个说法保留把老马放到草地上的旧意象。

放牧；草场
牧场用地

definition_zh: 父亲身份；父权；亲子关系；父亲一方
definition_en: the state of being a father, especially the legal link between a child and the man who fathered it
core_image: 一根线从孩子的手上牵出来，连到一位男子的名下
scene: 律师站在办公桌旁，手里拿着一份基因检测报告，想把孩子的法律父亲确定下来。The lawyer held the genetic test report in her hand, ready to settle the question of paternity.
sceneCN: 这里 paternity 是「父亲身份」（第 1 个义项：作为一个孩子的父亲这一身份）；句意：律师手里拿着基因检测报告，准备把亲子关系（孩子的父亲身份）弄清楚。

pos.zh: 父权；父亲的地位（法律用语）

derivatives.zh: 由 pater 加形容词后缀 -al 构成，义为「父亲的；父系的」
由拉丁语 pater 与 familias 合成，义为「一家之主、家长」
与 pater 同源的希腊语词，义为「家长；族长」
由 pater（父）与 onyma（名字）合成，义为「父名、以父名著称的姓氏」
出自同源拉丁语 pater（父），原指像父亲一样保护他人的人，今指「赞助人」

senses.title: The state of being a father
senses.definition: the state or condition of being the father of a particular child
senses.definitionCN: 作为某个孩子的父亲的状态
senses.example: The court asked for proof of paternity.
senses.exampleCN: 法院要求提供父子关系的证明。
senses.why: The Latin noun paternitas means fatherly feeling, and later English uses it for the plain state of being a father.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 paternitas 本指「父亲般的情感」，英语后来用它直接指「身为父亲」这一状态。

senses.title: The legal bond between father and child
senses.definition: the legal relationship between a child and its father, often decided by a test or a court
senses.definitionCN: 孩子与其生父之间的法律关系，常由检测或法院裁定
senses.example: A DNA test confirmed his paternity of the twins.
senses.exampleCN: 一项基因检测确认了他是这对双胞胎的父亲。
senses.why: Once a father is named in law, responsibility and rights follow, so the family word turns into a legal term.
senses.whyCN: 一旦在法律上确认父亲身份，责任与权利就随之而来，于是这个亲属词变成了法律术语。

senses.title: Fatherhood as a social role
senses.definition: the role, duties, or identity of a father in a family
senses.definitionCN: 在家庭中作为父亲的职责与身份
senses.example: The study explores how paternity shapes men at work.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究探讨父亲身份如何影响工作中的男性。
senses.why: Modern use extends the word from a legal label to the social experience and duties of being a father.
senses.whyCN: 现代用法把这个词从法律标签扩展到做父亲的真实体验与责任。

senses.title: Derivation from a father
senses.definition: the fact of coming from or being created by a particular father
senses.definitionCN: 来自或由某位父亲创造这一事实
senses.example: The novel traces the paternity of an inherited name.
senses.exampleCN: 小说追溯了一个继承下来的姓氏究竟出自哪位父亲。
senses.why: The same idea of a line running from father to child explains metaphors of origin and source.
senses.whyCN: 从父亲到孩子的那条连线，也被借来比喻来源与出处。

senses.title: Authorship or origin in speech
senses.definition: the identity of the person who is considered the father or author of something
senses.definitionCN: 被认为是某事物之父或创作者的人的身份
senses.example: Nobody could confirm the paternity of that rumour.
senses.exampleCN: 没有人能确认那个传言的出处。
senses.why: If a father gives life to a child, an author gives life to an idea, so the word stretches to authors and sources.
senses.whyCN: 父亲给予孩子生命，作者给予想法生命，因此这个词也被拉向作者与来源。

intro.en: Paternity comes from Latin paternitas, which comes from pater, the Latin word for father.
intro.cn: paternity 来自拉丁语 paternitas，后者出自 pater（父亲）。

items.en: The reconstructed root pat- carries the basic idea of protector and feeder, often applied to a father.
items.cn: 一般认为，重构词根 pat- 带有「保护者、供养者」的基本含义，常用来指父亲。

items.en: Pater means father, and the abstract noun paternitas means fatherly affection or the status of a father.
items.cn: 拉丁语 pater 意为父亲，抽象名词 paternitas 意为「父爱」或「作为父亲的身份」。

items.en: Paternitas appears in Latin writings on family and faith, always about the father and his line.
items.cn: paternitas 出现在拉丁语关于家庭与信仰的著作中，始终围绕父亲及其血脉。

items.en: Middle French paternite or the Latin form enters English legal and religious writing, sometimes spelled with a final e.
items.cn: 中古法语 paternite 或拉丁语原形进入英语的法律与宗教文献，早期拼写有时以 e 结尾。

items.en: Early English uses paternity for the fatherhood of God and of earthly parents alike.
items.cn: 早期英语把 paternity 同时用于上帝作为父、以及人世父母中的父亲这一身份。

items.en: Today paternity names legal fatherhood, often joined with test, suit, and leave.
items.cn: 现代英语中 paternity 指法律上的父亲身份，常与 test、suit、leave 等词搭配。

note.en: Paternity belongs to the Latin father family pater, and sits next to words about proof of fatherhood.
note.cn: paternity 属于拉丁语「父亲」家族 pater，并与表示「确认父亲身份」的说法相邻。

normalIntro.en: Memory is built on the Latin father word pater and the matching pattern of maternity and paternity.
normalIntro.cn: 记忆线索来自拉丁语「父亲」pater，以及 maternity 与 paternity 这一对对称构词。

normal.en: Paternity and maternity form a natural pair, one for the father and one for the mother.
normal.cn: paternity 与 maternity 自然成对：一个是「父亲」，一个是「母亲」。

normal.en: The root pater means father, also seen in paternal and patriarch.
normal.cn: 词根 pater 意为父亲，在 paternal 与 patriarch 中也能看到。

normal.en: A paternity test answers one question: who is the father.
normal.cn: paternity test（亲子鉴定）只回答一个问题：父亲是谁。

normal.en: Paternity leave is time off given to a new father.
normal.cn: paternity leave 就是给新爸爸的陪产假。

normal.en: Compare paternal: the adjective describes a father, while paternity names the status itself.
normal.cn: 对比 paternal：形容词描述「父亲的」，而 paternity 指「父亲身份」本身。

abstract.en: Imagine a line drawn from a child hand up to one man name.
abstract.cn: 想象一根线从孩子的手画到一个男人的名下。

abstract.en: Picture a courtroom where a single paper changes who is a father.
abstract.cn: 想象法庭里，一张纸改变了谁是父亲。

abstract.en: Think of a man carrying a hospital bag, ready to be called a father at work.
abstract.cn: 想象一个男人拎着医院包，准备在工作中被称作父亲。

examples.en: He was granted paternity leave for three months.
examples.cn: 他获准休三个月的陪产假。

examples.en: The evidence was used to establish his paternity.
examples.cn: 这些证据被用来确认他的父子关系。

examples.en: Questions of maternity often attract more public attention than questions of paternity.
examples.cn: 关于母亲身份的问题往往比父亲身份的问题更受公众关注。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕疼你」——孩子出生时，父亲在产房外「怕疼你」；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 pater（父亲）→ 派生名词 paternitas（父爱；父亲身份）→ 中古法语 paternite → 英语 paternity，核心义「父亲这层身份」。

sensesIntro.en: Paternity starts from the plain state of being a father, widens into the legal bond, then reaches the social role, the sense of origin, and finally authorship.
sensesIntro.cn: paternity 从「身为父亲」这一基本状态出发，扩展为法律上的亲子关系，再延伸到父职角色、来源之义，最后落到「说法或作品的父亲」即作者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line drawn from a child up to one man.
core.cn: 核心意象：从孩子身上画出、连到某位男子的一条线。

branches.en: The plain state of fatherhood is the first sense.
branches.cn: 「父亲身份」是最基本的义项。

branches.en: The legal bond is the courtroom sense of the word.
branches.cn: 「法律上的亲子关系」是法庭语境下的义项。

branches.en: Fatherhood as a role and duty is the social sense.
branches.cn: 作为角色与责任的父职是社会层面的义项。

branches.en: A father is first named, then legally confirmed.
branches.cn: 先有父亲之名，再由法律确认父子关系。

branches.en: A line of descent easily becomes a metaphor for origin and authorship.
branches.cn: 从父到子的血脉线条，很容易引申为来源与作者。

definition_zh: 病理学家；病理医生
definition_en: a doctor or scientist who studies disease and its effects by examining tissue, cells, and body fluids
core_image: 白大褂的人俯身看显微镜，镜下是一块被染色的组织
scene: 手术结束后，医生在实验室里持续观察那枚切下来的肿块切片，准备给出诊断。After the operation, a pathologist studied the stained slide of the removed lump before the diagnosis was announced.
sceneCN: 这里 pathologist 是「病理医生」（第 1 个义项：通过检验组织与细胞研究疾病的医生）；句意：手术结束后，病理医生在宣布诊断前仔细观察了切下来的肿块染色切片。

collocations.zh: 顾问病理学家；主任病理医师

derivatives.zh: 由 -ist 换为 -y 的名词，义为「病理学；病变」
加形容词后缀 -ical 构成，义为「病理的；病态的」
再加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「病理上；病态地」
加前缀 psycho- 构成，义为「精神病理学家」
与 patho- 同根，义为「病原体、致病菌」

senses.title: A doctor who studies disease in the lab
senses.definition: a medical doctor who diagnoses disease by examining tissues, cells, and laboratory samples
senses.definitionCN: 通过检验组织、细胞与实验室样本进行诊断的医生
senses.example: The pathologist found cancer cells in the sample.
senses.exampleCN: 病理医生在样本中发现了癌细胞。
senses.why: Greek pathos means suffering, and the -logist part means one who studies, so a pathologist is a student of what suffering does to the body.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 pathos 意为「疾病带来的痛苦」，-logist 意为「研究的人」，所以 pathologist 就是研究疾病在身体里如何表现的人。

senses.title: A research scientist of disease
senses.definition: a scientist who studies the nature, causes, and progress of disease, often without patient care
senses.definitionCN: 研究疾病本质、成因与进展、通常不直接诊治病人的科学家
senses.example: The pathologist raised rats in a clean laboratory.
senses.exampleCN: 那位病理学家在无菌实验室里饲养大鼠。
senses.why: The word covers anyone who follows disease through -logy as a field of study, not only hospital staff.
senses.whyCN: 凡以 -logy 所指的学科来追踪疾病的人，都属于「病理学家」，不限于医院里的医生。

senses.title: Usually followed by of, as in pathologist of plants
senses.titleCN: （常用于 of 前）某类病理学家
senses.definition: a specialist in the diseases of a particular group, such as plants or animals
senses.definitionCN: 某一类对象（如植物或动物）疾病的专长者
senses.example: She trained as a plant pathologist in the tropics.
senses.exampleCN: 她在热带地区接受植物病理学训练。
senses.why: Compounds such as plant pathologist show the -ist naming a person who works on pathology of a chosen group.
senses.whyCN: plant pathologist 这类复合词说明：-ist 指专门研究某类对象病理的人。

senses.title: A figurative expert who names a social ill
senses.definition: a person who analyses serious problems in society as if they were diseases
senses.definitionCN: 把社会严重问题当作疾病来分析的人
senses.example: The essay calls him the pathologist of modern cities.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章称他为现代城市的「病理医生」。
senses.why: Because pathology studies what is wrong with a body, writers borrow the word for people who diagnose what is wrong with society.
senses.whyCN: 病理学研究身体的毛病，于是写作者借这个词指「诊断社会毛病」的人。

intro.en: Pathologist joins Greek pathos, suffering, with logos, word or study, and the English agent suffix -ist.
intro.cn: pathologist 由希腊语 pathos（痛苦）与 logos（言说、学问）组成，再加表示「人」的英语后缀 -ist。

items.en: Pathos means what a person suffers, from paschein, to suffer; logos means word, account, or study.
items.cn: pathos 意为「人所遭受的痛苦」，出自 paschein（受苦）；logos 意为言说、记述、学问。

items.en: Writers such as Galen use the idea of the study of disease and the word pathe, diseases, in medical Greek.
items.cn: 一般认为，盖伦等作者在医学希腊语中使用「研究疾病」的观念及词形 pathe（疾病）。

items.en: The compound pathologia appears in Renaissance Latin for the study of diseases.
items.cn: 文艺复兴时期的新拉丁语中出现复合词 pathologia，意为「疾病之学」。

items.en: Around 1750 French medical writing puts the term pathologie into wide use.
items.cn: 一般认为，十八世纪中叶法语医学写作使 pathologie 一词广泛流行。

items.en: English takes pathology, and pathologist is formed from it with the agent suffix -ist.
items.cn: 英语借入 pathology，再由它加表示「人」的后缀 -ist 构成 pathologist。

items.en: In the twentieth century the hospital pathologist becomes a central figure in cancer diagnosis.
items.cn: 二十世纪，医院里的病理医生成为肿瘤诊断中的核心角色。

note.en: Pathologist sits inside the pathos word family, and is often confused with specialists in other fields.
note.cn: pathologist 属于 pathos 词族，日常常与其他科室的专家混淆。

normalIntro.en: Pathologist is read from three parts: the disease root patho-, the study sign -log-, and the person sign -ist.
normalIntro.cn: pathologist 可以拆成三段读：表示疾病的 patho-、表示学问的 -log-、表示人的 -ist。

normal.en: Patho- means disease, as in pathogen, pathology, and pathetic, all from Greek pathos.
normal.cn: patho- 表示疾病，在 pathogen、pathology、pathetic 中都能看到，都出自希腊语 pathos。

normal.en: The -log- part means study, the same part as in biologist and geologist.
normal.cn: -log- 表示学问，与 biologist、geologist 中的成分相同。

normal.en: The ending -ist marks the person: a pathologist is the one who studies disease.
normal.cn: 结尾 -ist 标记人：pathologist 就是研究疾病的人。

normal.en: A pathologist works mostly behind a microscope, so the result comes as a report.
normal.cn: 病理医生大部分时间在显微镜后工作，所以结论以报告形式出现。

normal.en: Compare pathology the field and pathologist the person, the same -y and -ist pattern as in biology and biologist.
normal.cn: 对比病理学 pathology 与人 pathologist，这与 biology 和 biologist 的 -y 与 -ist 模式相同。

abstract.en: Picture a white-coated figure leaning over a glowing screen.
abstract.cn: 想象一个穿白大褂的人俯身在发光的屏幕前。

abstract.en: Imagine a labelled jar holding a small piece of tissue, the key to one diagnosis.
abstract.cn: 想象一个贴好标签的标本罐，里面是决定诊断的一小片组织。

abstract.en: Think of the person who reads the body as a map of illness, saying nothing to the patient.
abstract.cn: 想象一个把身体当作疾病地图来阅读、却不与病人直接交谈的人。

examples.en: A forensic pathologist examined the body before the trial.
examples.cn: 一名法医病理学家在开庭前检验了尸体。

examples.en: The pathologist told the surgeon that the tissue was benign.
examples.cn: 病理医生告诉外科医生，那块组织是良性的。

examples.en: Several pathologists reviewed the same slides and reached the same conclusion.
examples.cn: 多位病理学家查看了同样的切片，得出了同样的结论。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕死啦」——病理医生最怕一句话是「太晚了」；也可记作「怕生病，就 log 下来研究」。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 pathos（痛苦、疾病）＋ -logia（学问）→ 新拉丁语 pathologia → 法语 pathologie → 英语 pathology ＋ -ist（人）→ pathologist，核心义「研究疾病的人」。

sensesIntro.en: Pathologist begins as a lab doctor, widens to any scientist of disease, narrows in compounds to the ills of plants, and is borrowed by analogy for social critics.
sensesIntro.cn: pathologist 先是实验室里的医生，再泛指任何研究疾病的科学家，在复合词中限定为植物等对象的疾病，最后被比喻借指社会批评者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white-coated figure reading a stained slide under a microscope.
core.cn: 核心意象：白大褂的人俯身看显微镜，镜下是一块被染色的组织。

branches.en: The hospital doctor is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 「病理医生」是日常最常用的义项。

branches.en: The research scientist is the broader professional sense.
branches.cn: 「病理学研究者」是更宽泛的专业义项。

branches.en: The compound sense names a specialist in one group.
branches.cn: 复合词用法指明研究某一类对象的专家。

branches.en: Both a clinical and a research pathologist follow disease through tests.
branches.cn: 临床病理医生与病理学研究者都通过检验追踪疾病。

branches.en: The figurative sense borrows the word for a critic of society.
branches.cn: 比喻义把该词借来指社会病症的批评者。

intro.en: Pathologist is built from the Greek combining form patho-, the combining form -log-, and the English agent suffix -ist.
intro.cn: pathologist 由希腊语组合成分 patho-、组合成分 -log- 与表示「人」的英语后缀 -ist 构成。

latinIntro.en: The parts come from Greek rather than Latin, but Greek and Latin formed it in Renaissance medical Latin as pathologia.
latinIntro.cn: 这些组成部分来自希腊语而非拉丁语，但文艺复兴时期的医学拉丁语把它们合成了 pathologia。

items.example: The form patho- opens many scientific terms.
items.exampleCN: 组合成分 patho- 出现在许多科学术语的开头。

items.example: The form -log- marks a branch of study.
items.exampleCN: 组合成分 -log- 标记一个学科分支。

items.example: The suffix -logy forms pathology and biology.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -logy 构成 pathology 与 biology。

items.meaning: a person who does or studies
items.example: The suffix -ist forms pathologist and biologist.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ist 构成 pathologist 与 biologist。

items.example: The suffix -ology joins patho- into pathology.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ology 与 patho- 合成 pathology。

items.example: Pathology is the field behind the person.
items.exampleCN: pathology 是该人物背后的学科。

items.example: The suffix -ical forms pathological.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ical 构成 pathological。

items.example: Pathogen shares the disease root patho-.
items.exampleCN: pathogen 共享表示疾病的词根 patho-。

items.example: A prefix such as neuro- can narrow the field.
items.exampleCN: neuro- 这类前缀可以缩小所指的领域。
